<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
a \times 3 - 8   &= -5 \\\\
3a - 8      &= -5 \\\\
3a          &= -5 + 8 \\\\
3a          &= 3 \\\\
a           &= \dfrac {3} {3} \\\\
a           &= \dfrac {\cancel {3}} {\cancel {3}} \\\\
a           &= 1
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$1$

</div>
</div>

**Question**

An approximate method of deciding how much  sleep a  young person   needs is to subtract their  age   from $33$ and divide   by $2$.   

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

How   much  sleep does  an eleven   year  old   need?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">How   much  sleep does  an eleven   year  old   need?
</code></pre>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Sleep} &= \dfrac{33 - 11}{2} \\\\
&= \dfrac{22}{2} \\\\
&= \dfrac{2 \times 11}{2} \\\\
&= \dfrac{\cancel{2} \times 11}{\cancel{2}} \\\\
&= 11 \ \text{hours}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$11 \ \text {hours}$

</div>
</div>

<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

a                             &= 23 \ \text {years}
\end{aligned}
$

**Question**

Does  it make  sense to use   the   formula  for   older people?  Give  a  reason   for   your  answer.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</code></pre>

<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

No, it does not make sense.

For people older than $33$, the result would be negative. For example, if the person is $35$ years old,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Sleep} &= \dfrac{33 - 35}{2} \\\\
&= \dfrac{-2}{2} \\\\
&= -1 \ \text{hour}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Nine  bus   stops are   equally  spaced   along a  bus   route.   The   distance from  the   first to the   third is $600 \ \text{metres}$.  How   far   is it from  the   first to the   last? 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Nine  bus   stops are   equally  spaced   along a  bus   route.   The   distance from  the   first to the   third is $600 \ \text{metres}$.  How   far   is it from  the   first to the   last? 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the space between bus stops $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
2a                                     &= 600 \\\\
a                                      &= \dfrac {600} {2} \\\\
a                                      &= \dfrac {300 \times 2} {2} \\\\
a                                      &= \dfrac {300 \times \cancel {2}} {\cancel {2}} \\\\
a                                      &= 300  \\\\
\text{Total distance} &= 8a \\\\
                                       &= 8 \times 300 \\\\
                                       &= 2400 \ \text{m}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$2400 \ \text {metres}$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

When  asked how   many  chickens and   cows  he had   on his   farm  Mr Brown refused  to answer   directly,   but   
he did   say   that  the   total number   of heads was $30$ and   the   total number   of legs  was $100$.  How   many  of each  was   there?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">When  asked how   many  chickens and   cows  he had   on his   farm  Mr Brown refused  to answer   directly,   but   
he did   say   that  the   total number   of heads was $30$ and   the   total number   of legs  was $100$.  How   many  of each  was   there?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number of chickens $= a$

Let the number of cows $= b$

As per the question, 

$ 
\begin{aligned}
a + b                                  &= 30 \\\\
2a + 4b                                &= 100
\end{aligned}
$

We have got $2$ variables and we have $2$ equations to solve them. Let's eliminate to reduce it to just one variable.

Multiply first equation by 2.

$
\begin{aligned}
2 \times a + 2 \times b    &= 2 \times 30 \\\\
2a + 2b                     &= 60
\end{aligned}
$

Subtract the new equation from the first to reduce it to one variable.

$
\begin{aligned}
2a + 4b - (2a + 2b)    &= 100 - 60 \\\\
4b - 2b                &= 40 \\\\
2b                     &= 40 \\\\
b                      &= \dfrac {40} {2} \\\\
b                      &= \dfrac {2 \times 20} {2} \\\\
b                      &= \dfrac {\cancel{2} \times 20} {\cancel{2}} \\\\
b                      &= 20
\end{aligned}
$

Let's substitute the value of $b$ in one of the equations.

$
\begin{aligned}
a + b               &= 30 \\\\
a + 20              &= 30 \\\\
a                   &= 30 - 20 \\\\
a                   &= 10
\end{aligned}
$

Number of chickens $= 10$

Number of cows $= 20$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$10 \ \text{chickens}$

</div>
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$20 \ \text{cows}$

</div>
</div>

**Question**

I think of a number, multiply it by $17$ and then subtract $19$. The result is $66$. What was the number I first thought of?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">I think of a number, multiply it by $17$ and then subtract $19$. The result is $66$. What was the number I first thought of?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
a \times 17 - 19        &= 66 \\\\
17a                     &= 66 + 19 \\\\
17a                     &= 85 \\\\
a                       &= \dfrac {85} {17} \\\\
a                       &= \dfrac {5 \times 17} {17} \\\\
a                       &= \dfrac {5 \times \cancel {17}} {\cancel {17}} \\\\
a                       &= 5
\end{aligned}
$

Number $= 5$
</div>

**Question**

What number must $k$ be to make this mathematical statement true?

$10 \times k + 23 = 4 \times k + 35$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">What number must $k$ be to make this mathematical statement true?
<emptyline>
$10 \times k + 23 = 4 \times k + 35$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
10 \times k + 23 &= 4 \times k + 35 \\\\
10k + 23    &= 4k + 35 \\\\
10k - 4k    &= 35 - 23 \\\\
6k          &= 12 \\\\
k           &= \dfrac {12} {6} \\\\
k           &= \dfrac {2 \times 6} {6} \\\\
k           &= \dfrac {2 \times \cancel {6}} {\cancel {6}} \\\\
k           &= 2
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$2$

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

I think of a number, divide it by $7$ and subtract $3$. The result is $6$. What was the number I first thought of?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">I think of a number, divide it by $7$ and subtract $3$. The result is $6$. What was the number I first thought of?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number $=a$ 

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {a} {7} - 3 &= 6 \\\\
\dfrac {a} {7}    &= 6 + 3 \\\\
\dfrac {a} {7}    &= 9 \\\\
a                 &= 9 \times 7 \\\\
a                 &= 63
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$63$

</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

There is a number, $x$. When I add $7$ to $x$ then multiply the answer by $8$, the overall result is the same as just multiplying $x$ by $22$. What is $x \text{?}$ 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">There is a number, $x$. When I add $7$ to $x$ then multiply the answer by $8$, the overall result is the same as just multiplying $x$ by $22$. What is $x \text{?}$ 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
(x + 7) \times 8    &= x \times 22 \\\\
8(x + 7)            &= 22x \\\\
8x + 56             &= 22x \\\\
22x - 8x            &= 56 \\\\
14x                 &= 56 \\\\
14x                 &= 56 \\\\
x                   &= \dfrac {56} {14} \\\\
x                   &= \dfrac {4 \times 14} {14} \\\\
x                   &= \dfrac {4 \times \cancel {14}} {\cancel {14}} \\\\
x                   &= 4
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$4$

</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

I think of a number, multiply it by $9$ and subtract $7$. The result is $101$. What was the number I first thought of? 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">I think of a number, multiply it by $9$ and subtract $7$. The result is $101$. What was the number I first thought of? 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number $= a$ 

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
9 \times a - 7    &= 101 \\\\
9a                &= 101 + 7 \\\\
9a                &= 108 \\\\
a                 &= \dfrac {108} {9} \\\\
a                 &= \dfrac {9 \times 12} {9} \\\\
a                 &= \dfrac {\cancel {9} \times 12} {\cancel {9}} \\\\
a                 &= 12
\end{aligned}
$

Number $= 12$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

As per the question,

\begin{aligned}
(x + 8) \times 6 &= 18 \times x \\\\
6(x + 8) &= 18x \\\\
6x + 48 &= 18x \\\\
18x - 6x    &= 48 \\\\
12x         &= 48 \\\\
x &= \dfrac {48} {12} \\\\
x &= \dfrac {12 \times 4} {12} \\\\
x &= \dfrac {\cancel{12} \times 4} {\cancel{12}} \\\\
x           &= 4
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

I think of a number, divide it by $7$ and add $9$. The result is $17$. What was the number I first thought of?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">I think of a number, divide it by $7$ and add $9$. The result is $17$. What was the number I first thought of?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {a} {7} + 9      &= 17 \\\\
\dfrac {a} {7}    &= 17 - 9 \\\\
\dfrac {a} {7}    &= 8 \\\\
a                 &= 8 \times 7 \\\\
a                 &= 56
\end{aligned}
$

Number $= 56$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$56$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

There is a number, $n$. When I add 3 to $n$ then multiply the answer by 4, the overall result is the same as just multiplying $n$ by 6. What is $n \text{?}$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">There is a number, $n$. When I add 3 to $n$ then multiply the answer by 4, the overall result is the same as just multiplying $n$ by 6. What is $n \text{?}$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
(n + 3) \times 4    &= n \times 6 \\\\
4n + 12             &= 6n \\\\
6n - 4n             &= 12 \\\\
2n                  &= 12 \\\\
n                   &= \dfrac {12} {2} \\\\
n                   &= \dfrac {2 \times 6} {2} \\\\
n                   &= \dfrac {\cancel {2} \times 6} {\cancel {2}} \\\\
n                   &= 6
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$6$  

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

$2$ packets of crisps and $2$ drinks cost $\pounds 1.50$. $2$ packets of crisps and $1$ drink costs $\pounds 1.10$. How much would $4$ packets of crisps and $3$ drinks cost? 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">$2$ packets of crisps and $2$ drinks cost $\pounds 1.50$. $2$ packets of crisps and $1$ drink costs $\pounds 1.10$. How much would $4$ packets of crisps and $3$ drinks cost? 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let cost of packets of crisps $= c$

Let cost of drink $= d$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
2c + 2d &= 1.50 \\\\
2c + d &= 1.10
\end{aligned}
$

Adding the two equations, we get

$
\begin{aligned}
(2c + 2d) + (2c + d)  &= 1.50 + 1.10 \\\\
4c + 3d           &= \pounds 2.60
\end{aligned}
$

Cost $= \pounds 2.60$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$\pounds 2.60$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

I think of a number, multiply it by $2$ and subtract $5$. The answer is $11$. What is my number? 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">I think of a number, multiply it by $2$ and subtract $5$. The answer is $11$. What is my number? 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number $=a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
2 \times a - 5    &= 11 \\\\
2a                &= 11 + 5 \\\\
2a                &= 16 \\\\
a                 &= \dfrac {16} {2} \\\\
a                 &= \dfrac {2 \times 8} {2} \\\\
a                 &= \dfrac {\cancel {2} \times 8} {\cancel {2}} \\\\
a                 &= 8
\end{aligned}
$

Number $= 8$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$8$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Sophie should have divided a number by $4$, but instead she subtracted $4$. She got the answer $88$. What should her answer have been?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Sophie should have divided a number by $4$, but instead she subtracted $4$. She got the answer $88$. What should her answer have been?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
a - 4 &= 88 \\\\
a     &= 88 + 4\\\\
a     &= 92 \\\\
\text{Correct answer} &= \dfrac {92} {4} \\\\
&= \dfrac {23 \times 4} {4} \\\\
&= \dfrac {23 \times \cancel{4}} {\cancel{4}} \\\\
&= 23
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$23$

</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

When two numbers are added together, the result is $32$. When the smaller number is subtracted from the larger one, the result is $6$. 
Find the numbers. 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">When two numbers are added together, the result is $32$. When the smaller number is subtracted from the larger one, the result is $6$. 
Find the numbers. 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the first number $= a$

Let the second number $= b$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned} 
a + b                    &= 32 \\\\
a - b                    &= 6
\end{aligned}
$

We have got $2$ variables and we have $2$ equations to solve them. Let's use elimination to reduce it to just one variable.

Add the first equation to the second to reduce it to one variable.

$
\begin{aligned}
(a + b) + (a - b)       &= 32 + 6 \\\\
2a                  &= 38 \\\\
a                   &= \dfrac {38} {2} \\\\
a                   &= \dfrac {19 \times 2} {2} \\\\
a                   &= \dfrac {19 \times \cancel {2}} {\cancel {2}} \\\\
a                   &= 19
\end{aligned}
$

Let's find the second number. Using equation $1$ we get,

$
\begin{aligned} 
a + b                    &= 32 \\\\
19 + b                   &= 32 \\\\
b                        &= 32 - 19 \\\\
b                        &= 13
\end{aligned}
$

First number $= 19$

Second number $= 13$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$13$

</div>
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$19$

</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Verity thinks of a number. She multiplies it by $7$ then adds $8$. If the resulting number is $71$ what number did she think of in the first place? 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Verity thinks of a number. She multiplies it by $7$ then adds $8$. If the resulting number is $71$ what number did she think of in the first place? 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>
</div>

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
7 \times a + 8  &= 71 \\\\
7a              &= 71 - 8 \\\\
a               &= \dfrac{63}{7} \\\\
a               &= \dfrac{7 \times 9}{7} \\\\
a               &= \dfrac{\cancel 7 \times 9}{\cancel 7} \\\\
a               &= 9
\end{aligned}
$

Number $= 9$
</div>
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$9$

**Question**

Write in the missing number to make this correct:

$0.627 = 0.6 + 0.02 + \ldots$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

a           &= 0.007
\end{aligned}
$

Missing number $= 0.007$
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Alysha and Julia have some biscuits. Altogether they have $14$ biscuits.  Alysha has $2$ more biscuits than Julia.  

How many biscuits do Alysha and Julia each have?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Alysha and Julia have some biscuits. Altogether they have $14$ biscuits.  Alysha has $2$ more biscuits than Julia.  
<emptyline>
How many biscuits do Alysha and Julia each have?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number of biscuits Julia has $= j$

Number of biscuits Alysha has $= j + 2$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
j + (j + 2)           &= 14 \\\\
2j + 2                &= 14 \\\\
2j                    &= 14 - 2 \\\\
2j                    &= 12 \\\\
j                     &= \dfrac{12}{2} \\\\
j                     &= \dfrac{6 \times 2}{2} \\\\
j                     &= \dfrac{6 \times \cancel{2}}{\cancel{2}} \\\\
j                     &= 6 \\\\
\text{Julia}          &= 6 \\\\
\text{Alysha}         &= j + 2 \\\\
                      &= 6 + 2 \\\\
                      &= 8
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

Julia $=$ $6$

</div>
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

Alysha $=$ $8$

</div>
</div>

What is Jemma's number?

</div>

<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Jemma thinks of a number. She says,

<emptyline>

</code></pre>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Sapna makes a fruit salad using bananas, oranges and apples.

For every one banana, she uses $2$ oranges and $3$ apples. 

Sapna uses $24$ fruits.

How many oranges does she use?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Sapna makes a fruit salad using bananas, oranges and apples.
<emptyline>
For every one banana, she uses $2$ oranges and $3$ apples. 
<emptyline>
Sapna uses $24$ fruits.
<emptyline>
How many oranges does she use?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number of bananas $= b$

Number of oranges $= 2b$

Number of apples $= 3b$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
b + 2b + 3b &= 24 \\\\
6b          &= 24 \\\\
b           &= \dfrac{24}{6} \\\\
b           &= \dfrac{6 \times 4}{6} \\\\
b           &= \dfrac{\cancel{6} \times 4}{\cancel{6}} \\\\
b           &= 4 \\\\
\text{Oranges} &= 2b \\\\
                         &= 2 \times 4 \\\\
                         &= 8
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$8$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

I am thinking of a number that when I multiply it by two and divide the result by four, then multiply the result of that by itself, gives me a number that when I subtract four and divide by ten, gives me six. What is the number that I originally thought of?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">I am thinking of a number that when I multiply it by two and divide the result by four, then multiply the result of that by itself, gives me a number that when I subtract four and divide by ten, gives me six. What is the number that I originally thought of?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {\left( \dfrac {2 a} {4} \right)^2 - 4} {10} &= 6 \\\\
\left( \dfrac {a} {2} \right)^2 - 4 &= 6 \times 10 \\\\
\dfrac {a^2} {4} - 4 &= 60 \\\\
\dfrac {a^2} {4} &= 60 + 4 \\\\
\dfrac {a^2} {4} &= 64 \\\\
a^2 &= 64 \times 4 \\\\
a^2 &= 256 \\\\
a &= \sqrt{256} \\\\
a &= 16
\end{aligned}
$

Number $= 16$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$16$

</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Three apples and a banana cost $32 \ \text{p}$. Six apples and a banana cost $53 \ \text{p}$. How much does one banana cost?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Three apples and a banana cost $32 \ \text{p}$. Six apples and a banana cost $53 \ \text{p}$. How much does one banana cost?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the cost of an apple $= a$

Let the cost of a banana $= b$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
3a + b &= 32 \\\\
6a + b &= 53
\end{aligned}
$

We have got $2$ variables and we have $2$ equations to solve them. Let's use elimination to reduce it to just one variable. 

Subtract the first equation from the second to reduce it to one variable.

$
\begin{aligned}
6a + b - (3a + b) &= 53 - 32 \\\\
6a - 3a + b - b &= 21 \\\\
3a &= 21 \\\\
a &= \dfrac{21}{3} \\\\
a &= \dfrac{7 \times 3}{3} \\\\
a &= \dfrac{7 \times \cancel{3}}{\cancel{3}} \\\\
a &= 7 \ \text{p}
\end{aligned}
$

Let's substitute the value of $a$ in the first equation to find the cost of a banana.

$
\begin{aligned}
3a + b &= 32 \\\\
3 \times 7 + b &= 32 \\\\
21 + b &= 32 \\\\
b &= 32 - 21 \\\\
b &= 11 \ \text{p}
\end{aligned}
$

Cost of one banana $= 11 \ \text{p}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$11 \ \text{p}$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

After a card game, four gamblers had $\pounds 234$ between them. Harry had $\pounds 20$ more than Dana, 
Charlotte had $\pounds 53$ more than Dana and Sid had $\pounds 71$ more than Dana.

How much did each of them have?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">After a card game, four gamblers had $\pounds 234$ between them. Harry had $\pounds 20$ more than Dana, 
Charlotte had $\pounds 53$ more than Dana and Sid had $\pounds 71$ more than Dana.
<emptyline>
How much did each of them have?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the money Dana has $= d$

Money Harry has $= d + 20$

Money Charlotte has $= d + 53$

Money Sid has $= d + 71$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
d + (d + 20) + (d + 53) + (d + 71) &= 234 \\\\
4d + 144 &= 234 \\\\
4d &= 234 - 144 \\\\
4d &= 90 \\\\
d &= \dfrac{90}{4} \\\\
d &= \dfrac{2 \times 45}{2 \times 2} \\\\
d &= \dfrac{\cancel{2} \times 45}{\cancel{2} \times 2} \\\\
d &= \pounds 22.50 \\\\
\text{Money Dana has} &= \pounds 22.50 \\\\
\text{Money Harry has} &= 22.50 + 20 \\\\
&= \pounds 42.50 \\\\
\text{Money Charlotte has} &= 22.50 + 53 \\\\
&= \pounds 75.50 \\\\
\text{Money Sid has} &= 22.50 + 71 \\\\
&= \pounds 93.50
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

Dana $=$ $\pounds 22.50$

</div>
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

Harry $=$ $\pounds 42.50$

</div>
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

Charlotte $=$ $\pounds 75.50$

</div>
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

Sid $=$ $\pounds 93.50$

</div>
</div>

</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

What does $\boxed{s} \ \boxed{a} \ \boxed{l} \ \boxed{t}$ add up to?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">What does $\boxed{s} \ \boxed{a} \ \boxed{l} \ \boxed{t}$ add up to?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">

</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the question,

$\begin{aligned}
s + a + t &= 8 && (1) \\\\
s + a + P &= 9 && (2) \\\\
l + a + P &= 11 && (3)
\end{aligned}$

Subtracting equation $2$ from $3$,

$\begin{aligned}
(l + a + P) - (s + a + P) &= 11 - 9 \\\\
l - s &= 2 \\\\
l - 1 &= 2 \\\\
l &= 3
\end{aligned}$

Use equation $1$ to find the sum:

$\begin{aligned}
s + a + l + t &= (s + a + t) + l \\\\
&= 8 + 3 \\\\
&= 11
\end{aligned}$
</div>
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

What does $\boxed{s} \ \boxed{P}  \ \boxed{l} \ \boxed{a} \ \boxed{t}$ add up to?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">What does $\boxed{s} \ \boxed{P}  \ \boxed{l} \ \boxed{a} \ \boxed{t}$ add up to?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

From the previous part, we know $s=1$ and $l=3$.

Using the given equations to find expressions for $P$ and $t$:

$\begin{aligned}
s + a + P &= 9 \\
1 + a + P &= 9 \\
a + P &= 8
\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}
s + a + t &= 8 \\
1 + a + t &= 8 \\
a + t &= 7
\end{aligned}$

Since the cards have distinct numbers from $1$ to $7$:
We must find an integer $a$ such that $P$ and $t$ are also distinct integers from $1$ to $7$, and none equal $1$ ($s$) or $3$ ($l$).

If $a=2$:
$\begin{aligned}
P &= 8 - 2 = 6 \\
t &= 7 - 2 = 5
\end{aligned}$
The set $\{1, 2, 3, 5, 6\}$ contains distinct values. This is a valid solution.

(Note: Other values for $a$ fail. For example, if $a=6$, then $t=1$, which duplicates $s$).

Now calculating the required sum:
$\begin{aligned}
&= s + P + l + a + t \\
&= 1 + 6 + 3 + 2 + 5 \\
&= 17
\end{aligned}$

Subtract equation $2$ from $1$

$
\begin{aligned}
s + a + p - (s + a + t)       &= 9 - 8 \\\\
p - t                         &= 1 \\\\
p - 1                         &= t \\\\
t                             &= p - 1 \\\\
l + a + p                     &= 11 \\\\
3 + a + p                     &= 11 \\\\
a + p                         &= 11 - 3 \\\\
a + p                         &= 8 \\\\
a                             &= 8 - p \\\\
\end{aligned}
$

Substitute $a$ and $p$ in equation $1$

$
\begin{aligned}
s + a + t                       &= 8 \\\\
1 + 8 - p + p - 1               &= 8 \\\\
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A shop sells apples and oranges.

Kate buys  $1$ apple and $2$ oranges. She paid $48 \ \text{p}$.

Jade buys  $1$ apple and $1$ orange. She paid $31 \ \text{p}$.

How much does $1$ orange cost?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A shop sells apples and oranges.
<emptyline>
Kate buys  $1$ apple and $2$ oranges. She paid $48 \ \text{p}$.
<emptyline>
Jade buys  $1$ apple and $1$ orange. She paid $31 \ \text{p}$.
<emptyline>
How much does $1$ orange cost?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the cost of an apple $= a$

Let the cost of an orange $= r$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
a + 2r &= 48 \\\\
a + r &= 31
\end{aligned}
$

Subtract the second equation from the first,

$
\begin{aligned}
(a + 2r) - (a + r) &= 48 - 31 \\\\
a + 2r - a - r &= 17 \\\\
r &= 17 \ \text{p}
\end{aligned}
$

Cost of $1$ orange $= 17 \ \text{p}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$17 \ \text{p}$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Alysha and Julia each have some money. 

Altogether they have $\pounds 3.20$. 

Alysha gives Julia $20 \ \text{p}$ so that they both have the same amount. 

How much money did each have at the start?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Alysha and Julia each have some money. 
<emptyline>
Altogether they have $\pounds 3.20$. 
<emptyline>
Alysha gives Julia $20 \ \text{p}$ so that they both have the same amount. 
<emptyline>
How much money did each have at the start?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR: It is really important to use the right units in calculations and convert where required.
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Total money $= \pounds 3.20 = 320 \ \text{p}$

Let the money they each have finally $= a$

Alysha's iniital amount $= a + 20$ (since she gave away $20$ p)

Julia's iniital amount $= a - 20$ (since she received $20$ p)

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
a + a                   &= 320 \\\\
2a                      &= 320 \\\\
a                       &= \dfrac{320}{2} \\\\
a                       &= \dfrac{160 \times 2}{2} \\\\
a                       &= \dfrac{160 \times \cancel{2}}{\cancel{2}} \\\\
a                       &= 160 \ \text{p} \\\\
\text{Julia had}        &= a - 20 \\\\
                        &= 160 - 20 \\\\
                        &= 140 \ \text{p} \\\\
\text{Alysha had}       &= a + 20 \\\\
                        &= 160 + 20 \\\\
                        &= 180 \ \text{p} \\\\
                        &= \pounds 1.80
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

Alysha had $=$ $\pounds 1.80$

</div>
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

Julia had $=$ $\pounds 1.40$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

If I treble a number and add $6$, I get the same answer as when I add $16$ to that number. What is my original number?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">If I treble a number and add $6$, I get the same answer as when I add $16$ to that number. What is my original number?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number$= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
3 \times a + 6      &= a + 16 \\\\
3a - a              &= 16 - 6 \\\\
2a                  &= 10 \\\\
a                   &= \dfrac {10} {2} \\\\
a                   &= \dfrac {2 \times 5} {2} \\\\
a                   &= \dfrac {\cancel {2} \times 5} {\cancel {2}} \\\\
a                   &= 5
\end{aligned}
$

Original number $= 5$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$5$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

My money box contains an equal number of $5 \ \text{p}, 10 \ \text{p}$ and $20 \ \text{p}$ coins and no other coins. 
How many coins are there altogether if there is $\pounds 4.90$ in the money box?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">My money box contains an equal number of $5 \ \text{p}, 10 \ \text{p}$ and $20 \ \text{p}$ coins and no other coins. 
How many coins are there altogether if there is $\pounds 4.90$ in the money box?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR: It is really important to use the right units in calculations and convert where required.
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the count of coins of each denomination $= c$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
5 \ \text{p} \times c + 10 \ \text{p} \times c + 20 \ \text{p} \times c &= \pounds 4.90 \\\\
5 \ \text{p} \times c + 10 \ \text{p} \times c + 20 \ \text{p} \times c &= 490 \ \text{p} \\\\
5c + 10c + 20c &= 490 \\\\
35c &= 490 \\\\
c &= \dfrac{490}{35} \\\\
c &= \dfrac{14 \times 7 \times 5}{7 \times 5} \\\\
c &= \dfrac{14 \times \cancel{7} \times \cancel{5}}{\cancel{7} \times \cancel{5}} \\\\
c &= 14 \\\\
\text{Total coins} &= 14 \times 3 \\\\
&= 42 \ \text{coins}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$42$

</div>
</div>

**Question**

Winston thinks of two different whole numbers that add together to make $20$ and multiply to give $84$. What are his two numbers?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Winston thinks of two different whole numbers that add together to make $20$ and multiply to give $84$. What are his two numbers?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the first number $= a$

Let the second number $= b$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
a + b &= 20 \\\\
ab &= 84
\end{aligned}
$

We can easily infer the values by using trial and error. Let's find out $2$ numbers which meets the following critiera based on the equations above.

- The sum of the $2$ numbers is $20$.
- The product of the $2$ numbers is $84$ 

Factor pairs of $84 = (1, 84), (2, 42), (3, 28), (4, 21), (6, 14), (7, 12)$

| Factor pair $(a, b)$ |  $a + b$ | $= 20$? |
|:--------------------:|:------------------:|:------------------:|
| $(1, 84)$            | $1 + 84 = 85$      | No                 |
| $(2, 42)$             | $2 + 42 = 44$      | No                 |
| $(3, 28)$             | $3 + 28 = 31$      | No                 |
| $(4, 21)$             | $4 + 21 = 25$      | No                 |
| $(6, 14)$             | $6 + 14 = 20$      | Yes                |
| $(7, 12)$             | $7 + 12 = 19$      | No                 |

A quick check shows $6$ and $14$ meets the criteria above.

Numbers $= 6$, $14$
</div>

**Question**

He then thinks of a new number, multiplies it by $9$ and subtracts $15$. The result is $66$. What was his original number?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">He then thinks of a new number, multiplies it by $9$ and subtracts $15$. The result is $66$. What was his original number?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
9 \times a - 15     &= 66 \\\\
9a          &= 66 + 15 \\\\
9a          &= 81 \\\\
a                   &= \dfrac {81} {9} \\\\
a                   &= \dfrac {9 \times 9} {9} \\\\
a                   &= \dfrac {\cancel{9} \times 9} {\cancel{9}} \\\\
a                   &= 9
\end{aligned}
$

New number $= 9$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$9$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question_envelope rag_not_found subquestion">
<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

How many moos are there in $3$ quacks and $1$ oink?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">How many moos are there in $3$ quacks and $1$ oink?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
&= 3 \ \text {quacks} + 1 \ \text {oink} \\\\
&= 3 \ \text {quacks} + 13 \ \text {quacks} \\\\
&= 16 \ \text {quacks} \\\\
&= 16 \times 3 \ \text {moos} \\\\
&= 48 \ \text {moos}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

**Question**

What fraction of an oink does $9$ moos represent?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">What fraction of an oink does $9$ moos represent?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
1 \ \text {oink}           &= 13 \ \text {quacks} \\\\
1 \ \text {quack}           &= 3 \ \text {moos} \\\\
1 \ \text {oink}            &= 13 \times (3 \ \text {moos}) \\\\
1 \ \text {oink}            &= 39 \ \text {moos} \\\\
1 \ \text {moo}             &= \dfrac {1} {39} \ \text {oink} \\\\
9 \ \text {moos}            &= 9 \times \dfrac {1} {39} \ \text {oink} \\\\
9 \ \text {moos}            &= \dfrac {9} {39} \ \text {oink} \\\\
                          &= \dfrac {3 \times 3} {3 \times 13} \\\\
                          &= \dfrac {3} {13} \ \text {oink}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</code></pre>

<div class="workings">

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{1 oink}             &= 39 \ \text{moos} \\\\
\text{1 pile (2 oinks)}   &= 2 \times 39 \\\\
                          &= 78 \ \text{moos} \\\\
\text{Number of piles}    &= \dfrac{\text{Total number of Moos}}{\text{Number of moos per pile}} \\\\
                          &= \dfrac{800}{78} \\\\
                          &= 10 \ \text{remainder} \ 20 \\\\
\text{Complete piles}     &= 10 \\\\
\text{Leftover}           &= 20 \ \text{moos} \\\\
                          &= \dfrac{20}{3} \ \text{quacks} \\\\
                          &= 6 \ \text{quacks} + 2 \ \text{moos}
\end{aligned}
$

piles $= 10$

quacks $= 6$

moos $= 2$

$10 \ \text{piles}$

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$6 \ \text{quacks}$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">What is the value of $b$ if $3 \ \spadesuit \ b = 15$
</code></pre>

<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
3 \ \spadesuit \  b  &= 15 \\\\
3 \times b + 3  &= 15 \\\\
3b              &= 15 - 3 \\\\
3b              &= 12 \\\\
b               &= \dfrac {12} {3} \\\\
b               &= \dfrac {3 \times 4} {3} \\\\
b               &= \dfrac {\cancel {3} \times 4} {\cancel {3}} \\\\
b               &= 4
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$4$

<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
a \ \spadesuit \  a                          &= 20 \\\\
a \times a + a                          &= 20 \\\\
a \times (a + 1)                        &= 20
\end{aligned}
$

We can easily infer the values by using trial and error. Let's find out $2$ numbers which meets the following critiera based on the equations above.

- The product of the $2$ numbers is $20$. 
- The difference between the $2$ numbers is $1$.

Factor pairs of $20 = (1, 20), (2, 10), (4, 5)$

Factor pairs of $20$ that have difference of $1 = (4,5)$

$a = 4$
</div>

<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$4$

**Question**

$(a \ \spadesuit \ b) \ \spadesuit \ c$ means work out $(a \ \spadesuit \ b)$ first and then work out "your answer" $\ \spadesuit \ c$.

For example: 

$(5 \ \spadesuit \ 2) \ \spadesuit \ 3$ means do $5 \ \spadesuit \ 2 = 5 \times 2 + 5 = 15$ first, then work out
$15 \ \spadesuit \ 3 = 15 \times 3 + 15 = 45 + 15 = 60 $

Work out $(2 \ \spadesuit \ 3) \ \spadesuit \ 4 =$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">$(a \ \spadesuit \ b) \ \spadesuit \ c$ means work out $(a \ \spadesuit \ b)$ first and then work out "your answer" $\ \spadesuit \ c$.
<emptyline>
For example: 
<emptyline>
$(5 \ \spadesuit \ 2) \ \spadesuit \ 3$ means do $5 \ \spadesuit \ 2 = 5 \times 2 + 5 = 15$ first, then work out
$15 \ \spadesuit \ 3 = 15 \times 3 + 15 = 45 + 15 = 60 $
<emptyline>
Work out $(2 \ \spadesuit \ 3) \ \spadesuit \ 4 =$
</code></pre>
</div>

</div>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
&= (2 \ \spadesuit \ 3) \ \spadesuit \ 4 \\\\
&= (2 \times 3 + 2) \ \spadesuit \  4 \\\\
&= (6 + 2) \ \spadesuit \  4 \\\\
&= 8 \ \spadesuit \  4 \\\\
&= 8 \times 4 + 8 \\\\
&= 32 + 8 \\\\
&= 40
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

I think of a number $n$. 

$5n$ is more than $60$, but $n + 5$ is less than $20$. What are the possible values of $n$?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">I think of a number $n$. 
<emptyline>
$5n$ is more than $60$, but $n + 5$ is less than $20$. What are the possible values of $n$?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
5n                                              &> 60 \\\\
\dfrac  {5n} {5}                                &> \dfrac {60} {5} \\\\
\dfrac {\cancel {5} \times n} {\cancel {5}}     &> \dfrac {5 \times 12} {5} \\\\
n                                               &> \dfrac {\cancel {5} \times 12} {\cancel {5}} \\\\
n                                               &> 12
\end{aligned}
$

Also,

$
\begin{aligned}
n + 5       &< 20 \\\\
n           &< 20 - 5 \\\\
n           &< 15
\end{aligned}
$

Combining the two inequalities:

$12 < n < 15$

Possible values of $n= 13$, $14$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$13$

</div>
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$14$

</div>
</div>

5n                                              &> 60 \\\\
\dfrac  {5n} {5}                                &> \dfrac {60} {5} \\\\
\dfrac {\cancel {5} \times n} {\cancel {5}}     &> \dfrac {5 \times 12} {5} \\\\
n                                               &> \dfrac {\cancel {5} \times 12} {\cancel {5}} \\\\
n                                               &> 12
\end{aligned}
$
<emptyline>
Also,
<emptyline>
$
\begin{aligned}
n + 5       &< 20 \\\\
n           &< 20 - 5 \\\\
n           &< 15
\end{aligned}
$
<emptyline>
Combining the two inequalities:
<emptyline>
$12 < n < 15$
<emptyline>
Possible values of $n= 13$, $14$
</code></pre>
</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A shop sells bananas and pears. 

Max buys $1$ banana and $2$ pears. He paid $94 \ \text{p}$. 

Emily buys $1$ banana and $1$ pear. She paid $62 \ \text{p}$. 

How much does $1$ banana cost?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A shop sells bananas and pears. 
<emptyline>
Max buys $1$ banana and $2$ pears. He paid $94 \ \text{p}$. 
<emptyline>
Emily buys $1$ banana and $1$ pear. She paid $62 \ \text{p}$. 
<emptyline>
How much does $1$ banana cost?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the cost of a banana $= b$

Let the cost of a pear $= p$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned} 
b + 2p &= 94 \\\\
b + p &= 62
\end{aligned}
$

We have got $2$ variables and we have $2$ equations to solve them. Let's use elimination to reduce it to just one variable. 

Subtract the second equation from the first to reduce it to one variable.

$
\begin{aligned} 
(b + 2p) - (b + p) &= 94 - 62 \\\\
b + 2p - b - p    &= 32 \\\\
p                 &= 32 \ \text{p}
\end{aligned}
$

Cost of a pear $= 32 \ \text{p}$

Let's substitute the value of $p$ in the second equation to find the cost of a banana.

$
\begin{aligned} 
b + p      &= 62 \\\\
b + 32     &= 62 \\\\
b          &= 62 - 32 \\\\
b          &= 30 \ \text{p}
\end{aligned}
$

Cost of a banana $= 30 \ \text{p}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$30 \ \text{p}$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

There are a number of coins on a table. One quarter of the coins show heads.

If I turn over two coins, then one third show heads. How many coins are there altogether?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">There are a number of coins on a table. One quarter of the coins show heads.
<emptyline>
If I turn over two coins, then one third show heads. How many coins are there altogether?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the total number of coins $= c$

As per the question, turning over two coins increases the number of heads by $2$.

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {c} {4} + 2                                                          &= \dfrac {c} {3} \\\\
\dfrac {c} {3} - \dfrac {c} {4}                                         &= 2 \\\\
\dfrac {c \times 4} {3 \times 4} - \dfrac {c \times 3} {4 \times 3}     &= 2 \\\\
\dfrac {4c} {12} - \dfrac {3c} {12}                                     &= 2 \\\\
\dfrac {4c - 3c} {12}                                                   &= 2 \\\\
\dfrac {c} {12}                                                         &= 2 \\\\
c                                                                       &= 2 \times 12 \\\\
c                                                                       &= 24
\end{aligned}
$

Number of coins $= 24$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$24$

</div>
</div>

</div>

$
<emptyline>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

There are twenty gifts stacked up into four piles. 

The first pile has $3$ less than the second pile. 

The second pile has two more than the third pile. 

The fourth pile has twice as many as the second pile. 

How many gifts are in each pile?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">There are twenty gifts stacked up into four piles. 
<emptyline>
The first pile has $3$ less than the second pile. 
<emptyline>
The second pile has two more than the third pile. 
<emptyline>
The fourth pile has twice as many as the second pile. 
<emptyline>
How many gifts are in each pile?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number of gifts in the second pile $= p$

Number of gifts in the first pile $= p - 3$

Number of gifts in the third pile $= p - 2$

Number of gifts in the fourth pile $= 2p$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
(p - 3) + p + (p - 2) + 2p &= 20 \\\\
p + p + p + 2p - 3 - 2     &= 20 \\\\
5p - 5                     &= 20 \\\\
5p                         &= 20 + 5 \\\\
5p                         &= 25 \\\\
p                          &= \dfrac{25}{5} \\\\
p                          &= \dfrac{5 \times 5}{5} \\\\
p                          &= \dfrac{\cancel{5} \times 5}{\cancel{5}} \\\\
p                          &= 5
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{First pile}  &= p - 3 \\\\
                  &= 5 - 3 \\\\
                   &= 2 \\\\
\text{Second pile} &= 5 \\\\
\text{Third pile}  &= p - 2 \\\\
                  &= 5 - 2 \\\\
                   &= 3 \\\\
\text{Fourth pile} &= 2p \\\\
                  &= 2 \times 5 \\\\
                   &= 10
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

**Answer**

**Answer**

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

*ABBR: TODO:: Find the right katex symbol.*


If the following statements are true, how many  $\sum \text{s}$ are there in a $\bigoplus \text{?}$

- $\sum + \sum = \Psi$
- $\Psi + \Psi + \sum = \ \spadesuit \ $
- $ \ \spadesuit \ + \Psi = \bigoplus$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">rtq_abbr_working_katex_show_correct_symbol
<emptyline>
If the following statements are true, how many  $\sum \text{s}$ are there in a $\bigoplus \text{?}$
<emptyline>
- $\sum + \sum = \Psi$
- $\Psi + \Psi + \sum = \ \spadesuit \ $
- $ \ \spadesuit \ + \Psi = \bigoplus$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\sum + \sum &= \Psi \\\\
2\sum       &= \Psi \\\\
\Psi        &= 2\sum \\\\
\end{aligned}
$

Substitute the value of $\Psi$ in equation $2$

$
\begin{aligned}
\Psi + \Psi + \sum               &= \spadesuit \\\\
2\sum + 2\sum + \sum             &= \spadesuit \\\\
5\sum                            &= \spadesuit \\\\
\spadesuit                       &= 5\sum \\\\
\end{aligned}
$

Substitute the value of $\spadesuit$ and $\Psi$ in equation $3$

$
\begin{aligned}
\spadesuit + \Psi                  &= \bigoplus \\\\
5\sum + 2\sum                      &= \bigoplus \\\\
7\sum                              &= \bigoplus \\\\
\bigoplus                          &= 7\sum \\\\
\end{aligned}
$

Number of $\sum$ in $\bigoplus$ $= 7$
</div>
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

If $p  \ \Phi \ p = 72$, what number must $p$ be? Show all your working.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">If $p  \ \Phi \ p = 72$, what number must $p$ be? Show all your working.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
p  \ \Phi \ p &= 72 \\\\
(p + p) \times p              &= 72  \\\\
2p \times p                   &= 72  \\\\
2p^2                          &= 72  \\\\
p^2                           &= \dfrac{72}{2}  \\\\
p^2                           &= \dfrac{36 \times 2}{2}  \\\\
p^2                           &= \dfrac{36 \times \cancel{2}}{\cancel{2}}  \\\\
p^2                           &= 36 \\\\
p                             &= \sqrt{36} \\\\
p                             &= 6
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$6$

</div>
</div>

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">$
\begin{aligned}
p  \ \Phi \ p &= 72 \\\\
(p + p) \times p              &= 72  \\\\
2p \times p                   &= 72  \\\\

p^2                           &= \dfrac{72}{2}  \\\\
p^2                           &= \dfrac{36 \times 2}{2}  \\\\
p^2                           &= \dfrac{36 \times \cancel{2}}{\cancel{2}}  \\\\
p^2                           &= 36 \\\\
p                             &= \sqrt{36} \\\\
p                             &= 6
\end{aligned}
$

**Question**

Explain why $x  \ \Phi \ y$ is not the same as $y  \ \Phi \ x$.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Explain why $x  \ \Phi \ y$ is not the same as $y  \ \Phi \ x$.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$\begin{aligned}
x \ \Phi \ y &= (x + y) \times y \\\\
&= xy + y^2 \\\\
y \ \Phi \ x &= (y + x) \times x \\\\
&= xy + x^2
\end{aligned}$

$y^2$ is not necessarily equal to $x^2$, so $xy + y^2$ is not the same as $xy + x^2$.
</div>
