<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Julia thinks of a number. She multiplies it by $5$ and then subtracts $14$. The answer she gets is $46$. What number did she originally think of?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Julia thinks of a number. She multiplies it by $5$ and then subtracts $14$. The answer she gets is $46$. What number did she originally think of?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
5 \times a - 14     &= 46 \\\\
5a                  &= 46 + 14 \\\\
5a                  &= 60 \\\\
a                   &= \dfrac{60}{5} \\\\
a                   &= \dfrac {5 \times 12} {5} \\\\
a                   &= \dfrac {\cancel {5} \times 12} {\cancel {5}} \\\\
a                   &= 12
\end{aligned}
$

Number $= 12$
</div>
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A boy spent $\dfrac{3}{8}$ of his allowance and put $\dfrac{1}{2}$ of the remainder in the bank. He then had $\pounds 15$ left. 

How much money did he have to start with?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A boy spent $\dfrac{3}{8}$ of his allowance and put $\dfrac{1}{2}$ of the remainder in the bank. He then had $\pounds 15$ left. 
<emptyline>
How much money did he have to start with?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let total money $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {3a} {8} + \dfrac {1} {2} \times (a - \dfrac {3a} {8}) + 15 &= a \\\\
a - \dfrac {3a} {8} - \dfrac {1} {2} \times (a - \dfrac {3a} {8})                  &= 15 \\\\
a - \dfrac {3a} {8} - \dfrac {1} {2} \times (\dfrac {8a} {8} - \dfrac {3a} {8})   &= 15 \\\\
a - \dfrac {3a} {8} - \dfrac {1} {2} \times \dfrac {5a} {8}                        &= 15 \\\\
a - \dfrac {3a} {8} - \dfrac {5a} {16}                                       &= 15 \\\\
\dfrac {16a} {16} - \dfrac {6a} {16} - \dfrac {5a} {16}                        &= 15 \\\\
\dfrac {16a - 6a - 5a} {16}                                                &= 15 \\\\
\dfrac {5a} {16}                                                           &= 15 \\\\
a                                                                          &= \dfrac {15 \times 16} {5} \\\\
a                                                                          &= \dfrac {3 \times 5 \times 16} {5} \\\\
a                                                                          &= \dfrac {3 \times \cancel {5} \times 16} {\cancel {5}} \\\\
a                                                                          &= 3 \times 16 \\\\
a                                                                                                  &= \pounds 48 
\end{aligned}
$

Total money $= \pounds 48$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$\pounds 48$

</div>
</div>
<div class="workingscodeblock">
<div class="tipcodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="tipcodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Tips Raw</strong>
</div>

</code></pre>

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Let total money $= a$
<emptyline>
As per the question,
<emptyline>
$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {3a} {8} + \dfrac {1} {2} \times (a - \dfrac {3a} {8}) + 15 &= a \\\\
a - \dfrac {3a} {8} - \dfrac {1} {2} \times (a - \dfrac {3a} {8})                  &= 15 \\\\
a - \dfrac {3a} {8} - \dfrac {1} {2} \times (\dfrac {8a} {8} - \dfrac {3a} {8})   &= 15 \\\\
a - \dfrac {3a} {8} - \dfrac {1} {2} \times \dfrac {5a} {8}                        &= 15 \\\\
a - \dfrac {3a} {8} - \dfrac {5a} {16}                                       &= 15 \\\\
\dfrac {16a} {16} - \dfrac {6a} {16} - \dfrac {5a} {16}                        &= 15 \\\\
\dfrac {16a - 6a - 5a} {16}                                                &= 15 \\\\
\dfrac {5a} {16}                                                           &= 15 \\\\
a                                                                          &= \dfrac {15 \times 16} {5} \\\\
a                                                                          &= \dfrac {3 \times 5 \times 16} {5} \\\\
a                                                                          &= \dfrac {3 \times \cancel {5} \times 16} {\cancel {5}} \\\\
a                                                                          &= 3 \times 16 \\\\
a                                                                                                  &= \pounds 48 
\end{aligned}
$
<emptyline>
Total money $= \pounds 48$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Vale Youth Club has $126$ members. There are $20$ more boys than 
girls. How many girls are members of the Youth Club? 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Vale Youth Club has $126$ members. There are $20$ more boys than 
girls. How many girls are members of the Youth Club? 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number of girls $= g$

Number of boys $= g + 20$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
g + (g + 20)                                              &= 126 \\\\
2g + 20                                                   &= 126 \\\\
2g                                                        &= 126 - 20 \\\\
2g                                                        &= 106 \\\\
g                                                         &= \dfrac {106} {2} \\\\
g                                                         &= \dfrac {2 \times 53} {2} \\\\
g                                                         &= \dfrac {\cancel{2} \times 53} {\cancel{2}} \\\\
g                                                         &= 53
\end{aligned}
$

Number of girls $= 53$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$53$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

How much would it cost for one pack of sandwiches, one biscuit and one cup of tea?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">How much would it cost for one pack of sandwiches, one biscuit and one cup of tea?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the cost of a pack of sandwiches $= s$

Let the cost of a biscuit $= b$

Let the cost of a cup of tea $= t$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
s + b + 2t  &= 5.80 \\\\
2s + 2b + t &= 6.50
\end{aligned}
$

Let's add both equations,

$
\begin{aligned}
(s + b + 2t) + (2s + 2b + t)    &= 5.80 + 6.50 \\\\
3s + 3b + 3t                &= 12.30 \\\\
3 \times (s + b + t)        &= 12.30 \\\\
s + b + t                   &= \dfrac {12.30} {3} \\\\
s + b + t                   &= \pounds 4.10
\end{aligned}
$

Cost $= \pounds 4.10$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$\pounds 4.10$

</div>
</div>

\end{aligned}

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

The difference between a third of a certain number and one quarter of the number is $5$. What is the number?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">The difference between a third of a certain number and one quarter of the number is $5$. What is the number?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {a} {3} - \dfrac {a} {4}                                     &= 5 \\\\
\dfrac {a \times 4} {3 \times 4} - \dfrac {a \times 3} {4 \times 3} &= 5 \\\\
\dfrac {4a} {12} - \dfrac {3a} {12}                                 &= 5 \\\\
\dfrac {4a - 3a} {12}                                               &= 5 \\\\
\dfrac {a} {12}                                                     &= 5 \\\\
a                                                                   &= 5 \times 12 \\\\
a                                                                   &= 60
\end{aligned}
$

Number $= 60$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$60$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Find $n$ if $126 \div n = 9$

- $14$
- $16$
- $17$
- $11$
- $13$ 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>

<emptyline>

- $16$
- $17$
- $11$
- $13$ 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">

126 \div n          &= 9 \\\\
\dfrac {126} {n}    &= 9 \\\\

n                   &= \dfrac {9 \times 14} {9} \\\\
n                   &= \dfrac {\cancel {9} \times 14} {\cancel {9}} \\\\
n                   &= 14
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

$P = 9a - 7b^{2}$

Work out the value of $P$ when $a = 3$ and $b = -2$.

- $14$
- $-169$
- $3$
- $55$
- $-1$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">$P = 9a - 7b^{2}$
<emptyline>
Work out the value of $P$ when $a = 3$ and $b = -2$.
<emptyline>
- $14$
- $-169$
- $3$
- $55$
- $-1$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
P   &= 9a - 7b^2 \\\\
    &= 9 \times 3 - 7 \times (-2)^2 \\\\
    &= 27 - 7 \times 4 \\\\
    &= 27 - 28 \\\\
    &= -1
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="option" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Option**

<p>E</p>
</div>
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Khris Krigle gives each of his helper's one twelfth of a giant chocolate bar that he had. 
One third of the bar was left. How many helpers did he have?

- $6$
- $8$
- $12$
- $15$
- $18$ 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Khris Krigle gives each of his helper's one twelfth of a giant chocolate bar that he had. 
One third of the bar was left. How many helpers did he have?
<emptyline>
- $6$
- $8$
- $12$
- $15$
- $18$ 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number of helpers $= h$

Let the size of the chocolate bar $= b$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
h \times \dfrac {b} {12} + \dfrac {b} {3}          &= b \\\\
\dfrac {h \times b} {12}                           &= b - \dfrac {b} {3} \\\\
\dfrac {h \times b} {12}                           &= \dfrac {3b} {3}  - \dfrac {b} {3} \\\\
\dfrac {h \times b} {12}                           &= \dfrac {3b - b} {3} \\\\
\dfrac {h \times b} {12}                           &= \dfrac {2b} {3} \\\\
h                                                  &= \dfrac {2b \times 12} {3 \times b} \\\\
h                                                  &= \dfrac {2 \times b \times 4 \times 3} {3 \times b} \\\\
h                                                  &= \dfrac {2 \times \cancel b \times 4 \times \cancel 3} {\cancel 3 \times \cancel b} \\\\
h                                                &= 8
\end{aligned}
$

Number of helpers $= 8$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="option" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Option**

<p>B</p>
</div>
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$8$

</div>
</div>

$560 \div \boxed{ \phantom{70} } = 8$

- $7$
- $70$

- $0.7$
- $0.007$

</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

I think of a number, multiply by $2$ and add $5$. The answer is $19$. What was the number?

- $6$
- $8$
- $7$
- $48$
- $28$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>

<emptyline>
- $6$
- $8$
- $7$
- $48$
- $28$
</code></pre>
</div>

**Working**

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
2 \times a + 5  &= 19 \\\\
2a              &= 19 - 5 \\\\
2a              &= 14 \\\\
a               &= \dfrac{14} {2} \\\\
a               &= \dfrac {2 \times 7} {2} \\\\
a               &= \dfrac {\cancel {2} \times 7} {\cancel {2}} \\\\
a               &= 7
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Think of two integers that have a product of $18$ and a difference 
that is the same as one of the two integers that you are thinking of. 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Think of two integers that have a product of $18$ and a difference 
that is the same as one of the two integers that you are thinking of. 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the first number $= a$

Let the second number $= b$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
a \times b            &= 18 \\\\
a - b                 &= b \\\\
a                     &= 2b
\end{aligned}
$

Substituting the value of $a$ from second equation to first equation,

$
\begin{aligned}
a \times b            &= 18 \\\\
2b \times b           &= 18 \\\\
2 b^2                 &= 18 \\\\
b ^ 2                 &= \dfrac {18} {2} \\\\
b ^ 2                 &= \dfrac {2 \times 9} {2} \\\\
b ^ 2                 &= \dfrac {\cancel {2} \times 9} {\cancel {2}} \\\\
b ^ 2                 &= 9 \\\\
b                     &= \sqrt {9} \\\\
b                     &= 3
\end{aligned}
$

Substituting the value of $b$ in second equation.

$
\begin{aligned}
a - b &= b \\\\
a - 3 &= 3 \\\\
a     &= 3 + 3 \\\\
a     &= 6
\end{aligned}
$

Numbers $= 3$, $6$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$3$

</div>
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Sam thinks of a number. 
If you double the number and add $6$ you get the same answer as multiplying it by $3$ and subtracting $3$.

Find the number that Sam was thinking of. 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</code></pre>
</div>

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
2 \times a + 6    &= 3 \times a - 3 \\\\
2a + 6            &= 3a - 3 \\\\
3a - 2a            &= 6 + 3 \\\\
a                 &= 9
\end{aligned}
$

Number $= 9$
</div>
</div>

**Question**

Three friends went to a burger restaurant.

Tom had a burger and chips and he paid $\pounds 8.00$.

Fred had two burgers and a drink. Fred paid $\pounds 15.00$.

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the cost of a burger $= b$

Let the cost of chips $= c$

Let the cost of a drink $= d$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
b + c &= 8.00 \quad &(1) \\\\
2b + d &= 15.00 \quad &(2) \\\\
b + d &= 8.50 \quad &(3)
\end{aligned}
$

Subtract equation $(3)$ from equation $(2)$ to find the cost of a burger.

$
\begin{aligned}
(2b + d) - (b + d) &= 15.00 - 8.50 \\\\
2b + d - b - d &= 6.50 \\\\
b &= \pounds 6.50
\end{aligned}
$

Substitute the value of $b$ in equation $(3)$ to find the cost of a drink.

$
\begin{aligned}
6.50 + d &= 8.50 \\\\
d &= 8.50 - 6.50 \\\\
d &= \pounds 2.00
\end{aligned}
$

Substitute the value of $b$ in equation $(1)$ to find the cost of chips.

$
\begin{aligned}
6.50 + c &= 8.00 \\\\
c &= 8.00 - 6.50 \\\\
c &= \pounds 1.50
\end{aligned}
$

Cost of burger $= \pounds 6.50$

Cost of chips $= \pounds 1.50$

Cost of drink $= \pounds 2.00$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

Burger $=$ $\pounds 6.50$

</div>
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

Chips $=$ $\pounds 1.50$

</div>
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

Drink $=$ $\pounds 2.00$

</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

I think of a number, double it, take the answer away from $41$, and I am left with $3$. What number did I think of?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">I think of a number, double it, take the answer away from $41$, and I am left with $3$. What number did I think of?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
41 - 2a         &= 3 \\\\
41 - 3          &= 2a \\\\
2a              &= 41 - 3 \\\\
2a              &= 38 \\\\
a               &= \dfrac {38} {2} \\\\
a               &= \dfrac {2 \times 19} {2} \\\\
a               &= \dfrac {\cancel {2} \times 19} {\cancel {2}} \\\\
a               &= 19
\end{aligned}
$

Number $= 19$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$19$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Ravi has two sisters, Harsha and Harpreet. He likes to share out his sweets unfairly. 
One day he gives Harsha twice as many as he gives himself, and he gives Harpreet half 
as many as he gives himself. 
If there are $42$ sweets in total how many does Ravi get?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Ravi has two sisters, Harsha and Harpreet. He likes to share out his sweets unfairly. 
One day he gives Harsha twice as many as he gives himself, and he gives Harpreet half 
as many as he gives himself. 
If there are $42$ sweets in total how many does Ravi get?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number of sweets Harpreet gets $= h$

Number of sweets Ravi gets $= 2h$

Number of sweets Harsha gets $= 2 \times 2h = 4h$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
h + 2h + 4h             &= 42 \\\\
7h                      &= 42 \\\\
h                       &= \dfrac{42}{7} \\\\
h                       &= \dfrac{7 \times 6}{7} \\\\
h                       &= \dfrac{\cancel{7} \times 6}{\cancel{7}} \\\\
h                       &= 6 \\\\
\text{Sweets Ravi gets} &= 2h \\\\
                        &= 2 \times 6 \\\\
                        &= 12
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

An orange costs twice as much as an apple. Which one of the following does not cost the same as the other four?

- Two oranges and three apples

- Seven apples

- One orange and five apples

- Three oranges and one apple

- Four oranges

</div>

<emptyline>

<emptyline>

<emptyline>
- Three oranges and one apple
<emptyline>

</code></pre>

As per the question,

| Option                                   | Cost                 | Total |
|:----------------------------------------:|:-------------------------------:|:-----------|

| $7$ apples                               | $7 \times a$                    | $7a$       |

| $3$ oranges and $1$ apple                | $(3 \times 2a) + (1 \times a)$  | $7a$       |
| $4$ oranges                              | $4 \times 2a$                    | $8a$       |

All options cost $7a$ except $4$ oranges which costs $8a$.

Four oranges

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

What number do you multiply $0.2$ by to get an answer of $6?$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">What number do you multiply $0.2$ by to get an answer of $6?$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number $= a$.

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
a \times 0.2    &= 6 \\\\
a \times \dfrac{2}{10}    &= 6 \\\\
a               &= \dfrac {6 \times 10} {2} \\\\
a               &= \dfrac {6 \times 2 \times 5} {2} \\\\
a               &= \dfrac {6 \times \cancel {2} \times 5} {\cancel {2}} \\\\
a               &= 6 \times 5 \\\\
a               &= 30
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$30$

</div>

**Question**

Write down two numbers which differ by $2$ and multiply to $168$.

- The product of the $2$ numbers is $168$. 
- The difference of the $2$ numbers is $2$.

Factor pairs of $168$ that has difference of $2 = (12, 14)$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Suzie is given a number and told to divide it by $2$ and then subtract $14$. 
Although Suzie starts with the correct number she gets in a muddle and multiplies by $2$ and then adds $14$ instead. 
If her final answer is $142$, what answer should she have got?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Suzie is given a number and told to divide it by $2$ and then subtract $14$. 
Although Suzie starts with the correct number she gets in a muddle and multiplies by $2$ and then adds $14$ instead. 
If her final answer is $142$, what answer should she have got?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
2a + 14           &= 142 \\\\
2a                &= 142 - 14 \\\\
2a                &= 128 \\\\
a                 &= \dfrac{128}{2} \\\\
a                 &= \dfrac{64 \times 2}{2} \\\\
a                 &= \dfrac{64 \times \cancel{2}}{\cancel{2}} \\\\
a                 &= 64 \\\\
\text{Correct Answer }   &= \dfrac{64}{2} - 14 \\\\ 
                                    &= \dfrac{64}{2} - 14 \\\\ 
                                    &= \dfrac{32 \times 2}{2} - 14 \\\\ 
                                    &= \dfrac{32 \times \cancel{2}}{\cancel{2}} - 14 \\\\ 
                                    &= 32 - 14 \\\\ 
                                    &= 18
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$18$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

The cost of $3$ apples, $5$ oranges and $2$ grapefruit is $\pounds 3.02$. 

The cost of $5$ apples, $7$ oranges and $4$ grapefruit is $\pounds 5.12$. 

What is the total cost of one of each type of fruit?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">The cost of $3$ apples, $5$ oranges and $2$ grapefruit is $\pounds 3.02$. 
<emptyline>
The cost of $5$ apples, $7$ oranges and $4$ grapefruit is $\pounds 5.12$. 
<emptyline>
What is the total cost of one of each type of fruit?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let cost of an apple $= a$

Let cost of an orange $= o$

Let cost of a grapefruit $= g$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
3a + 5o + 2g                                &= 3.02 \\\\
5a + 7o + 4g                                &= 5.12
\end{aligned}
$

Subtracting equation $1$ from equation $2$

$
\begin{aligned}
5a + 7o + 4g - (3a + 5o + 2g)                     &= 5.12 - 3.02 \\\\
2a + 2o + 2g                                      &= 2.10 \\\\
2 \times (a + o + g)                              &= 2.10 \\\\
a + o + g                                         &= \dfrac{2.10}{2} \\\\
a + o + g                                         &= \pounds 1.05\\\\
\end{aligned}
$

Total cost $= \pounds 1.05$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$\pounds 1.05$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Children are offered a $25\%$ discount on the cost of an adult ticket to visit Hamshaw House. 
Senior citizens are given a $20\%$ discount. If a child's ticket costs $\pounds 30$, how much does a senior citizen pay?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Children are offered a $25\%$ discount on the cost of an adult ticket to visit Hamshaw House. 
Senior citizens are given a $20\%$ discount. If a child's ticket costs $\pounds 30$, how much does a senior citizen pay?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the cost of an adult ticket $= a$

If children are offered a $25 \%$ discount, they pay $100 - 25 = 75 \%$ of the adult ticket.

Senior citizens are offered a $20 \%$ discount, so they pay $100 - 20 = 80 \%$ of the adult ticket.

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac{75}{100} \times a &= 30 \\\\
a &= \dfrac{30 \times 100}{75} \\\\
a &= \dfrac{3 \times 10 \times 4 \times 25}{3 \times 25} \\\\
a &= \dfrac{\cancel{3} \times 10 \times 4 \times \cancel{25}}{\cancel{3} \times \cancel{25}} \\\\
a &= \pounds 40 \\\\
\text{Senior Cost} &= \dfrac{80}{100} \times 40 \\\\
&= \dfrac{80}{100} \times 40 \\\\
&= \dfrac{8 \cancel{0} \times 4 \cancel{0}}{1\cancel{0} \cancel{0}} \\\\
&= 8 \times 4 \\\\
&= \pounds 32
\end{aligned}
$

Senior citizen pays $= \pounds 32$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$\pounds 32$

</div>
</div>

</div>

**Question**

Five Whatsits and four Thingummyjigs cost $\pounds 14.95$. Work out the cost of a Whatsit in each of the following cases: 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

When twelve Thingummyjigs cost $\pounds 10.20$. 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">When twelve Thingummyjigs cost $\pounds 10.20$. 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
12b                                                       &= 10.20 \\\\
\dfrac{12b}{3}                                            &= \dfrac{10.20}{3} \\\\
\dfrac{4 \times 3 \times b}{3}                            &= \dfrac{3.4 \times 3}{3} \\\\
\dfrac{4 \times \cancel{3} \times b}{\cancel{3}}          &= \dfrac{3.4 \times \cancel{3}}{\cancel{3}} \\\\
4b                                                        &= 3.4
\end{aligned}
$

Let's substitute the value of $4b$ in first equation.

$
\begin{aligned}
5a + 4b           &= 14.95 \\\\
5a + 3.4          &= 14.95 \\\\
5a                &= 11.55 \\\\
a                 &= \dfrac{11.55}{5} \\\\
a                 &= \dfrac{2.31 \times 5}{5} \\\\
a                 &= \dfrac{2.31 \times \cancel{5}}{\cancel{5}} \\\\
a                 &= \pounds 2.31 \\\\
4b                &= 3.4 \\\\ 
b                 &= \dfrac{0.85 \times 4}{4} \\\\ 
b                 &= \dfrac{0.85 \times \cancel{4}}{\cancel{4}} \\\\ 
b                 &= \pounds 0.85
\end{aligned}
$

The cost of Whatsits $= \pounds 2.31$

The cost of Thingummyjigs $= \pounds 0.85$

$\pounds 2.31$ and $\pounds 0.85$

b                          &= 2 \times 1.15 \\\\
b                          &= \pounds 2.3
\end{aligned}
$

The cost of Whatsits $= \pounds 1.15$

The cost of Thingummyjigs $= \pounds 2.3$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Pens cost $7 \ \text{p}$ each and pencils cost $5 \ \text{p}$ each.  I buy some pens and pencils which cost $55 \ \text{p}$ exactly.

How many of each did I buy?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Pens cost $7 \ \text{p}$ each and pencils cost $5 \ \text{p}$ each.  I buy some pens and pencils which cost $55 \ \text{p}$ exactly.
<emptyline>
How many of each did I buy?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number of pens $= a$

and the number of pencils $= b$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
7a + 5b       &= 55 \\\\
b            &= \dfrac{55 - 7a}{5}
\end{aligned}
$

We can easily infer the values by using trial and error. 

$(55 - 7a)$ must be a multiple of $5$ for $b$ to be a whole number. So $7a$ must also be a multiple of $5$.

| $a$ (pens) |     $b = (55 - 7a) \div 5$       | $b$ whole? |
|:-------------------:|:---------------------------------:|:----------:|
| $5$                 | $(55 - 7 \times 5) \div 5 = 20 \div 5 = 4$  | Yes  |
| $10$                | $(55 - 7 \times 10) \div 5 = -15 \div 5 = -3$ | No |

Number of pens $= 5$

Number of pencils $= 4$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

pens $=$ $5$

</div>
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

pencils $=$ $4$

</div>
</div>

**Question**

Mrs Catchpole gives the following instructions to her Year $6$ class:

-  Think of a number. 
-  Subtract $13$ from this number to get the first result. 
-  Go back to the original number and subtract 5 to get the second result. 
-  Multiply the first and second results together to get the final answer.

</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Snow White and the seven dwarves work in a mining company. 
As Chief Executive, Snow White earns as much as all the dwarves put together. 
Sneezy gets $24$ gold galleons a day. Sleepy earns $50\%$ more than Happy. 
Bashful earns twice as much as Grumpy who earns one more galleon than Sneezy. 
Doc gets $24$ galleons a day more than Dopey and between them they get four times that of Sneezy. 
Sleepy earns seven-eighths of Sneezy's salary.

Complete the table below to work out how much Snow White earns in a day.

|                |  Gold Galleons  |
|:--------------:|:---------------:|
|  Bashful       |                 | 
|  Doc           |                 |  
|  Dopey         |                 |   
|  Grumpy        |                 |   
|  Happy         |                 |   
|  Sleepy        |                 |   
|  Sneezy        |                 |   
|  Snow White    |                 |   


</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Snow White and the seven dwarves work in a mining company. 
As Chief Executive, Snow White earns as much as all the dwarves put together. 
Sneezy gets $24$ gold galleons a day. Sleepy earns $50\%$ more than Happy. 
Bashful earns twice as much as Grumpy who earns one more galleon than Sneezy. 
Doc gets $24$ galleons a day more than Dopey and between them they get four times that of Sneezy. 
Sleepy earns seven-eighths of Sneezy's salary.
<emptyline>
Complete the table below to work out how much Snow White earns in a day.
<emptyline>
|                |  Gold Galleons  |
|:--------------:|:---------------:|
|  Bashful       |                 | 
|  Doc           |                 |  
|  Dopey         |                 |   
|  Grumpy        |                 |   
|  Happy         |                 |   
|  Sleepy        |                 |   
|  Sneezy        |                 |   
|  Snow White    |                 |   
<emptyline>
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the question,

$\begin{aligned}
\text{Sneezy} &= 24 \ \text{galleons} \\\\
\text{Grumpy} &= \text{Sneezy} + 1 \\\\
&= 24 + 1 \\\\
&= 25 \ \text{galleons} \\\\
\text{Bashful} &= 2 \times \text{Grumpy} \\\\
&= 2 \times 25 \\\\
&= 50 \ \text{galleons} \\\\
\text{Sleepy} &= \dfrac{7}{8} \times \text{Sneezy} \\\\
&= \dfrac{7}{8} \times 24 \\\\
&= \dfrac{7 \times 24}{8} \\\\
&= \dfrac{7 \times 3 \times 8}{8} \\\\
&= \dfrac{7 \times 3 \times \cancel{8}}{\cancel{8}} \\\\
&= 21 \ \text{galleons}
\end{aligned}$

If Sleepy earns $50\%$ more than Happy, then Sleep earns $100 + 50 = 150\% = 1.5$ of Happy.

Let Happy earns $= h$

As per the question,

$\begin{aligned}
1.5h &= 21 \\\\
h    &= \dfrac{21}{1.5} \\\\
     &= \dfrac{21 \times 10}{15} \\\\
     &= \dfrac{7 \times 3 \times 2 \times 5}{3 \times 5} \\\\
     &= \dfrac{7 \times \cancel{3} \times 2 \times \cancel{5}}{\cancel{3} \times \cancel{5}} \\\\
      &= 14 \ \text{galleons} 
\end{aligned}$

Let Dopey earns $= p$

Doc earns $= p + 24$

As per the question,

$\begin{aligned}
(p + 24) + p &= 4 \times 24 \\\\
2p + 24     &= 96 \\\\
2p          &= 96 - 24 \\\\
2p          &= 72 \\\\
p           &= \dfrac{72}{2} \\\\
p           &= 36 \\\\
\text{Dopey}  &= 36 \ \text{galleons} \\\\
\text{Doc}   &= 36 + 24 \\\\
             &= 60 \ \text{galleons} \\\\
\text{Snow White} &= 24 + 25 + 50 + 21 + 14 + 36 + 60 \\\\
              &= 230 \ \text{galleons} 
\end{aligned}$

**Question**

Write down two numbers that add to $14$ and multiply to $48$.

Let the second number $=b$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
a + b               &= 14 \\\\
a \times b          &= 48
\end{aligned}
$

We can easily infer the values by using trial and error. Let's find out $2$ numbers which meets the following critiera based on the equations above.

- The product of the $2$ numbers is $48$.
- The addition of the $2$ numbers is $14$.

Factor pairs of $48 = (1, 48), (2, 24), (3, 16), (4, 12), (6, 8)$

| Factor pair $(a, b)$ |  $a + b$ | $= 14$? |
|:--------------------:|:------------------:|:------------------:|
| $(1, 48)$            | $1 + 48 = 49$      | No                 |
| $(2, 24)$             | $2 + 24 = 26$      | No                 |
| $(3, 16)$             | $3 + 16 = 19$      | No                 |
| $(4, 12)$             | $4 + 12 = 16$      | No                 |
| $(6, 8)$             | $6 + 8 = 14$      | Yes                |

A quick check shows $6$ and $8$ meets the criteria above.

Numbers $= 6$, $8$

He multiplies that number by $5$.

**Working**

Let the number $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {(5a -12)}{3} + 17                                    &= 38 \\\\
\dfrac {5a -12}{3}                                           &= 38 - 17\\\\
\dfrac {5a -12}{3}                                           &= 21 \\\\
5a - 12                                                      &= 21 \times 3 \\\\
5a - 12                                                      &= 63 \\\\  
5a                                                           &= 63 + 12 \\\\ 
5a                                                           &= 75 \\\\
a &= \dfrac{5 \times 15}{5} \\\\
a &= \dfrac{\cancel{5} \times 15}{\cancel{5}} \\\\
a                                                            &= 15
\end{aligned}
$

Number $= 15$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Elizabeth writes down:

One multiple of $13$ and two different factors of $77$.

Elizabeth adds up her three numbers. Her answer is greater than fifty but less than sixty.

What three numbers could Elizabeth have written down?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Elizabeth writes down:
<emptyline>
One multiple of $13$ and two different factors of $77$.
<emptyline>
Elizabeth adds up her three numbers. Her answer is greater than fifty but less than sixty.
<emptyline>
What three numbers could Elizabeth have written down?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the two factors of 77 $= a, b$

Let the multiple of 13 $= c$

As per the question,

50 < a + b + c < 60

Factors of $77 = 1, 7, 11, 77$

We can easily infer the values by using trial and error. Lets find out the value of a, b and c which satisfies the condition above.

We can ignore 77 as it is greater than 60.

|  c   |    a,b    |          sum           |  50 < sum < 60  |
|:----:|:---------:|:----------------------:|:---------------:|
| $13$ |  $1,7$    |  $13 + 1 + 7 = 21$     |       No        |
| $13$ |  $1,11$   |  $13 + 1 + 11 = 25$    |       No        |
| $13$ |  $7,11$   |  $13 + 7 + 11 = 31$    |       No        |
| $26$ |  $1,7$    |  $26 + 1 + 7 = 34$     |       No        |
| $26$ |  $1,11$   |  $26 + 1 + 11 = 38$    |       No        |
| $26$ |  $7,11$   |  $26 + 7 + 11 = 44$    |       No        |
| $39$ |  $1,7$    |  $39 + 1 + 7 = 47$     |       No        |
| $39$ |  $1,11$   |  $39 + 1 + 11 = 51$    |       Yes       |
| $39$ |  $7,11$   |  $39 + 7 + 11 = 57$    |       Yes       |

A quick check shows that $a = 1,b = 11,c = 39$ or $a = 7,b = 11,c = 39$ meets all the criteria above.

Numbers Elizabeth could have written down $= 1,11,39$ or $7,11,39$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$1,11,39$ or $7,11,39$

</div>
</div>

<li class="questionContainer">
<div class="question_envelope rag_not_found subquestion">
<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Annie and Bradley each think of a number. 

The difference between their numbers is $6$.

The sum of their numbers is $20$.

What are the two numbers?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Annie and Bradley each think of a number. 
<emptyline>
The difference between their numbers is $6$.
<emptyline>
The sum of their numbers is $20$.
<emptyline>
What are the two numbers?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number Annie thinks $= a$

Let the number Bradley thinks $= b$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned} 
a + b      &= 20 \\\\
a - b      &= 6         
\end{aligned}
$

There are two variables, $a$ and $b$. Let's eliminate to reduce it to just one variable.

Subtract the second equation from the first to reduce it to one variable.

$
\begin{aligned}
a + b - (a - b)     &= 20 - 6 \\\\
a + b -a + b        &= 14 \\\\
2b                  &= 14 \\\\
b                   &= \dfrac {14} {2} \\\\
b                   &= \dfrac {7 \times 2} {2} \\\\
b                   &= \dfrac {7 \times \cancel 2} {\cancel 2} \\\\
b                   &= 7
\end{aligned}
$

Let's substitute the value of $b$ in one of the initial equations.

$
\begin{aligned} 
a + b                          &= 20 \\\\
a + 7                          &= 20 \\\\
a                              &= 20 - 7 \\\\
a                              &= 13
\end{aligned}
$

Annie's number $= 13$

Bradley's number $= 7$
</div>
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$7, 13$

</div>
</div>

**Question**

Jack thinks of a number.

Jack calls his number $n$.

**Jack multiplies his number by $3$, and then subtracts $5$**.

**He gets the answer $16$**.

Use this information to write down an equation, and then solve it to find $n$.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

James counts down in $9$'s starting from $345$ until he passes zero. 
Which will be the last  positive number which he counts?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">James counts down in $9$'s starting from $345$ until he passes zero. 
Which will be the last  positive number which he counts?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

This is same as finding the remainder when $345$ is divided by $9$.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Last positive number}    &= \dfrac {345} {9} \\\\
											&= 38 \text{ remainder } 3 \\\\
											&= 3
\end{aligned}
$

Answer $= 3$
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Jack has thought of two numbers.

When he multiplies them together he gets $96$.

When he takes one number away from the other, he gets $4$.

What are the two numbers? 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$a \times b = 96$

We can easily infer the values by using trial and error. Let's find out $2$ numbers which meets the following critiera based on the equations above.

- The product of the $2$ numbers is $96$ 
- The difference of the $2$ numbers is $4$.

Factor pairs of $96 = (1, 96), (2, 48), (3, 32), (4, 24), (6, 16), (8, 12)$

Factor pairs of $96$ that have difference of $4 = (8, 12)$

Numbers are $= 8$, $12$

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

How much will $2$ Mars bars cost?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">How much will $2$ Mars bars cost?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR: It is really important to use the right units in calculations and convert where required.
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the cost of a Mars bar $= m$

Let the cost of a Crunchie bar $= c$

Let's convert all the costs into pence.

$\pounds 1.90 = 190 \ \text{p}$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
3m + c &= 190 \\\\
m + c &= 90
\end{aligned}
$

We have got $2$ variables and we have $2$ equations to solve them. Let's use elimination to reduce it to just one variable. 

Subtract the second equation from the first to eliminate $c$.

$
\begin{aligned}
(3m + c) - (m + c) &= 190 - 90 \\\\
2m &= 100 \\\\
m &= \dfrac{100}{2} \\\\
m &= \dfrac{50 \times 2}{2} \\\\
m &= \dfrac{50 \times \cancel 2}{\cancel 2} \\\\
m &= 50 \ \text{p} \\\\
\text{Cost of 2 Mars bars} &= 2 \times 50 \\\\
&= 100 \ \text{p} \\\\
&= \pounds 1.00
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$\pounds 1.00$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

If two numbers multiply to give $36$ and their sum is $15$, what are the two numbers?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">If two numbers multiply to give $36$ and their sum is $15$, what are the two numbers?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the first number $= a$

Let the second number $= b$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
a \times b          &= 36 \\\\
a + b               &= 15
\end{aligned}
$

We can easily infer the values by using trial and error. Let's find out $2$ numbers which meets the following critiera based on the equations above.

- The product of the $2$ numbers is $36$ 
- The sum of the $2$ numbers is $15$.

Factor pairs of $36 = (1, 36)$, $(2, 18)$, $(3, 12)$, $(4, 9)$, $(6, 6)$

| Factor pair $(a, b)$ |  $a + b$ | $= 15$? |
|:--------------------:|:------------------:|:------------------:|
| $(1, 36)$            | $1 + 36 = 37$      | No                 |
| $(2, 18)$             | $2 + 18 = 20$      | No                 |
| $(3, 12)$             | $3 + 12 = 15$      | Yes                 |
| $(4, 9)$             | $4 + 9 = 13$      | No                 |
| $(6, 6)$             | $6 + 6 = 12$      | No                |

A quick check shows $3$ and $12$ meets the criteria above.

Numbers $= 3$, $12$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$3, 12$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Kristina bought a bag of sweets and ate $\dfrac{3}{5}$  of them. If she ate $18$ sweets, how many sweets were left over?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Kristina bought a bag of sweets and ate $\dfrac{3}{5}$  of them. If she ate $18$ sweets, how many sweets were left over?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number of sweets $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac{3}{5} \times a &= 18 \\\\
a                     &= \dfrac{18 \times 5}{3} \\\\
a                     &= \dfrac{6 \times 3 \times 5}{3} \\\\
a                     &= \dfrac{6 \times \cancel 3 \times 5}{\cancel 3} \\\\
a                     &= 30 \\\\
\text{Sweets left} &= 30 - 18 \\\\
						     &= 12
\end{aligned}
$                     
</div>
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

If she ate $\dfrac{3}{5}$ of sweets, the sweets left over is $ 1 - \dfrac{3}{5} = \dfrac{2}{5} $ of the total sweets.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Sweets left} &= \dfrac{2}{5} \times 30 \\\\
					&= \dfrac{2 \times 30}{5} \\\\
					&= \dfrac{2 \times 6 \times 5}{5} \\\\
					&= \dfrac{2 \times 6 \times \cancel 5}{\cancel 5} \\\\
					&= 2 \times 6 \\\\
						     &= 12
\end{aligned}
$                     
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$12$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

In a money-bag there are an equal number of $2 \ \text{pence}$ and $5 \ \text{pence}$ pieces and no other coins. How many coins are in the bag altogether if the total amount of money is $\pounds 1.26?$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">In a money-bag there are an equal number of $2 \ \text{pence}$ and $5 \ \text{pence}$ pieces and no other coins. How many coins are in the bag altogether if the total amount of money is $\pounds 1.26?$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR: It is really important to use the right units in calculations and convert where required.
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the count of coins of each denomination $= c$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
2\ \text{p} \times c + 5\ \text{p} \times c &= \pounds 1.26 \\\\
2\ \text{p} \times c + 5\ \text{p} \times c &= 126 \ \text{p} \\\\
2c + 5c                                 &= 126 \\\\
7c                                      &= 126 \\\\
c                                       &= \dfrac {126} {7} \\\\
c                                       &= \dfrac {18 \times 7} { 7} \\\\
c                                       &= \dfrac {18 \times \cancel{7}} { \cancel{7} } \\\\
c                                       &= 18 \\\\
\text{Total coins}   &=  18 \times 2  \\\\
                     &= 36
\end{aligned}
$
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$36$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Oni has $11$ penpals. Last week she wrote to all of them.

She wrote a $4$-page letter to some of her penpals and a $3$-page letter to the rest. Altogether she wrote $38$ pages.

To how many penpals did Oni write a $3$-page letter?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Oni has $11$ penpals. Last week she wrote to all of them.
<emptyline>
She wrote a $4$-page letter to some of her penpals and a $3$-page letter to the rest. Altogether she wrote $38$ pages.
<emptyline>
To how many penpals did Oni write a $3$-page letter?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">

</div>

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number of penpals receiving a $3$-page letter $= a$

Then the number of penpals receiving a $4$-page letter $= 11 - a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
3 \times a + 4 \times (11 - a) &= 38 \\\\
3a + 44 - 4a &= 38 \\\\
a &= 44 - 38 \\\\
a &= 6
\end{aligned}
$

Penpals receiving a $3$-page letter $= 6$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

6

</div>
</div>

**Question**

If $a$ and $b$ are whole numbers, then $a \ \clubsuit \ b$ means $(b \times  b) \div (a + 1)$

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Find $1 \ \clubsuit \ 10$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Find $1 \ \clubsuit \ 10$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
&= 1 \ \clubsuit \ 10 \\\\
&= (10 \times 10) \div (1 + 1) \\\\
&= \dfrac{10 \times 10}{2} \\\\
&= \dfrac{5 \times 2 \times 10}{2} \\\\
&= \dfrac{5 \times \cancel 2 \times 10}{\cancel 2} \\\\
&= 5 \times 10 \\\\
&= 50
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$50$

</div>
</div>

Find $(3 \ \clubsuit \ 4) \ \clubsuit \ 5$

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
&= (3 \ \clubsuit \ 4) \ \clubsuit \ 5 \\\\
&= ((4 \times 4) \div (3 + 1)) \ \clubsuit \ 5 \\\\
&= (\dfrac{4 \times 4}{4}) \ \clubsuit \ 5 \\\\
&= (\dfrac{4 \times \cancel 4}{\cancel 4}) \ \clubsuit \ 5 \\\\
&= 4  \ \clubsuit \ 5 \\\\
&= (5 \times 5) \div (4 + 1) \\\\
&= \dfrac{5 \times 5}{5} \\\\
&= \dfrac{5 \times \cancel 5}{\cancel 5} \\\\
&= 5
\end{aligned}
$

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">%empty%

<div class="formulacodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">$
\begin{aligned}
&= (3 \ \clubsuit \ 4) \ \clubsuit \ 5 \\\\
&= ((4 \times 4) \div (3 + 1)) \ \clubsuit \ 5 \\\\
&= (\dfrac{4 \times 4}{4}) \ \clubsuit \ 5 \\\\
&= (\dfrac{4 \times \cancel 4}{\cancel 4}) \ \clubsuit \ 5 \\\\
&= 4  \ \clubsuit \ 5 \\\\
&= (5 \times 5) \div (4 + 1) \\\\
&= \dfrac{5 \times 5}{5} \\\\
&= \dfrac{5 \times \cancel 5}{\cancel 5} \\\\
&= 5
\end{aligned}
$

**Question**

If $6  \ \clubsuit \  y = 7$, what is the value of $y$?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">If $6  \ \clubsuit \  y = 7$, what is the value of $y$?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
6  \ \clubsuit \  y &= 7 \\\\
(y \times y) \div (6 + 1) &= 7 \\\\
\dfrac{y^2}{7} &= 7 \\\\
y ^2                &= 7 \times 7 \\\\
y ^2                      &= 49 \\\\
y                         &= \sqrt{49} \\\\
y                         &= 7
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$7$

**Working**

TODO: Its easier to solve it backwards. look at generated answers for details

Let the number of toffees $= a$

As per the question,

After eating $1$ and dividing it equally with emily, toffees left $= b = \dfrac{(a-1)}{2}$

Again after eating one and dividing it equally with Detti, toffees left $= c = \dfrac{b-1}{2}$

After eating one and giving last to Sean, toffees left $= c - 1 -1 = 0$

So,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Initial toffees}  &= a \\\\
\text{After eating 1}  &= a - 1 \\\\
\text{Shared with Emily} &= \dfrac{a - 1}{2} \\\\
\text{After eating 1 more}  &= \dfrac{a - 1}{2} - 1 \\\\
\text{Shared with Detti} &= \dfrac{1}{2} \times \left(\dfrac{a - 1}{2} - 1\right) \\\\
\text{After eating 1}  &= c - 1 \\\\
\text{Given to Sean} &= c - 1 - 1 = 0 \\\\
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Initial toffees}  &= a \\\\
\text{After eating 1}  &= a - 1 \\\\
\text{Shared with Emily} &= \dfrac{a - 1}{2} \\\\
\text{After eating 1 more}  &= \dfrac{a - 1}{2} - 1 \\\\
\text{Shared with Detti} &= \dfrac{1}{2} \times \left(\dfrac{a - 1}{2} - 1\right) \\\\
\text{After eating 1}  &= c - 1 \\\\
\text{Given to Sean} &= c - 1 - 1 = 0 \\\\
\end{aligned}
$

Number of toffees detti got $= 2$

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$2$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Three pet rabbits cost $\pounds 19.70$.

The second rabbit cost $\pounds 2$ more than the first.

The third rabbit cost $80 \ \text{p}$ less than the second. 

What is the cost of the first rabbit?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Three pet rabbits cost $\pounds 19.70$.
<emptyline>
The second rabbit cost $\pounds 2$ more than the first.
<emptyline>
The third rabbit cost $80 \ \text{p}$ less than the second. 
<emptyline>
What is the cost of the first rabbit?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the cost of the first rabbit $= r$

Cost of the second rabbit $= r + 2$

Cost of the third rabbit $= r + 2 - 0.80$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
r + (r +2) + (r + 2 - 0.8) &= 19.70 \\\\
3 r + 3.2                 &= 19.70 \\\\
3 r                       &= 19.70 - 3.2 \\\\
3 r                       &= 16.50 \\\\
r                         &= \dfrac {16.50} {3} \\\\
r                         &= \pounds 5.50
\end{aligned}
$

Cost of the first rabbit $=\pounds 5.50$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$\pounds 5.50$

</div>
</div>

**Question**

Emily's brother, Jack, is now $105\ \text{cm}$ tall, having grown by one sixth of his height a year ago. How tall was Jack one year ago?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Emily's brother, Jack, is now $105\ \text{cm}$ tall, having grown by one sixth of his height a year ago. How tall was Jack one year ago?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">
%empty%

</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let Jack's height one year ago $= h$

As per the question,

$\begin{aligned}
h + \dfrac{h}{6} &= 105 \\\\
\dfrac{6h}{6} + \dfrac{h}{6} &= 105 \\\\
\dfrac{6h + h}{6} &= 105 \\\\
\dfrac{7h}{6} &= 105 \\\\
h &= \dfrac{105 \times 6}{7} \\\\
h &= \dfrac{7 \times 15 \times 6}{7} \\\\
h &= \dfrac{\cancel{7} \times 15 \times 6}{\cancel{7}} \\\\
h &= 90 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$90 \text { cm}$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Amir, Anna and Arjun have bought some fruit at a market stall.

Amir bought $2$ Pears and $1$ Mango for $\pounds 1.35$

Anna bought $1$ Pear and $2$ Mangos for $\pounds 1.20$

Arjun bought $1$ Pear, $1$ Mango and $1$ Apple for $\pounds 1$

How much, in pence, did the apple cost?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Amir, Anna and Arjun have bought some fruit at a market stall.
<emptyline>
Amir bought $2$ Pears and $1$ Mango for $\pounds 1.35$
<emptyline>
Anna bought $1$ Pear and $2$ Mangos for $\pounds 1.20$
<emptyline>
Arjun bought $1$ Pear, $1$ Mango and $1$ Apple for $\pounds 1$
<emptyline>
How much, in pence, did the apple cost?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the cost of a pear $= p$

Let the cost of a mango $= m$

Let the cost of an apple $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
2p + m    &= 1.35  && (1) \\\\
p + 2m    &= 1.20  && (2) \\\\
p + m + a &= 1    && (3)
\end{aligned}
$

Let's add equation $(1)$ and $(2)$

$
\begin{aligned}
(2p + m) + (p + 2m)   &= 1.35 + 1.20 \\\\
3p + 3m           &= 2.55 \\\\
3(p + m)          &= 2.55 \\\\
p + m             &= \dfrac{2.55}{3} \\\\
p + m             &= \pounds 0.85
\end{aligned}
$

Substituting the value of $p + m$ into $(3)$, we have

$
\begin{aligned}
(p + m) + a         &= 1 \\\\
0.85 + a         &= 1 \\\\
a                   &= 1 - 0.85 \\\\
a                   &= \pounds 0.15 \\\\
a                   &= 15 \ \text{p}
\end{aligned}
$

Cost of the apple $= 15 \ \text{p}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$15 \ \text{p}$

</div>
</div>
