The rule is to divide by $4$ and then add $6$.

Since $6$ is a whole number, for the final result to be a whole number, the result of dividing the input by $4$ must also be a whole number.

Therefore, the input numbers must be multiples of $4$.

Answer = multiples of $4$

a              &= 12 \times 4 \\\\
a              &= 48
\end{aligned}
$

**Question**

A number is put through the number machine twice.

After the second time, the output number is $9$.

Work out the original input number.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A number is put through the number machine twice.
<emptyline>
After the second time, the output number is $9$.
<emptyline>
Work out the original input number.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let do it step by step.

Let the intermediate output after the first pass $= a$

As per the question,

$\begin{aligned}
(a \div 4) + 6 &= 9 \\\\
\dfrac{a}{4} + 6 &= 9 \\\\
\dfrac{a}{4}     &= 9 - 6 \\\\
\dfrac{a}{4}     &= 3 \\\\
a                &= 3 \times 4 \\\\
a                &= 12
\end{aligned}$

Now, let the original input number $= b$

$\begin{aligned}
( b \div 4) + 6 &= 12 \\\\
\dfrac{b}{4} + 6 &= 12 \\\\
\dfrac{b}{4}     &= 12 - 6 \\\\
\dfrac{b}{4}     &= 6 \\\\
b                &= 6 \times 4 \\\\
b                &= 24
\end{aligned}$

Input number $=24$
</div>
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

![papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2013/group-1/s01-q20-i00.png](/assets/papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2013/group-1/s01-q20-i00.png "papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2013/group-1/s01-q20-i00.png")

At SuperMart, a packet of jam tarts costs $\pounds 1.20$.

This week, there is a special offer:

*If you buy one packet, you can buy a second packet at half price.*

Erika needs to buy $13$ packets of jam tarts.

Using the special offer, how much will it cost Erika to buy $13$ packets?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">%image%
<emptyline>
At SuperMart, a packet of jam tarts costs $\pounds 1.20$.
<emptyline>
This week, there is a special offer:
<emptyline>
*If you buy one packet, you can buy a second packet at half price.*
<emptyline>
Erika needs to buy $13$ packets of jam tarts.
<emptyline>
Using the special offer, how much will it cost Erika to buy $13$ packets?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Cost of 1st packet} &= \pounds 1.20 \\\\
\text{Cost of 2nd packet (half price)} &= \dfrac{1.20}{2} \\\\
&= \pounds 0.60 \\\\
\text{Cost of a pair (2 packets)} &= 1.20 + 0.60 \\\\
&= \pounds 1.80 \\\\
\text {Number of pairs} &= \dfrac{13}{2} \\\\
&= 6 \ \text{pairs and} \ 1 \ \text{packet remaining} \\\\
\text{Total Cost} &= 6 \times 1.80 + 1 \times 1.20 \\\\
&= 10.80 + 1.20 \\\\
&= \pounds 12
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$\pounds 12$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A shopping bag, of mass $0.4 \ \text{kg}$, and its contents have 
a total mass of $2.5 \ \text{kg}$.

Inside the shopping bag are the following items:

$2$ bags of carrots, each with a mass of $250 \ \text{grams}$

$1$ cabbage with a mass of $\dfrac{3}{4} \ \text{kilogram}$

$1$ bag of potatoes

![papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2013/group-1/s01-q30-i00.png](/assets/papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2013/group-1/s01-q30-i00.png "papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2013/group-1/s01-q30-i00.png")

Use this information to work out the mass of the bag of potatoes.

Give your answer in $\text{grams}$.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A shopping bag, of mass $0.4 \ \text{kg}$, and its contents have 
a total mass of $2.5 \ \text{kg}$.
<emptyline>
Inside the shopping bag are the following items:
<emptyline>
$2$ bags of carrots, each with a mass of $250 \ \text{grams}$
<emptyline>
$1$ cabbage with a mass of $\dfrac{3}{4} \ \text{kilogram}$
<emptyline>
$1$ bag of potatoes
<emptyline>
%image%
<emptyline>
Use this information to work out the mass of the bag of potatoes.
<emptyline>
Give your answer in $\text{grams}$.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the mass of the bag of potatoes (in $\text{kg}$) $= p$

$\begin{aligned}
\text{Total mass} &= 2.5 \ \text{kg} \\\\
\text{Shopping bag} &= 0.4 \ \text{kg} \\\\
\text{Mass of cabbage}      &= \dfrac{3}{4} \ \text{kg} \\\\
                            &= 0.75 \ \text{kg} \\\\
\text{Mass of carrots}      &= 2 \times 250 \ \text{grams} \\\\
                            &= 500 \ \text{grams} \\\\
                            &= 0.5 \ \text{kg}
\end{aligned}$

As per the question,

$\begin{aligned}
0.4 + 0.75 + 0.5 + p &= 2.5 \\\\
1.65 + p            &= 2.5 \\\\
p                   &= 2.5 - 1.65 \\\\
p                   &= 0.85 \ \text{kg} \\\\
p                   &= 850 \ \text{grams}
\end{aligned}$

Mass of the bag of potatoes $= 850 \ \text{grams}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$850 \ \text{grams}$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

George buys $5$ packets of oranges and some packets of apples.

In total he has $31$ pieces of fruit.

How many packets of apples did George buy?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">George buys $5$ packets of oranges and some packets of apples.
<emptyline>
In total he has $31$ pieces of fruit.
<emptyline>
How many packets of apples did George buy?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number of packets of apple $=a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
5 \times 3 + 4 \times a  &= 31 \\\\
15 + 4a                  &= 31 \\\\
4a                       &= 31 - 15 \\\\
4a                       &= 16 \\\\
a                        &= \dfrac{16}{4} \\\\
a                        &= \dfrac{4 \times 4}{4} \\\\ 
a                        &= \dfrac{4 \times \cancel 4}{\cancel 4} \\\\
a                        &= 4
\end{aligned}
$

Number of packets of apple $= 4$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$4$

</div>
</div>

**Question**

Chris buys $2$ more packets of apples than packets of oranges.

In total he has $29$ pieces of fruit.

How many packets of each type of fruit did Chris buy?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<emptyline>

</code></pre>

<div class="workings">

Let the number of packets of apples $=a + 2$ 

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
a\times 3 + (a  + 2) \times 4 &= 29 \\\\
3a + 4a + 8                  &= 29 \\\\
7a + 8                       &= 29 \\\\

7a                           &= 21 \\\\
a                            &= \dfrac{21}{7} \\\\
a                            &= \dfrac{7 \times 3}{7} \\\\
a                            &= \dfrac{\cancel 7 \times 3}{\cancel 7} \\\\
a                            &= 3 \\\\
\text{Orange packets} &= 3 \\\\
\text{Apple packets}  &= 3 + 2 \\\\
                        &= 5
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

**Question**

Jamie buys $11$ packets of fruit.

How many more apples than oranges does he have?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

Let the number of packets of oranges $=11 - a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
(11 - a)\times 3 + a \times 4 &= 40 \\\\
33 - 3a + 4a                  &= 40 \\\\
a                             &= 40 - 33 \\\\
a                             &= 7 \\\\
\text{Apple packets}  &= 7 \\\\
\text{Orange packets} &= 11 - a \\\\
                        &= 11 - 7 \\\\
                        &= 4 \\\\
\text{Difference}  &= 7 \times 4 - 4 \times 3 \\\\
                        &= 28 - 12 \\\\
                        &= 16
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$4 \times \boxed{\phantom{1}} + 8 = 44$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

a               &= 9
\end{aligned}

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Jennie and Freddie have each thought of a number.

The difference between their numbers is $8$.

The sum of their numbers is $30$.

What are the two numbers?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Jennie and Freddie have each thought of a number.
<emptyline>
The difference between their numbers is $8$.
<emptyline>
The sum of their numbers is $30$.
<emptyline>
What are the two numbers?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number Jennie thought of $= a$

Let the number Freddie thought of $= b$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
a - b      &= 8 \\\\
a + b      &= 30
\end{aligned}
$

We have got $2$ variables and we have $2$ equations to solve them. Let's eliminate to reduce it to just one variable. 

Let's add above two equation.

$
\begin{aligned}
a - b + a + b   &= 8 + 30 \\\\
2a              &= 38 \\\\
a               &= \dfrac{38}{2} \\\\
a               &= \dfrac{2 \times 19}{2} \\\\
a               &= \dfrac{\cancel 2 \times 19}{\cancel 2} \\\\
a               &= 19 \\\\
\text{Jennie's number}  &= 19 \\\\
\text{Freddie's number} &= 30 - 19 \\\\ 
                                 &= 11
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$19, 11$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Thomasina, Dixie and Harriet are playing a game of marbles.

They start with $20$ marbles each and they play three rounds.

In first round, Dixie wins $4$ marbles from Thomasina and loses $5$ to Harriet.

In the second round, Harriet wins $6$ marbles from Dixie and loses $2$ to Thomasina.

In the third round, Thomasina wins $3$ marbles from Harriet and loses $6$ to Dixie.

How many marbles does each girl have at the end of three round?

TODOTABLE


name       number of marbles
Thomasina
Dixie
Harriet

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Thomasina, Dixie and Harriet are playing a game of marbles.
<emptyline>
They start with $20$ marbles each and they play three rounds.
<emptyline>
In first round, Dixie wins $4$ marbles from Thomasina and loses $5$ to Harriet.
<emptyline>
In the second round, Harriet wins $6$ marbles from Dixie and loses $2$ to Thomasina.
<emptyline>
In the third round, Thomasina wins $3$ marbles from Harriet and loses $6$ to Dixie.
<emptyline>
How many marbles does each girl have at the end of three round?
<emptyline>
%table%
<emptyline>
name       number of marbles
Thomasina
Dixie
Harriet
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number of marbles left with Dixie after first round}       &= 20 + 4 - 5 \\\\
                                                                 &= 19 \\\\
\text{Number of marbles left with Thomasina after first round}   &= 20 - 4 \\\\
                                                                 &= 16 \\\\
\text{Number of marbles left with Harriet after first round}     &= 20 + 5 \\\\
                                                                 &= 25 \\\\
\text{Number of marbles left with Harriet after second round}     &= 25 + 6 - 2 \\\\
                                                                  &= 29 \\\\
\text{Number of marbles left with Dixie after second round}       &= 19 - 6 \\\\
                                                                  &= 13 \\\\
\text{Number of marbles left with Thomasina after second round}   &= 16 + 2 \\\\
                                                                  &= 18 \\\\
\text{Number of marbles left with Thomasina after third round}     &= 18 + 3 - 6 \\\\
                                                                   &= 15 \\\\
\text{Number of marbles left with Harriet after third round}       &= 29 - 3 \\\\
                                                                   &= 26 \\\\
\text{Number of marbles left with Dixie after third round}         &= 13 + 6 \\\\
                                                                   &= 19 
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$15, 26, 19$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Magda and her friends go to the cinema.

They buy $1$ large tub of popcorn, $4$ fizzy drinks, and $10$ packets of crisps.

The bill comes to $\pounds 10.89$

Lena and her friends go to the cinema.

They buy $1$ large tub of popcorn, $3$ fizzy drinks, and $7$ packets of crisps.

The bill comes to $\pounds 8.64$

How much would it cost to buy $1$ large tub of popcorn, $1$ fizzy drink and $1$ packet of crisps?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Magda and her friends go to the cinema.
<emptyline>
They buy $1$ large tub of popcorn, $4$ fizzy drinks, and $10$ packets of crisps.
<emptyline>
The bill comes to $\pounds 10.89$
<emptyline>
Lena and her friends go to the cinema.
<emptyline>
They buy $1$ large tub of popcorn, $3$ fizzy drinks, and $7$ packets of crisps.
<emptyline>
The bill comes to $\pounds 8.64$
<emptyline>
How much would it cost to buy $1$ large tub of popcorn, $1$ fizzy drink and $1$ packet of crisps?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the cost of popcorn $= p$

Let the cost of fizzy drinks $= d$

Let the cost of crisps $= c$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
p + 4d + 10c   &= \pounds 10.89 \\\\
p + 3d + 7c    &= \pounds 9.64 \\\\
\end{aligned}
$

We will use elimination method to find the value of 1 large tub of popcorn, 1 fizzy drink and 1 packet of crisps.

First Subtract second equation from first

$
\begin{aligned}
p + 4d + 10c - (p + 3d + 7c)  &= 10.89 - 8.64 \\\\
p + 4d + 10c - p - 3d - 7c    &= 2.25 \\\\
d + 3c                        &= 2.25 \\\\                     
\end{aligned}
$

Now multiply the above equation by 3 and then subtract it from the first equation.

$
\begin{aligned}
3 \times (d + 3c)        &= 3\times 2.25 \\\\ 
3d + 9c                  &= 6.75 \\\\
p + 4d + 10c - (3d + 9c) &= 10.89 - 6.75 \\\\
p + d + c                &= 4.14
\end{aligned}
$

Cost of 1 large tub of popcorn, 11 fizzy drink and 11 packet of crisps $= 4.14$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$4.14$

</div>
</div>

**Question**

An apple, $2$ oranges and $3$ pears cost $\pounds 2.10$ altogether.
An orange and a pear cost $64 \ \text{pence}$.

How much more does an apple cost than an orange?

<emptyline>
How much more does an apple cost than an orange?
<emptyline>

<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the cost of an apple $= a$

Let the cost of an orange $= b$

Let the cost of a pear $= c$

Convert $\pounds 2.10$ to pence: $\pounds 2.10 = 210 \ \text{p}$

As per the question,

Using this, we get

$
\begin{aligned}
a + 2b + 3c                 &= 210 \\\\
b + c                       &= 64 \\\\
c                           &= 64 - b 
\end{aligned}
$

Let's substitute the value of $c$ in first equation 

$
\begin{aligned}
a + 2b + 3 \times (64 - b)  &= 210 \ \text{p} \\\\
a + 2b + 192 - 3b   &= 210 \\\\
a - b + 192                 &= 210 \\\\
a - b                       &= 210 - 192 \\\\
a - b                       &= 18 \ \text{p}
\end{aligned}
$

Difference in cost $= 18 \ \text{p}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$18 \ \text {pence}$

</div>

**Question**

Mike has $27$ vehicles to service at his garage.

Some are cars ($4$ wheels) and the rest are motorcycles ($2$ wheels).

Altogether, the $27$ vehicles have $78$ wheels.

How many cars does Mike have to service?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Mike has $27$ vehicles to service at his garage.

<emptyline>

</code></pre>

<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number of cars $= c$

Let the number of bikes $= 27 - c$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
c \times 4 + (27 - c) \times 2  &= 78 \\\\
4c + 54 - 2c                  &= 78 \\\\
2c + 54                      &= 78 \\\\
2c                           &= 78 - 54 \\\\
2c                           &= 24 \\\\
c                            &= \dfrac {24} {2} \\\\
c                            &= \dfrac {12 \times 2} {2} \\\\
c                            &= \dfrac {12 \times \cancel {2}} { \cancel 2} \\\\
c                            &= 12
\end{aligned}
$

Number of cars $= 12$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$12$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

$11$ and $12$ are consecutive whole numbers.

Write down two consecutive whole numbers which add up to $75$.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">$11$ and $12$ are consecutive whole numbers.
<emptyline>
Write down two consecutive whole numbers which add up to $75$.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>

</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the first number $=a$

Second number $=a+1$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
a + (a + 1) &=  75 \\\\
2a +1 &=  75 \\\\
2a &= 75 - 1 \\\\
2a &= 74 \\\\
a  &= \dfrac{74}{2} \\\\
a  &= \dfrac{37 \times 2}{2} \\\\
a  &= \dfrac{37 \times \cancel    2}{\cancel 2} \\\\
a  &= 37
\end{aligned}
$

Numbers $= 37$, $38$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$37, 38$

</div>

$88 \div 4 = \boxed{{\phantom{11}}} - 9$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

a - 9                                          &= 22 \\\\
a                                              &= 22 + 9 \\\\
a                                              &= 31
\end{aligned}
$

**Question**

$7^2 =5 1 - (\boxed{{\phantom{11}}} \times 4)$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">$7^2 =5 1 - (\boxed{{\phantom{11}}} \times 4)$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the missing number $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
7 ^ 2            &= 51 - (a \times 4) \\\\
49       &= 51 - 4 a \\\\
4 a              &= 51 - 49 \\\\
4 a              &= 2 \\\\
a                &= \dfrac {2} {4} \\\\
a                &= \dfrac {2} {2 \times 2} \\\\
a                &= \dfrac {\cancel 2} {2 \times \cancel 2} \\\\
a                &= \dfrac {1} {2}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Let the missing number $= a$

7 ^ 2            &= 51 - (a \times 4) \\\\
49       &= 51 - 4 a \\\\
4 a              &= 51 - 49 \\\\
4 a              &= 2 \\\\
a                &= \dfrac {2} {4} \\\\
a                &= \dfrac {2} {2 \times 2} \\\\
a                &= \dfrac {\cancel 2} {2 \times \cancel 2} \\\\

\end{aligned}
$

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A packet of $9$ chocolate cookies costs $\pounds 2.61$

What is the cost of $4$ of these chocolate cookies?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A packet of $9$ chocolate cookies costs $\pounds 2.61$
<emptyline>
What is the cost of $4$ of these chocolate cookies?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Cost of 1 cookie} &= \dfrac{2.61}{9} \\\\
&= \dfrac{9 \times 0.29}{9} \\\\
&= \dfrac{\cancel{9} \times 0.29}{\cancel{9}} \\\\
&= \pounds 0.29 \\\\
\text{Cost of 4 cookies} &= 4 \times 0.29 \\\\
&= \pounds 1.16
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$\pounds 1.16$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Carla bought 2 books from a shop, and paid a total of $\pounds 8.50$

One book cost $60 \ \text{pence}$ more than the other.

What was the price of the cheaper book?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Carla bought 2 books from a shop, and paid a total of $\pounds 8.50$
<emptyline>
One book cost $60 \ \text{pence}$ more than the other.
<emptyline>
What was the price of the cheaper book?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR: It is really important to use the right units in calculations and convert where required.
_no_dot
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the price of the cheaper book $= c$

Price of the other book $= c + 0.60$

As per the question,

$\begin{aligned}
c + (c + 0.60) &= 8.50 \\\\
2c + 0.60 &= 8.50 \\\\
2c &= 8.50 - 0.60 \\\\
2c &= 7.90 \\\\
c &= \dfrac{7.90}{2} \\\\
c &= \dfrac{2 \times 3.95}{2} \\\\
c &= \dfrac{\cancel{2} \times 3.95}{\cancel{2}} \\\\
c &= \pounds 3.95
\end{aligned}$

Price of the cheaper book $= \pounds 3.95$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$\pounds 3.95$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Jane bought a packet of sweets.

A quarter of them were green, a third of them were red and the rest were yellow.

There were $10$ yellow sweets.

What was the total number of sweets in the packet?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Jane bought a packet of sweets.
<emptyline>
A quarter of them were green, a third of them were red and the rest were yellow.
<emptyline>
There were $10$ yellow sweets.
<emptyline>
What was the total number of sweets in the packet?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number of sweets $= a$

Number of green sweets $= \dfrac{a}{4}$

Number of red sweets $= \dfrac{a}{3}$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {a} {4} + \dfrac {a} {3} + 10                                                                        &= a \\\\
a - \dfrac {a} {4} - \dfrac {a} {3}                                                                         &= 10 \\\\
\dfrac {a \times 12} {1 \times 12} - \dfrac {a \times 3} {4 \times 3} - \dfrac {a \times 4} {3 \times 4}    &= 10 \\\\
\dfrac {12a} {12} - \dfrac {3a} {12} - \dfrac {4a} {12}                                                     &= 10 \\\\
\dfrac {12a - 3a - 4a} {12}                                                                                 &= 10 \\\\
\dfrac{5a}{12}                                                                                              &= 10 \\\\
5a                                                                                                          &= 10 \times 12 \\\\
a                                                                                                           &= \dfrac {10 \times 12} {5} \\\\
a                                                                                                           &= \dfrac {5 \times 2 \times 12} {5} \\\\
a                                                                                                           &= \dfrac {\cancel {5} \times 2 \times 12} {\cancel {5}} \\\\
a                                                                                                           &= 24
\end{aligned}
$

Total number of sweets $=24$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$24$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Janet has written down two numbers.

When she subtracts the smaller number from the larger one, the answer is $7$.

When she multiplies the two numbers together, the answer is $60$.

Which two numbers has Janet written down?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

As per the question,

$a \times b = 60$

$a - b = 7$

We can easily infer the values by using trial and error. Let's find out $2$ numbers which meets the following critiera based on the equations above.

- The product of the $2$ numbers is $60$ 
- The difference of the $2$ numbers is $7$.

Factor pairs of $60 = (1, 60), (2, 30), (3, 20), (4, 15), (5, 12), (6, 10)$

Factor pairs of $60$ that have difference of $7 = (5, 12)$

Numbers $= 5, 12$
</div>

a &= 9
\end{aligned}

a &= 10
\end{aligned}
$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Emily bought a sandwich and a muffin from the cafe.

She paid for these with a $\pounds 10$ note, and received $\pounds 4.36$ change.

Given that the sandwich cost $\pounds 3.85$, how much did the muffin cost?

![papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2015/group-1/s01-q13-i00.png](/assets/papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2015/group-1/s01-q13-i00.png "papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2015/group-1/s01-q13-i00.png")

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Emily bought a sandwich and a muffin from the cafe.
<emptyline>
She paid for these with a $\pounds 10$ note, and received $\pounds 4.36$ change.
<emptyline>
Given that the sandwich cost $\pounds 3.85$, how much did the muffin cost?
<emptyline>
%image%
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">

</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the cost of muffin $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\pounds 3.85 + a    &= \pounds 10 - \pounds 4.36 \\\\
a                   &= 5.64 - 3.85 \\\\
a                   &= 1.79
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$1.79$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question_envelope rag_not_found subquestion">
<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

If Hattie has $12$ sweets, how many sweets did Georgia take?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">If Hattie has $12$ sweets, how many sweets did Georgia take?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the total number of sweets in the bag $= a$

Georgia share $= \dfrac{a}{4}$

Remaining sweets $= a - \dfrac{a}{4} = \dfrac{3a}{4}$

Hattie's share $= \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{3a}{4} = \dfrac{3a}{8}$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac{3a}{8} &= 12 \\\\
a &= \dfrac{12 \times 8}{3} \\\\
a &= \dfrac{3 \times 4 \times 8}{3} \\\\
a &= \dfrac{\cancel{3} \times 4 \times 8}{\cancel{3}} \\\\
a &= 32 \\\\
\text{Georgia's share} &= \dfrac{a}{4} \\\\
&= \dfrac{32}{4} \\\\
&= \dfrac{4 \times 8}{4} \\\\
&= \dfrac{\cancel{4} \times 8}{\cancel{4}} \\\\
&= 8
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$8$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Anna's Aquarium has only two types of creature: jupiterian jellyfish and ordinary octopus.

Each jupiterian jellyfish has $25$ tentacles.

Each ordinary octopus has $8$ tentacles.

In Anna's Aquarium, there are $20$ creatures and $279$ tentacles.


How many jupiterian jellyfish are there in the aquarium?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Anna's Aquarium has only two types of creature: jupiterian jellyfish and ordinary octopus.
<emptyline>
Each jupiterian jellyfish has $25$ tentacles.
<emptyline>
Each ordinary octopus has $8$ tentacles.
<emptyline>
In Anna's Aquarium, there are $20$ creatures and $279$ tentacles.
<emptyline>

How many jupiterian jellyfish are there in the aquarium?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">

</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number of jupiterian jellyfish $= j$

So, the number of octopus $= 20 - j$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
25 \times j + 8 \times (20 - j)  &= 279 \\\\
25j + 160 - 8j                   &= 279 \\\\
17j                              &= 279 - 160 \\\\
17j                              &= 119 \\\\
j                                &= \dfrac{119}{17} \\\\
j                                &= \dfrac{17 \times 7}{17} \\\\
j                                &= \dfrac{\cancel {17} \times 7}{\cancel {17}} \\\\
j                                &= 7
\end{aligned}
$

Number of jupiterian jellyfish $= 7$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$7$

</div>
</div>

On planet Dichrome, the symbol  has a special meaning in arithmetic.

$g \ \spadesuit \ h$ means multiply $g$ by $5$, then subtract $2$ times $h$.


For example, 

$
\begin{aligned}
3 \ \spadesuit \ 4 &=  3 \times 5 - 2 \times 4 \\
                   &=  15 - 8 \\
                   &=  7
\end{aligned}
$

**Question**

Work out the value of $k$ so that $k \ \spadesuit \ 3 = 29$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Work out the value of $k$ so that $k \ \spadesuit \ 3 = 29$
</code></pre>

<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
k \ \spadesuit \ 3    &= 29 \\\\
k \times 5 - 2 \times 3    &= 29 \\\\
5k - 6                     &= 29 \\\\
5k                         &= 29 + 6 \\\\
5k                         &= 35 \\\\
k                          &= \dfrac{35}{5} \\\\
k                          &= \dfrac{7 \times 5}{5} \\\\
k                          &= \dfrac{7 \times \cancel 5}{\cancel 5} \\\\
k                          &= 7
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

It is possible to use the symbol twice in a calculation.

For example, 

$
\begin{aligned}
4 \ \spadesuit \ (2 \ \spadesuit \ 1) &= 4 \ \spadesuit \ (2 \times 5 - 2 \times 1) \\
                              &= 4 \ \spadesuit \ 8 \\
                              &= 4 \times 5  2 \times 8 \\
                              &= 4
\end{aligned}
$

Work out $5 \ \spadesuit \ (4 \ \spadesuit \ 3)$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">It is possible to use the symbol twice in a calculation.
<emptyline>
For example, 
<emptyline>
$
\begin{aligned}
4 \ \spadesuit \ (2 \ \spadesuit \ 1) &= 4 \ \spadesuit \ (2 \times 5 - 2 \times 1) \\
                              &= 4 \ \spadesuit \ 8 \\
                              &= 4 \times 5  2 \times 8 \\
                              &= 4
\end{aligned}
$
<emptyline>
Work out $5 \ \spadesuit \ (4 \ \spadesuit \ 3)$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
&= 5 \ \spadesuit \ (4 \ \spadesuit \ 3) \\\\
&= 5 \ \spadesuit \ (5 \times 4 - 2 \times 3) \\\\
&= 5 \ \spadesuit \ (20 - 6) \\\\
&= 5 \ \spadesuit \ 14 \\\\
&= 5 \times 5 - 2 \times 14 \\\\
&= 25 - 28 \\\\
&= - 3
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Work out the value of $t$ so that $(6 \ \spadesuit \ t) \ \spadesuit \ 4 = 12$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Work out the value of $t$ so that $(6 \ \spadesuit \ t) \ \spadesuit \ 4 = 12$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
(6 \ \spadesuit \ t) \ \spadesuit \ 4       &= 12 \\\\
(5 \times 6 - 2 \times t) \ \spadesuit \ 4       &= 12 \\\\
(30 - 2t) \ \spadesuit \ 4                       &= 12 \\\\
5 \times (30 - 2t) - 2 \times 4  &= 12 \\\\
150 - 10t - 8                    &= 12 \\\\
10t &= 150 - 8 - 12 \\\\
10t &= 130 \\\\
t                                &= \dfrac{130}{10} \\\\
t                                &= \dfrac{13 \times 10}{10} \\\\
t                                &= \dfrac{13 \times \cancel {10}}{\cancel {10}} \\\\
t                                &= 13
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$13$

</div>
</div>

**Question**

A third of a certain number is $27$.

What is the number?

\end{aligned}
$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Lara and Cathy have each thought of a positive whole number less than $20$.
The product of their numbers is $56$ and the difference between them is $10$.


What are their two numbers?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</code></pre>

**Working**

Let the number that Lara thought $= a$

Let the number that Cathy thought $= b$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
a - b           &= 10 \\\\
a \times b      &= 56
\end{aligned}
$

We can easily infer the values by using trial and error. Let's find out $2$ numbers which meets the following critiera based on the equations above.

- The product of the $2$ numbers is $56$. 
- The difference of the $2$ numbers is $10$.

Factor pairs of $56 = (1, 56), (2, 28), (4, 14), (7, 8)$

Factor pairs of $56$ that has difference of $10 = (4, 14)$

Numbers $= 4$, $14$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$4, 14$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Belinda ate $\dfrac{3}{5}$ of a bar of chocolate.

$60 \ \text{grams}$ of chocolate remained.

What was the original mass of the chocolate bar?

![papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2015/group-2/s01-q19-i00.png](/assets/papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2015/group-2/s01-q19-i00.png "papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2015/group-2/s01-q19-i00.png")

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Belinda ate $\dfrac{3}{5}$ of a bar of chocolate.
<emptyline>
$60 \ \text{grams}$ of chocolate remained.
<emptyline>
What was the original mass of the chocolate bar?
<emptyline>
%image%
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the original mass of the chocolate bar $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
a - \dfrac {3} {5} \times a &= 60 \\\\
a - \dfrac {3a} {5} &= 60 \\\\
\dfrac {5 a} {5} - \dfrac {3 a} {5}                     &= 60 \\\\
\dfrac {5a - 3a} {5} &= 60 \\\\
\dfrac {2a} {5} &= 60 \\\\
a                                                       &= \dfrac {60 \times 5} {2} \\\\
a                                                       &= \dfrac {2 \times 30 \times 5} {2} \\\\\
a                                                       &= \dfrac {\cancel {2} \times 30 \times 5} {\cancel {2}} \\\\
a                                                       &= 30 \times 5 \\\\
a                                                       &= 150 \ \text {g}
\end{aligned}
$

Original mass $= 150 \ \text{g}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$150 \ \text {g}$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Maddie spent the same amount on pineapples as she did on mangoes.

Given that she bought at least one of each fruit, what is the smallest amount she could have spent?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Maddie spent the same amount on pineapples as she did on mangoes.
<emptyline>
Given that she bought at least one of each fruit, what is the smallest amount she could have spent?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR: It is really important to use the right units in calculations and convert where required.
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number of pineapples $= a$

Let the number of mangoes $= b$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\pounds 1.40 \times a               &= 80 \ \text{p} \times b \\\\
1.40 \times 100 \ \text{p} \times a   &= 80 \ \text{p} \times b \\\\
140 \times a                        &= 80 \times b \\\\
80 \times b                         &= 140 \times a
\end{aligned}
$

We can easily infer the values by using trial and error. Let's find out $2$ numbers which satisfies the above equation.

| Value of $a$  |  Value of $b$   |   $140a$           |    $80b$       |
|:----------:   |:-----------:    |:----------------:  |:------------:  |
| $1$           |     $2$         |        140         |    160         |
| $2$           |     $3$         |        280         |    240         |
| $5$           |     $6$         |        700         |    480         |
| $4$           |     $7$         |        560         |    560         |

A quick check shows that $4$ and $7$ meets all the criteria above.

Number of pineapples $= 4$

Number of mangoes $= 7$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

Pineapples $=$ $4$

</div>
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

Mangoes $=$ $7$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Belinda spends $\pounds 9$ altogether on pineapples and mangoes.

How many mangoes does she buy?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Belinda spends $\pounds 9$ altogether on pineapples and mangoes.
<emptyline>
How many mangoes does she buy?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR: It is really important to use the right units in calculations and convert where required.
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number of pineapples $= a$

Let the number of mangoes $= b$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\pounds 1.40 \times a + 80\ \text{p} \times b                    &= \pounds 9 \\\\
1.40 \times 100\ \text{p} \times a + 80 \ \text{p} \times b       &= 9 \times 100 \ \text{p} \\\\
140a + 80b                                                     &= 900 \\\\
20 (7a + 4b)                                                   &= 900 \\\\
7a + 4b                                                        &= \dfrac{900} {20} \\\\
7a + 4b                                                        &= \dfrac{45 \times 2 \times 10} {2 \times 10} \\\\
7a + 4b                                                        &= \dfrac{45 \times \cancel 2 \times \cancel {10}} {\cancel 2 \times \cancel {10}} \\\\
7a + 4b                                                        &= 45
\end{aligned}
$

We can easily infer the values by using trial and error. Let's find out $2$ numbers which satisfies the above equation.

| Value of $a$  |  Value of $b$   |    $7a +4b$          |
|:---------:    |:--------------: |:------------------:  |
| $2$           |      $4$        |       30             |
| $4$           |      $5$        |       48             |
| $3$           |      $6$        |       45             |

A quick check shows that $3$ and $6$ meets all the criteria above.

Number of mangoes $= 6$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$6$

</div>

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Let the number of pineapples $= a$

Let the number of mangoes $= b$
<emptyline>
As per the question,
<emptyline>
$
\begin{aligned}
\pounds 1.40 \times a + 80\ \text{p} \times b                    &= \pounds 9 \\\\
1.40 \times 100\ \text{p} \times a + 80 \ \text{p} \times b       &= 9 \times 100 \ \text{p} \\\\
140a + 80b                                                     &= 900 \\\\
20 (7a + 4b)                                                   &= 900 \\\\
7a + 4b                                                        &= \dfrac{900} {20} \\\\
7a + 4b                                                        &= \dfrac{45 \times 2 \times 10} {2 \times 10} \\\\
7a + 4b                                                        &= \dfrac{45 \times \cancel 2 \times \cancel {10}} {\cancel 2 \times \cancel {10}} \\\\
7a + 4b                                                        &= 45
\end{aligned}
$
<emptyline>
We can easily infer the values by using trial and error. Let's find out $2$ numbers which satisfies the above equation.
<emptyline>
| Value of $a$  |  Value of $b$   |    $7a +4b$          |

| $2$           |      $4$        |       30             |
| $4$           |      $5$        |       48             |
| $3$           |      $6$        |       45             |
<emptyline>

<emptyline>
Number of mangoes $= 6$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Aisha thinks of a number.

She adds four and then multiplies by $8$.

Her result is $56$.


What was the number Aisha first thought of? 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Aisha thinks of a number.
<emptyline>
She adds four and then multiplies by $8$.
<emptyline>
Her result is $56$.
<emptyline>

What was the number Aisha first thought of? 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
(a + 4) \times 8  &= 56 \\\\
a + 4             &= \dfrac {56} {8} \\\\
a + 4             &= \dfrac {8 \times 7} {8} \\\\
a + 4             &= \dfrac {\cancel {8} \times 7} {\cancel {8}} \\\\
a + 4             &= 7 \\\\
a                 &= 7 - 4 \\\\
a                 &= 3
\end{aligned}
$

Number $= 3$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$3$

</div>
</div>

<div class="formulacodeblock_title">

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">%empty%
</code></pre>

<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Working Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Let the number $= a$
<emptyline>
As per the question,
<emptyline>
$
\begin{aligned}
(a + 4) \times 8  &= 56 \\\\
a + 4             &= \dfrac {56} {8} \\\\
a + 4             &= \dfrac {8 \times 7} {8} \\\\
a + 4             &= \dfrac {\cancel {8} \times 7} {\cancel {8}} \\\\
a + 4             &= 7 \\\\
a                 &= 7 - 4 \\\\
a                 &= 3
\end{aligned}
$
<emptyline>
Number $= 3$
</code></pre>
</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Celia and Autumn have each thought of an integer (whole number) between $0$ and $20$.

The product of their numbers is $72$ and the difference between the numbers is the same as Celia's number.

What is Autumn's number? 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Celia and Autumn have each thought of an integer (whole number) between $0$ and $20$.
<emptyline>
The product of their numbers is $72$ and the difference between the numbers is the same as Celia's number.
<emptyline>
What is Autumn's number? 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let Celia's number $= a$

Let Autumn's number $= b$

As per the question, 

$ a \times b   = 72$

$b - a = a$ 

$b = 2a$

Using this in first equation, 

$
\begin{aligned}
a \times b   &= 72 \\\\
a \times 2a  &= 72 \\\\
2a ^ 2       &= 72 \\\\
a ^ 2        &= \dfrac {72} {2} \\\\
a ^ 2        &= \dfrac {36 \times 2} {2} \\\\
a ^ 2        &= \dfrac {36 \times \cancel {2}} {\cancel {2}} \\\\
a ^ 2        &= 36 \\\\
a            &= \sqrt {36} \\\\
a            &= 6 \\\\
\text{Autumn's number} &= 2a \\\\
&= 2 \times 6 \\\\ 
                       &= 12 
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$12$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Three hedgehogs, Rana, Sarah and Tina, are collecting leaves.

Rana collects twice as many as Sarah.

Sarah collects one and a half times as many as Tina.

Between them they collect $198$ leaves.


How many leaves did each hedgehog collect?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Three hedgehogs, Rana, Sarah and Tina, are collecting leaves.
<emptyline>
Rana collects twice as many as Sarah.
<emptyline>
Sarah collects one and a half times as many as Tina.
<emptyline>
Between them they collect $198$ leaves.
<emptyline>

How many leaves did each hedgehog collect?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number of leaves Tina collects $= t$

Number of leaves Sarah collects $= 1.5t$

Number of leaves Rana collects $= 2 \times 1.5t = 3t$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
t + 1.5t + 3t &= 198 \\\\
5.5t &= 198 \\\\
t &= \dfrac{198}{5.5} \\\\
t &= \dfrac{1980}{55} \\\\
t &= \dfrac{5 \times 11 \times 36}{5 \times 11} \\\\
t &= \dfrac{\cancel{5} \times \cancel{11} \times 36}{\cancel{5} \times \cancel{11}} \\\\
t &= 36 \\\\
\text{Leaves Tina collects} &= 36 \\\\
\text{Leaves Sarah collects} &= 1.5t \\\\
&= 1.5 \times 36 \\\\
&= 54 \\\\
\text{Leaves Rana collects} &= 3t \\\\
&= 3 \times 36 \\\\
&= 108
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$36, 54, 108$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

How many custard creams are there?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">How many custard creams are there?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number of custard creams $= c$

Number of chocolate biscuits $= 8$

Number of ginger biscuits $= 12$

The **other** biscuits correspond to the custard creams and ginger biscuits.

Other biscuits $= c + 12$

As per the question, a third of the other biscuits are custard creams.

$
\begin{aligned}
c &= \dfrac{1}{3} \times (c + 12) \\\\
3c &= c + 12 \\\\
3c - c &= 12 \\\\
2c &= 12 \\\\
c &= \dfrac{12}{2} \\\\
c &= 6
\end{aligned}
$

Number of custard creams $= 6$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$6$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A bird has $2$ legs, a cat has $4$ legs, an insect has $6$ legs and a spider has $8$ legs.

Claire looks at some animals and counts all their legs.

She counts $38$ legs.

There are twice as many birds as spiders and twice as many cats as insects.

How many of each type of animal can she see?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A bird has $2$ legs, a cat has $4$ legs, an insect has $6$ legs and a spider has $8$ legs.
<emptyline>
Claire looks at some animals and counts all their legs.
<emptyline>
She counts $38$ legs.
<emptyline>
There are twice as many birds as spiders and twice as many cats as insects.
<emptyline>
How many of each type of animal can she see?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number of spiders $=a$

Number of birds $=2a$

Let the number of insects $=b$

Number of cats $=2b$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
a \times 8 + 2a \times 2 + b \times 6 + 2b \times 4 &= 38 \\\\
8a + 4a + 6b + 8b                                   &= 38 \\\\
12a + 14b                                           &= 38 \\\\
2 \times (6a + 7b)                                  &= 38 \\\\
(6a + 7b)                                           &= \dfrac{38} {2} \\\\ 
6a + 7b                                             &= \dfrac{19 \times 2} {2} \\\\  
6a + 7b                                             &= \dfrac{19 \times \cancel 2} {\cancel 2} \\\\ 
6a + 7b                                             &= 19     
\end{aligned}
$

We can easily infer the values by using trial and error. Let's find out $2$ numbers which satisfies the equation above.

| Value of $a$  |  Value of $b$   |    $6a + 7b$         |
|:---------:    |:--------------: |:------------------:  |
| $1$           |      $1$        |       $13$           |
| $2$           |      $1$        |       $19$           |

A quick check shows $2$ and $1$ satisfies the above equation.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Number of spiders} &= 2 \\\\
\text {Number of birds}   &= 2 \times 2 \\\\
                          &= 4 \\\\
\text {Number of insects} &= 1 \\\\
\text {Number of cats}    &= 1 \times 2 \\\\
                          &= 2
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$2 ,4 , 1, 2$

</div>
</div>
<div class="workingscodeblock">
<div class="tipcodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="tipcodeblock_title">

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Let the number of spiders $=a$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

In an arithmetic test, $4$ marks were given for each correct answer and a mark was deducted for each wrong answer. Tim got $17$ questions right and $3$ questions wrong. How many marks did he obtain?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">In an arithmetic test, $4$ marks were given for each correct answer and a mark was deducted for each wrong answer. Tim got $17$ questions right and $3$ questions wrong. How many marks did he obtain?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Marks for correct answer} &= 17 \times 4  \\\\
&= 68 \\\\
\text{Marks deducted} &= 3 \times 1 \\\\
&= 3 \\\\
\text{Total marks} &= 68 - 3 \\\\
&= 65
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$65$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Nigel spent $\pounds 71$ on CDs, some costing $\pounds 8$ each, and the rest $\pounds 5$ each. He bought more of the dearer ones. How many CDs did he buy altogether?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Nigel spent $\pounds 71$ on CDs, some costing $\pounds 8$ each, and the rest $\pounds 5$ each. He bought more of the dearer ones. How many CDs did he buy altogether?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the count of the expensive CDs $= d$

Let the count of the cheaper CDs $= c$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
8d + 5c     &= 71 \\\\
d           &> c
\end{aligned}
$

We have got $2$ variables and so we need $2$ equations to solve them. 
Here we have got $2$ equations but the second one is an inequality equation, so we 
can't use elimination or substitution to solve the equations.

This can be solved instead by using trial and error but applying conditions to narrow down options.

We know $d > c$, so let's start with the biggest value possible for $d$.
If $d$ is $9$, that will equate to $8 \times 9 = 72$ and thats more than total spent $71$, so the biggest possible value for $d$ is $8$.

Let's try for $d = 8$.

$
\begin{aligned}
8d + 5c             &= 71 \\\\
8 \times 8 + 5c     &= 71 \\\\
64 + 5c             &= 71 \\\\
5c                  &= 71 - 64 \\\\
5c                  &= 7
\end{aligned}
$

$7$ is not exactly divisible by $5$ and so this value of $d$ is not the solution.

Let's try for $d = 7$.

$
\begin{aligned}
8d + 5c             &= 71 \\\\
8 \times 7 + 5c     &= 71 \\\\
56 + 5c             &= 71 \\\\
5c                  &= 71 - 56 \\\\
5c                  &= 15 \\\\
c                   &= \dfrac{15}{5} \\\\
c                   &= \dfrac{5 \times 3}{5} \\\\
c                   &= \dfrac{\cancel{5} \times 3}{\cancel{5}} \\\\
c                   &= 3
\end{aligned}
$

For $d = 7$, we have a solution where $c = 3$ and it satisfies the inequality $d > c$ too. So we have our solution.

Let's find the total CDs count.

$
\begin{aligned}
c                    &= 3 \\\\
d                    &= 7 \\\\
\text{Total CDs}     &= 7 + 3 \\\\
                     &= 10
\end{aligned}
$

{/*
Bebs explanation

We know that the total of the CDs was $\pounds 71. If we name the number of the more expensive CDs a and the cheaper CDs b, we can form an equation.
8a + 5b = 71
a > b
As the cost of the cheaper CDs are $\pounds 5, however many of these CDs Nigel buys, the cost of them will always be a multiple of 5. This means it will end in 5 or 0.
If $\pounds 71 and the total cost of the expensive CDs Nigel buys, don't subtract to a result which is a multiple of 5, some money would be left over.
This means that we need to find which numbers the cost of the expensive CDs could end with so all the $\pounds 71 is spent.
To get from 71 to a number ending with 0, you could subtract 1.
To get from 71 to a number ending with 5, you could subtract 6.
This means that the total cost of the expensive CDs will either end in the number 6 or 1. We now need to find a multiple of 8 ending in 6 0r 1 which is less than 71.
8 * 1 = 8 (doesn't end in 6 or 1)
8 * 2 = 16 (ends in 6)
8 * 3 = 24 (doesn't end in 6 or 1)
8 * 4 = 32 (doesn't end in 6 or 1)
8 * 5 = 40 (doesn't end in 6 or 1)
8 * 6 = 48 (doesn't end in 6 or 1)
8 * 7 = 56 (ends in 6)
8 * 8 = 64 (doesn't end in 6 or 1)
8 * 9 = 72 (greater than 71)
8 * 10 = 80 (greater than 71)
We have now discovered that there are either 2 or 7 of the more expensive CDs.
If there were 2, the cost of them would be $\pounds 16. This would mean that the cost of the cheaper CDs would be $\pounds 71 - $\pounds 16 which is $\pounds 55. There would be 11 of the cheaper CDs.
However, the questions states that he bought more of the dearer (more expensive) CDs. This means that he bought 7 of the more expensive CDs which would cost $\pounds 56. The cost of the cheaper CDs would be $\pounds 71 - $\pounds 56 which is $\pounds 15. There would be 3 of the cheaper CDs.
We need to find the total number of the CDs which would be 7 + 3 which is 10 CDs.

answer = 10

d = 7
c = 3

Total CDs = 7 + 3

= 10 CDs 
*/}
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

10

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A sum of $90\ \text{pence}$ is made up of equal numbers of $1 \ \text{p}$ coins, $2 \ \text{p}$ coins, $5 \ \text{p}$ coins and $10 \ \text{p}$ coins. How many coins are there in total?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A sum of $90\ \text{pence}$ is made up of equal numbers of $1 \ \text{p}$ coins, $2 \ \text{p}$ coins, $5 \ \text{p}$ coins and $10 \ \text{p}$ coins. How many coins are there in total?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the count of coins of each denomination $= c$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
1 \times c + 2 \times c + 5 \times c + 10 \times c &= 90 \\\\
c + 2c + 5c + 10c                                        &= 90 \\\\
18c                                                      &= 90 \\\\
c                                                        &= \dfrac {90} {18} \\\\
c                                                        &= \dfrac {5 \times 18} { 18} \\\\
c                                                        &= \dfrac {5 \times \cancel{18}} { \cancel{18} } \\\\
c                                                        &= 5 \\\\
\text{Total coins}     &=  5 \times \text{c} \\\\
                       &=  5 \times 4  \\\\
                       &= 20 \ \text{coins}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$20 \ \text{coins}$

</div>
</div>
