<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A bull and three cows costs $\pounds 1300$. Four bulls and eight cows cost $\pounds4000$. What is the cost of a bull?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A bull and three cows costs $\pounds 1300$. Four bulls and eight cows cost $\pounds4000$. What is the cost of a bull?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the cost of a bull $= b$

Let the cost of a cow $= c$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned} 
b + 3c      &= 1300 \\\\
4b + 8c     &= 4000         
\end{aligned}
$

There are two variables, $b$ and $c$. Let's eliminate to reduce it to just one variable. 

Multiply the first equation by $4$ to eliminate $b$.

$
\begin{aligned} 
b + 3c                      &= 1300 \\\\
4 \times b + 4 \times 3c    &= 4 \times 1300 \\\\
4b + 12c                    &= 5200
\end{aligned}
$

Subtract the second equation from the new equation to reduce it to one variable.

$
\begin{aligned}
4b + 12c - (4b + 8c)        &= 5200 - 4000 \\\\
4b + 12c - 4b - 8c          &= 5200 - 4000 \\\\
4c                          &= 1200 \\\\
c                           &= \dfrac{1200}{4} \\\\
c                           &= \dfrac{300 \times 4}{4} \\\\
c                           &= \dfrac{300 \times \cancel 4}{\cancel 4} \\\\
c                           &= \pounds 300
\end{aligned}
$

Cost of a cow $= \pounds 300$ 

Let's substitute the value of $c$ in one of the initial equations to find the cost of a bull.

$
\begin{aligned} 
b + 3c                      &= 1300  \\\\
b + 3 \times 300            &= 1300 \\\\
b + 900                     &= 1300 \\\\
b                           &= 1300 - 900 \\\\
b                           &= \pounds 400
\end{aligned}
$

Cost of a bull $= \pounds 400$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$\pounds 400$

</div>
</div>

&= 28 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

**Question**

If he cuts it into three pieces so that one piece is $10 \ \text{cm}$ longer than the shortest piece and the longest piece is $25 \ \text{cm}$ longer than the shortest piece. What are the three lengths?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">If he cuts it into three pieces so that one piece is $10 \ \text{cm}$ longer than the shortest piece and the longest piece is $25 \ \text{cm}$ longer than the shortest piece. What are the three lengths?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the shortest Length $= a$

Length of the longest piece $= a + 25$

Length of the third piece $= a + 10$

$
\begin{aligned}
(a + 25) + (a + 10) + a     &= 80 \\\\
3a + 35                 &= 80 \\\\
3a                      &= 80 - 35 \\\\
3a                      &= 45 \\\\
a                       &= \dfrac{45}{3} \\\\
a                       &= \dfrac{15 \times 3}{3} \\\\
a                       &= \dfrac{15 \times \cancel 3}{ \cancel 3} \\\\
a                       &= 15 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text{Shortest Length} &= 15 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text{Longest piece}   &= 25 + 15 \\\\
                       &= 40 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text{Third piece}     &= 10 + 15 \\\\ 
                       &= 25 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$15 \ \text{cm}, 40 \ \text{cm}, 25 \ \text{cm}$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question_envelope rag_not_found subquestion">
<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

If there are four pieces, such that one is $\dfrac{1}{5}$ of the stick, one is $\dfrac{3}{10}$, and another $\dfrac{1}{8}$ of the stick, what are the four lengths?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">If there are four pieces, such that one is $\dfrac{1}{5}$ of the stick, one is $\dfrac{3}{10}$, and another $\dfrac{1}{8}$ of the stick, what are the four lengths?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{First stick}      &= \dfrac{1}{5} \times 80 \\\\
                        &= \dfrac{80}{5}  \\\\
                        &= \dfrac{16 \times 5}{5}  \\\\
                        &= \dfrac{16 \times \cancel 5}{\cancel 5} \\\\
                        &= 16 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text{Second stick}     &= \dfrac{3}{10} \times 80\\\\
                        &= \dfrac{3 \times 80}{10} \\\\
                        &= \dfrac{3 \times 8 \cancel{0}}{1 \cancel{0}} \\\\
                        &= 3 \times 8 \\\\
                        &= 24  \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text{Third stick}      &= \dfrac{1}{8} \times 80\\\\
                        &= \dfrac{80}{8} \\\\
                        &= \dfrac{10 \times 8}{8} \\\\
                        &= \dfrac{10 \times \cancel {8}}{\cancel 8} \\\\
                        &= 10 \ \text{cm}\\\\
\text{Fourth stick}     &= 80 - 16 - 24 - 10 \\\\
                        &= 30 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>

**Question**

Claire adds $3$ to her number and then subtracts $11$ from the result. She obtains the answer $7$. What is Claire's number?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Claire adds $3$ to her number and then subtracts $11$ from the result. She obtains the answer $7$. What is Claire's number?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let Claire's number $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
(a + 3) - 11 &= 7 \\\\
a + 3 - 11   &= 7 \\\\
a - 8        &= 7 \\\\
a            &= 7 + 8 \\\\
a            &= 15
\end{aligned}
$

Claire's number $= 15$
</div>
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Alison subtracts $3$ from the product of $4$ and her number. She obtains the answer $17$. What is Alison's number?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Alison subtracts $3$ from the product of $4$ and her number. She obtains the answer $17$. What is Alison's number?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let Alison's number $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
4 \times a - 3 &= 17 \\\\
4a - 3           &= 17 \\\\
4a               &= 17 + 3 \\\\
4a               &= 20 \\\\
a                &= \dfrac {20} {4} \\\\
a                &= \dfrac {4 \times 5} {4} \\\\
a                &= \dfrac {\cancel 4 \times 5} {\cancel 4} \\\\
a                &= 5
\end{aligned}
$

Alison's number $= 5$
</div>

<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Fiona's number is $8$ less than Kath's number. Kath's number is $5$ times as big as Fiona's number. Find the two numbers.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Fiona's number is $8$ less than Kath's number. Kath's number is $5$ times as big as Fiona's number. Find the two numbers.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>

<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let Fiona's number $= f$

Let Kath's number $= k$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
k &= 8 + f \\\\
k &= 5f
\end{aligned}
$

Lets substitute the value of $k$ from the second equation into the first equation.

$
\begin{aligned}
k      &= 8 + f \\\\
5f     &= 8 + f \\\\
5f - f &= 8 \\\\
4f     &= 8 \\\\
f      &= \dfrac {8} {4} \\\\
f      &= \dfrac {4 \times 2} {4} \\\\
f      &= \dfrac {\cancel 4 \times 2} {\cancel 4} \\\\
f      &= 2 \\\\
k      &= 5f \\\\
k      &= 5 \times 2 \\\\
k      &= 10
\end{aligned}
$

Fiona's number $= 2$

Kath's number $= 10$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$2, 10$

</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A baby crocodile grows by $\dfrac{1}{5}$ of its length 
every week. Today it is $30 \ \text{cm}$ long. 
How long was it last week?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A baby crocodile grows by $\dfrac{1}{5}$ of its length 
every week. Today it is $30 \ \text{cm}$ long. 
How long was it last week?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the length of the baby crocodile last week $= a$.

As per the question, 

$
\begin{aligned}
a + \dfrac {a} {5}                      &= 30 \\\\
\dfrac {5a} {5}  + \dfrac {a} {5}       &= 30 \\\\
\dfrac {5a + a} {5}                       &= 30 \\\\
\dfrac {6a} {5}                         &= 30 \\\\
a                                       &= \dfrac {30 \times 5} {6} \\\\
a                                       &= \dfrac {5 \times 6 \times 5} {6} \\\\
a                                       &= \dfrac {5 \times \cancel{6} \times 5} {\cancel{6}} \\\\
a                                       &= 5 \times  5 \\\\
a                                       &= 25 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

Length of the baby crocodile last week $= 25 \ \text{cm}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$25 \ \text{cm}$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

I have some $20\ \text{p}$ pieces. I have twice as 
many $10\ \text{p}$ pieces as $20\ \text{p}$ pieces. I have 
twice as many $5\ \text{p}$ pieces as I 
have $10\ \text{p}$ pieces. I have $\pounds 4.80$ altogether. 
How many coins do I have?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">I have some $20\ \text{p}$ pieces. I have twice as 
many $10\ \text{p}$ pieces as $20\ \text{p}$ pieces. I have 
twice as many $5\ \text{p}$ pieces as I 
have $10\ \text{p}$ pieces. I have $\pounds 4.80$ altogether. 
How many coins do I have?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR: It is really important to use the right units in calculations and convert where required.
_no_dot
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number of $20 \ \text{p}$ pieces $= c$

Number of $10 \ \text{p}$ pieces $= 2c$

Number of $5 \ \text{p}$ pieces $= 2 \times 2c = 4c$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
20\ \text{p} \times c + 10\ \text{p} \times (2c) + 5\ \text{p} \times (4c) &= \pounds 4.80 \\\\
20c + 20c + 20c &= 480 \\\\
60c &= 480 \\\\
c &= \dfrac{480}{60} \\\\
c &= \dfrac{8 \times 60}{60} \\\\
c &= \dfrac{8 \times \cancel{60}}{\cancel{60}} \\\\
c &= 8 \\\\
\text{Total coins} &= c + 2c + 4c \\\\
&= 7c \\\\
&= 7 \times 8 \\\\
&= 56
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$56$ coins

</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Irfan is standing in a queue of $24$ people.

What position is he in the queue if there are $7$ more people ahead of him than behind him?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Irfan is standing in a queue of $24$ people.
<emptyline>
What position is he in the queue if there are $7$ more people ahead of him than behind him?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let Irfan's position in the queue $= p$

Number of people ahead $= p - 1$

Number of people behind $= p - 1 - 7$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
(p - 1) + 1 + (p - 1 - 7)    &= 24 \\\\
2p - 8                     &= 24 \\\\
2p                         &= 24 + 8 \\\\
2p                         &= 32 \\\\
p                          &= \dfrac{32}{2} \\\\
p                          &= \dfrac{16 \times \cancel{2}}{\cancel{2}} \\\\
p                          &= 16
\end{aligned}
$

Irfan's position $= 16$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

<emptyline>
As per the question,

p                          &= \dfrac{16 \times \cancel{2}}{\cancel{2}} \\\\

\end{aligned}
$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Three CDs and two DVDs cost $\pounds 43$. Two CDs and three DVDs cost $\pounds 47$. What is the cost of one CD?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Three CDs and two DVDs cost $\pounds 43$. Two CDs and three DVDs cost $\pounds 47$. What is the cost of one CD?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the cost of one CD $= c$

Let the cost of one DVD $= d$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned} 
3c + 2d &= 43 \\\\
2c + 3d &= 47
\end{aligned}
$

We have got $2$ variables and we have $2$ equations to solve them. Let's eliminate to reduce it to just one variable. 

Multiply the first equation by $3$ and the second equation by $2$ to equate the coefficients of $d$.

$
\begin{aligned} 
3 \times (3c + 2d) &= 3 \times 43 \\\\
9c + 6d &= 129 \\\\
2 \times (2c + 3d) &= 2 \times 47 \\\\
4c + 6d &= 94
\end{aligned}
$

Subtract the second modified equation from the first to reduce it to one variable.

$
\begin{aligned} 
(9c + 6d) - (4c + 6d) &= 129 - 94 \\\\
9c + 6d - 4c - 6d &= 35 \\\\
5c &= 35 \\\\
c &= \dfrac {35} {5} \\\\
c &= \dfrac {5 \times 7} {5} \\\\
c &= \dfrac {\cancel 5 \times 7} {\cancel 5} \\\\
c &= \pounds 7
\end{aligned}
$

Cost of one CD $= \pounds 7$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$\pounds 7$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Ger has $\pounds 2$ made up of $20\ \text{p}$ and $10\ \text{p}$ coins. He has twice as many $20\ \text{p}$ coins as $10\ \text{p}$ ones. How many $10\ \text{p}$ coins does he have?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Ger has $\pounds 2$ made up of $20\ \text{p}$ and $10\ \text{p}$ coins. He has twice as many $20\ \text{p}$ coins as $10\ \text{p}$ ones. How many $10\ \text{p}$ coins does he have?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR: It is really important to use the right units in calculations and convert where required.
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number of $10 \ \text{p}$ coins $= c$

Number of $20 \ \text{p}$ coins $= 2c$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
10\ \text{p} \times c + 20\ \text{p} \times 2c &= \pounds 2 \\\\
10c + 40c &= 200 \\\\
50c &= 200 \\\\
c &= \dfrac{200}{50} \\\\
c &= \dfrac{4 \times 50}{50} \\\\
c &= \dfrac{4 \times \cancel{50}}{\cancel{50}} \\\\
c &= 4
\end{aligned}
$

Number of $10 \ \text{p}$ coins $= 4$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$4$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Alison has $8$ more pencils than rulers. If she has a total of $52$ pencils and rulers, how many rulers does she have?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Alison has $8$ more pencils than rulers. If she has a total of $52$ pencils and rulers, how many rulers does she have?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the count of rulers $= r$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned} 
r + (r + 8)                                &= 52 \\\\
2r + 8                                     &= 52 \\\\
2r                                         &= 52 - 8 \\\\
2r                                         &= 44 \\\\
r                                          &= \dfrac {44}{2} \\\\
r                                          &= \dfrac {2 \times 22}{2} \\\\
r                                          &= \dfrac {\cancel {2} \times 22}{\cancel {2}} \\\\
r                                          &= 22
\end{aligned}
$

Number of rulers $= 22$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$22$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Jo writes down a two digit number. When she reverses the digits and subtracts the smaller 
number from the larger number the answer she gets is $36$. What is the difference between the 
two digits in her original number?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Jo writes down a two digit number. When she reverses the digits and subtracts the smaller 
number from the larger number the answer she gets is $36$. What is the difference between the 
two digits in her original number?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the tens digit for the number $= a$

Let the unit digit for the number $= b$

Value of the original number $= 10a + b$

When the digits are reversed, the value of the reversed number $= 10b + a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
(10a + b)- (10b + a)    &= 36 \\\\
10a + b- 10b - a        &= 36 \\\\
9a -9b                  &= 36 \\\\
9 (a - b)               &= 36 \\\\
a - b                   &= \dfrac {36}{9} \\\\
a - b                   &= 4
\end{aligned}
$

Difference between the digits $= 4$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$4$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A festival in Platt Fields attracted a huge crowd and all the people attending brought food with them to share out. Some people brought bread with them, others brought fish while the remainder brought fruit in the form of apples.

Everyone agreed that they would share their food with each other according to the following rules.

\begin{aligned}
\text{Number of loaves Irfan get}         &= 3 \ \text{fish} + 12 \ \text{apples} \\\\

                                          &= 6 + 4 \\\\
                                          &= 10 \ \text{loaves}
\end{aligned}
$

**Question**

Aidan wanted four fish to go with each loaf, how many loaves and fish could he exchange for $54$ apples?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Aidan wanted four fish to go with each loaf, how many loaves and fish could he exchange for $54$ apples?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number of loaves be $= a$

Number of fish $= 4a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
a \times 3 + 4a \times 2 \times 3         &= 54 \\\\
3a + 24a                                  &= 54 \\\\
27a                                       &= 54 \\\\
a                                         &= \dfrac {54} {27} \\\\
a                                         &= \dfrac {27 \times 2} {27} \\\\
a                                         &= \dfrac {\cancel {27} \times 2} {\cancel {27}} \\\\
a                                         &= 2
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number of loaves}          &= 2 \\\\
\text{Number of fish}            &= 2 \times 4 \\\\
                                 &= 8
\end{aligned}
$

$2 \ \text{loaves}, 8 \ \text{fish}$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Neil thinks of a number, he halves it and then subtracts $9$.  If the answer he gets is $12$, what was the original number he thought of?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</code></pre>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Two shirts and three tops cost $\pounds 29$. Three shirts and one top cost $\pounds 19$. What is the cost of a top?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Two shirts and three tops cost $\pounds 29$. Three shirts and one top cost $\pounds 19$. What is the cost of a top?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the cost of a shirt $= s$

Let the cost of a top $= t$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned} 
2s + 3t &= 29 \\\\
3s + t &= 19
\end{aligned}
$

We have got $2$ variables and we have $2$ equations to solve them. Let's eliminate to reduce it to just one variable.

Multiply the first equation by $3$ and the second equation by $2$.

$
\begin{aligned} 
3 \times (2s + 3t) &= 3 \times 29 \\\\
2 \times (3s + t) &= 2 \times 19 \\\\
6s + 9t &= 87 \\\\
6s + 2t &= 38
\end{aligned}
$

Subtract the second modified equation from the first modified equation to reduce it to one variable.

$
\begin{aligned} 
(6s + 9t) - (6s + 2t) &= 87 - 38 \\\\
6s + 9t - 6s - 2t &= 49 \\\\
7t &= 49 \\\\
t &= \dfrac{49}{7} \\\\
t &= \dfrac{7 \times 7}{7} \\\\
t &= \dfrac{\cancel 7 \times 7}{\cancel 7} \\\\
t &= \pounds 7
\end{aligned}
$

Cost of a top $= \pounds 7$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$\pounds 7$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

When I emptied my pockets recently I found I had a mixture of $10\ \text{p}$, $20\ \text{p}$, $50\ \text{p}$ and $\pounds 1$ coins. 
When I counted the value of all the coins, the total amount came to $\pounds 7.20$ and there were equal numbers of each coin. 

How many coins were there altogether?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">When I emptied my pockets recently I found I had a mixture of $10\ \text{p}$, $20\ \text{p}$, $50\ \text{p}$ and $\pounds 1$ coins. 
When I counted the value of all the coins, the total amount came to $\pounds 7.20$ and there were equal numbers of each coin. 
<emptyline>
How many coins were there altogether?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR: It is really important to use the right units in calculations and convert where required.
_no_dot
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the count of coins of each denomination $= c$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
10 \ \text{p} \times c + 20\ \text{p} \times c + 50\ \text{p} \times c + 100\ \text{p} \times c   &= \pounds 7.20 \\\\
10 \ \text{p} \times c + 20\ \text{p} \times c + 50\ \text{p} \times c + 100\ \text{p} \times c   &= 720 \ \text{p} \\\\
10c + 20c + 50c + 100c                                                                    &= 720 \\\\
180c                                                                                      &= 720 \\\\
c                                                                                         &= \dfrac {720} { 180} \\\\
c                                                                                         &= \dfrac {180 \times 4} { 180} \\\\
c                                                                                         &= \dfrac {\cancel{180} \times 4} { \cancel{180}} \\\\
c                                                                                         &= 4 \\\\
\text{Total coins} &= 4c \\\\
&= 4 \times 4 \\\\
&= 16
\end{aligned}
$ 
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$16$

</div>
</div>

<div class="formulacodeblock_title">

180c                                                                                      &= 720 \\\\

c                                                                                         &= \dfrac {180 \times 4} { 180} \\\\
c                                                                                         &= \dfrac {\cancel{180} \times 4} { \cancel{180}} \\\\
c                                                                                         &= 4 \\\\

One of the ways to check if a number is divisible by $11$ is by alternately subtracting and adding its digits as follows.

Consider the digits in $121$. Since $1 - 2 + 1 = 0$ we can say that $121$ is divisible by $11$. 

For the number $16918$, the digits combine as $1 - 6 + 9 - 1 + 8 = 11$, which is a multiple of $11$ so $16918$ is divisible by $11$.

**Question**

In the number $74\text{n}130$ what value does the digit $\text{n}$ have to be, if the number is divisible by $11?$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">In the number $74\text{n}130$ what value does the digit $\text{n}$ have to be, if the number is divisible by $11?$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Alternating sum} &= 7 - 4 + n - 1 + 3 - 0 \\\\
&= n + 5
\end{aligned}
$

Since $n$ is a single digit ($0-9$), the value $n + 5$ can range from $5$ to $14$. The only multiple of $11$ in this range is $11$.

Using that,

$
\begin{aligned}
n + 5 &= 11 \\\\
n &= 11 - 5 \\\\
n &= 6
\end{aligned}
$

$n = 6$
</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

In the number $83\text{a}4b9$, the digit $\text{b}$ is three times digit $\text{a}$. Find values for $\text{a}$ and $\text{b}$ if the number is divisible by $11$.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">In the number $83\text{a}4b9$, the digit $\text{b}$ is three times digit $\text{a}$. Find values for $\text{a}$ and $\text{b}$ if the number is divisible by $11$.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the question, for $83\text{a}4b9$ to be divisible by $11$:

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Alternating sum} &= 8 - 3 + a - 4 + b - 9 \\\\
&= 5 + a - 4 + 3a - 9 \\\\
&= 4a - 8
\end{aligned}
$

For the number to be divisible by $11$, $4a - 8$ must be a multiple of $11$.

We can easily infer the values by using trial and error. Let's tabulate the values:

|  $a$ |      $4a - 8$      | Multiple of $11$? |
|:------------:|:-------------------:|:------------------:|
| $0$          | $4 \times 0 - 8 = -8$     | No                |
| $1$          | $4 \times 1 - 8 = -4$     | No                |
| $2$          | $4 \times 2 - 8 = 0$      | Yes            |
| $3$          | $4 \times 3 - 8 = 4$      | No                |
| $4$          | $4 \times 4 - 8 = 8$      | No                |
| $5$          | $4 \times 5 - 8 = 12$     | No                |
| $6$          | $4 \times 6 - 8 = 16$     | No                |
| $7$          | $4 \times 7 - 8 = 20$     | No                |
| $8$          | $4 \times 8 - 8 = 24$     | No                |
| $9$          | $4 \times 9 - 8 = 28$     | No                |

A quick check shows $a = 2$ meets the criteria above.

Lets use the value of $a$ to find $b$.

$
\begin{aligned}
b   &= 3a \\\\
b   &= 3 \times 2 \\\\
b   &= 6
\end{aligned}
$

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">As per the question, for $83\text{a}4b9$ to be divisible by $11$:
<emptyline>
$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Alternating sum} &= 8 - 3 + a - 4 + b - 9 \\\\
&= 5 + a - 4 + 3a - 9 \\\\
&= 4a - 8
\end{aligned}
$
<emptyline>
For the number to be divisible by $11$, $4a - 8$ must be a multiple of $11$.
<emptyline>
We can easily infer the values by using trial and error. Let's tabulate the values:
<emptyline>
|  $a$ |      $4a - 8$      | Multiple of $11$? |
|:------------:|:-------------------:|:------------------:|
| $0$          | $4 \times 0 - 8 = -8$     | No                |
| $1$          | $4 \times 1 - 8 = -4$     | No                |
| $2$          | $4 \times 2 - 8 = 0$      | Yes            |
| $3$          | $4 \times 3 - 8 = 4$      | No                |
| $4$          | $4 \times 4 - 8 = 8$      | No                |
| $5$          | $4 \times 5 - 8 = 12$     | No                |
| $6$          | $4 \times 6 - 8 = 16$     | No                |
| $7$          | $4 \times 7 - 8 = 20$     | No                |
| $8$          | $4 \times 8 - 8 = 24$     | No                |
| $9$          | $4 \times 9 - 8 = 28$     | No                |
<emptyline>
A quick check shows $a = 2$ meets the criteria above.
<emptyline>
Lets use the value of $a$ to find $b$.
<emptyline>
$
\begin{aligned}
b   &= 3a \\\\
b   &= 3 \times 2 \\\\
b   &= 6
\end{aligned}
$
</code></pre>
</div>

If $n \ (.)\ 4 = 8\ (.)\ n$, what number must $n$ be?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">If $n \ (.)\ 4 = 8\ (.)\ n$, what number must $n$ be?
</code></pre>

<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
n\ (.)\ 4        &= 8\ (.)\ n \\\\
5 \times n + 4   &= 5 \times 8 + n \\\\

5n - n           &= 40 - 4 \\\\

n                &= \dfrac{36} {9} \\\\
n                &= \dfrac{9 \times 4} {9} \\\\
n                &= \dfrac{\cancel 9 \times 4} {\cancel 9} \\\\
n                &= 9 
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$n = 9$

**Question**

For football at Rovers ground an adult ticket costs $\pounds 15$ and a child's ticket costs $\pounds 4$. Find the total cost for $20$ adults and $12$ children.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</div>

</code></pre>
</div>

<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

                    &= (20 \times 15) + (12 \times 4) \\\\
                    &= 300 + 48 \\\\
                    &= \pounds 348
\end{aligned}
$

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

For a rugby match, $30$ adults and $16$ children paid $\pounds 408$ to see the game. A child's ticket cost $\pounds 3$. Work out the cost of one adult ticket.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">For a rugby match, $30$ adults and $16$ children paid $\pounds 408$ to see the game. A child's ticket cost $\pounds 3$. Work out the cost of one adult ticket.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the cost of adult ticket $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
30 \times a + 16 \times 3  &= 408 \\\\
30a + 48                   &= 408 \\\\
30a                        &= 408 - 48 \\\\
30a                        &= 360 \\\\
a                          &= \dfrac {360} {30} \\\\
a                          &= \dfrac {12 \times 30} {30} \\\\
a                          &= \dfrac {12 \times \cancel {30}}{\cancel {30}} \\\\
a                          &= \pounds 12
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$\pounds 12$

</div>
</div>

</code></pre>

**Question**

At the swimming tournament a child's ticket cost $\pounds 6$ less than an adult ticket. 
The total cost of the tickets for $25$ adults and $30$ children was $\pounds 370$. Work out the cost of one child ticket.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">At the swimming tournament a child's ticket cost $\pounds 6$ less than an adult ticket. 
The total cost of the tickets for $25$ adults and $30$ children was $\pounds 370$. Work out the cost of one child ticket.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the cost of a adult ticket $= a$

Cost of a child ticket $= a - 6$

As per question,

$
\begin{aligned}
25 \times a + 30 \times (a - 6) &= 370 \\\\
25a + 30a - 180                 &= 370 \\\\
55a - 180                       &= 370 \\\\
55a                             &= 370 + 180 \\\\
55a                             &= 550 \\\\
a                               &= \dfrac {550} {55} \\\\
a                               &= \dfrac {55 \times 10} {55} \\\\
a                               &= \dfrac {\cancel {55} \times 10} {\cancel {55}} \\\\
a                               &= \pounds 10
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Cost of a child ticket} &= a - 6 \\\\
                               &= 10 - 6 \\\\
                               &= \pounds 4
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$\pounds 4$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A cow eats $8  \ \text{kg}$ of food per day and a pig eats $6  \ \text{kg}$ of 
food per day. A farmer has $30$ cows and some pigs.  If the animals 
eat a total of $360  \ \text{kg}$ of food each day, work out how 
many pigs the farmer has.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A cow eats $8  \ \text{kg}$ of food per day and a pig eats $6  \ \text{kg}$ of 
food per day. A farmer has $30$ cows and some pigs.  If the animals 
eat a total of $360  \ \text{kg}$ of food each day, work out how 
many pigs the farmer has.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number of pigs $= p$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned} 
30 \times 8 + p \times 6    &= 360 \\\\
240 + 6p                    &= 360 \\\\
6p                          &= 360 - 240 \\\\
6p                          &= 120 \\\\
p                           &= \dfrac {120} {6} \\\\
p                           &= \dfrac {20 \times 6} {6} \\\\
p                           &= \dfrac {20 \times \cancel{6}} {\cancel{6}} \\\\
p                           &= 20
\end{aligned}
$

Number of pigs $= 20$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$20$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

David cuts a $6  \ \text{metre}$ long pole into three different 
pieces.  The largest piece is $40 \ \text{cm}$ longer than the middle piece 
and the middle piece is $70 \ \text{cm}$ longer than the shortest piece.

What is the size of the largest piece?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">David cuts a $6  \ \text{metre}$ long pole into three different 
pieces.  The largest piece is $40 \ \text{cm}$ longer than the middle piece 
and the middle piece is $70 \ \text{cm}$ longer than the shortest piece.
<emptyline>
What is the size of the largest piece?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR: It is really important to use the right units in calculations and convert where required.
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the shortest piece $= a$

Middle piece $= a + 70$

Largest piece $= a + 70 + 40$

Total length of the pole $= 6 \ \text{m} = 600 \ \text{cm}$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned} 
a + (a + 70) + (a + 70 + 40)    &= 600 \\\\
3a + 180                        &= 600 \\\\
3a                              &= 600 - 180\\\\
3a                              &= 420 \\\\
a                              &= \dfrac {420} {3} \\\\
a                               &= \dfrac {140 \times 3} {3} \\\\
a                               &= \dfrac {140 \times \cancel{3}} {\cancel{3}} \\\\
a                               &= 140 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text{Largest piece}   &= a + 70 + 40 \\\\
                       &= 140 + 70 + 40 \\\\
                       &= 250  \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

Largest piece $=$ $250  \ \text{cm}$

</div>
</div>
<div class="workingscodeblock">

</code></pre>
</div>

<div class="formulacodeblock_title">

</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">%empty%
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workingcodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="workingcodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Working Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Let the shortest piece $= a$
<emptyline>
Middle piece $= a + 70$
<emptyline>
Largest piece $= a + 70 + 40$
<emptyline>

<emptyline>

$

3a                              &= 600 - 180\\\\
3a                              &= 420 \\\\

a                               &= \dfrac {140 \times 3} {3} \\\\
a                               &= \dfrac {140 \times \cancel{3}} {\cancel{3}} \\\\
a                               &= 140 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text{Largest piece}   &= a + 70 + 40 \\\\
                       &= 140 + 70 + 40 \\\\
                       &= 250  \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$
</code></pre>
</div>
</div>

</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Largest piece</code></pre>

<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Answer Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">$250  \ \text{cm}$
</code></pre>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Two bags of crisps and five chocolate biscuits cost $\pounds 1.76$. If 
each bag of crisps costs  $4 \text{p}$ more than a chocolate 
biscuit, what is the cost of a biscuit?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Two bags of crisps and five chocolate biscuits cost $\pounds 1.76$. If 
each bag of crisps costs  $4 \text{p}$ more than a chocolate 
biscuit, what is the cost of a biscuit?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR: It is really important to use the right units in calculations and convert where required.
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the cost of a chocolate biscuit $= b$

Cost of a bag of crisps (in pence) $= b + 4$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned} 
2 \times (b + 4) + 5 \times b   &= \pounds 1.76  \\\\
2 \times (b + 4) + 5 \times a   &= 176 \ \text{p}  \\\\
2b + 8 + 5a                     &= 176  \\\\
7b                              &= 176 - 8  \\\\
7b                              &= 168  \\\\
b                               &= \dfrac {168}{7}  \\\\
b                               &= \dfrac {24 \times 7}{7}  \\\\
b                               &= \dfrac {24 \times \cancel{7}}{\cancel{7}}  \\\\
b                               &= 24 \ \text{p}
\end{aligned}
$

Cost of a chocolate biscuit $=24 \ \text{p}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$24 \ \text{p}$

</div>
</div>
<div class="workingscodeblock">
<div class="tipcodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="tipcodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Tips Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">- rtq_abbr_note_md_unit
</code></pre>
</div>

<div class="formulacodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Formulas Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">%empty%
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workingcodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="workingcodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Working Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Let the cost of a chocolate biscuit $= b$
<emptyline>
Cost of a bag of crisps (in pence) $= b + 4$
<emptyline>
As per the question,
<emptyline>
$
\begin{aligned} 
2 \times (b + 4) + 5 \times b   &= \pounds 1.76  \\\\
2 \times (b + 4) + 5 \times a   &= 176 \ \text{p}  \\\\
2b + 8 + 5a                     &= 176  \\\\
7b                              &= 176 - 8  \\\\
7b                              &= 168  \\\\
b                               &= \dfrac {168}{7}  \\\\
b                               &= \dfrac {24 \times 7}{7}  \\\\
b                               &= \dfrac {24 \times \cancel{7}}{\cancel{7}}  \\\\
b                               &= 24 \ \text{p}
\end{aligned}
$
<emptyline>
Cost of a chocolate biscuit $=24 \ \text{p}$
</code></pre>
</div>
</div>

<div class="answercodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>

<div class="answercodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Answer Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">$24 \ \text{p}$
</code></pre>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

The **BACT** of two numbers is found by adding together the common factors of the two
numbers. So to find the **BACT** of $20$ and $30$ which is written as $B(20,30)$ we would work out:

Factors of $20$ are $\bold {\underline{1, 2}}, 4, \bold {\underline{5, 10}}, 20$

and Factors of $30$ are $\bold {\underline{1, 2}}, 3, \bold {\underline{5}}, 6, \bold {\underline{10}}, 15, 30$

the Common Factors, underlined in bold are $\bold {\underline{1, 2, 5, 10}}$

and then the **BACT** of $20$ and $30$ is $B(20,30) = 1 + 2 + 5 + 10 = 18$

Using this method:

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">The **BACT** of two numbers is found by adding together the common factors of the two
numbers. So to find the **BACT** of $20$ and $30$ which is written as $B(20,30)$ we would work out:
<emptyline>
Factors of $20$ are $\bold {\underline{1, 2}}, 4, \bold {\underline{5, 10}}, 20$
<emptyline>
and Factors of $30$ are $\bold {\underline{1, 2}}, 3, \bold {\underline{5}}, 6, \bold {\underline{10}}, 15, 30$
<emptyline>
the Common Factors, underlined in bold are $\bold {\underline{1, 2, 5, 10}}$
<emptyline>
and then the **BACT** of $20$ and $30$ is $B(20,30) = 1 + 2 + 5 + 10 = 18$
<emptyline>
Using this method:
</code></pre>

**Question**

David unfortunately scored zero. Give **TWO** ways in which this could have happened, **other than** him leaving **all** the answer spaces blank.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">David unfortunately scored zero. Give **TWO** ways in which this could have happened, **other than** him leaving **all** the answer spaces blank.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">

</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number of questions David got right $= a$

Let the number of questions David got wrong $= b$

Number of questions David left blank $= 20 - a - b$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
a \times 5 - (20 - a) \times 3 &= 0 \\\\
5a - 60 + 3b                   &= 0 \\\\
5a + 3b                        &= 60
\end{aligned}
$

We can easily infer the values by using trial and error. Let's find out $2$ numbers which can satisfy the equations above.

| Value of a   |   Value of b      |     5a + 3b    |   
|:------------:|:-----------------:|:--------------:|
|     $1$      |         $2$       |       $11$     | 
|     $2$      |         $5$       |       $25$     |         
|     $3$      |         $15$      |       $60$     |         
|     $6$      |         $10$      |       $60$     |        

Hence, the $2$ cases in which score $0$ is possible are -

- David gets $3$ right $15$ wrong and $2$ left blank spaces

- David gets $6$ right $10$ wrong and $4$ left blank spaces
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$3, 15, 2$

</div>
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$6, 10, 4$

</div>

**Question**

Eve got twice as many right as she got wrong and scored $35$. How many answer spaces did she leave blank?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Eve got twice as many right as she got wrong and scored $35$. How many answer spaces did she leave blank?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number of questions Eve got wrong $= a$

Number of questions Eve got right $= 2a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
2a \times 5 - a \times 3 &= 35 \\\\
10a - 3a                 &= 35 \\\\
7a                       &= 35 \\\\
a                        &= \dfrac {35} {7} \\\\
a                        &= \dfrac {5 \times 7} {7} \\\\
a                        &= \dfrac {5 \times \cancel 7} {\cancel 7} \\\\
a                        &= 5
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Number of questions Eve got wrong}     &= 5 \\\\
\text {Number of questions Eve got right}     &= 5 \times 2 \\\\
                                              &= 10 \\\\
\text {Number of questions Eve left as blank} &= 20 - 5 - 10 \\\\ 
                                              &= 5                                        
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$5$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A shop reduces its prices by $20 \%$ in a sale. David bought a coat for $\pounds 40$ in the sale. How much would the coat have cost him **before** the sale?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A shop reduces its prices by $20 \%$ in a sale. David bought a coat for $\pounds 40$ in the sale. How much would the coat have cost him **before** the sale?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the original cost of the coat $= c$

If the price is reduced by $20 \%$, then the sale price would be $100 - 20 = 80 \%$ of the original price.

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
80 \% \text{ of } c               &= 40 \\\\
\dfrac {80 } { 100 } \times c     &= 40 \\\\
c                                 &= \dfrac {40 \times 100} { 80 } \\\\
c                                 &= \dfrac {40 \times 2 \times 50} { 40 \times 2 } \\\\
c                                 &= \dfrac {\cancel{40} \times \cancel{2} \times 50} { \cancel{40} \times \cancel{2} } \\\\
c                                 &= \pounds 50 
\end{aligned}
$

Original price $= \pounds 50$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$\pounds 50$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Rachel buys three identical bags of sweets and five cans of drink, the total cost of these items came to $\pounds 4.90$. 
Rosie buys just one bag of sweets and three cans of drink and pays $\pounds 2.70$.

What is the cost of a bag of sweets?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Rachel buys three identical bags of sweets and five cans of drink, the total cost of these items came to $\pounds 4.90$. 
Rosie buys just one bag of sweets and three cans of drink and pays $\pounds 2.70$.
<emptyline>
What is the cost of a bag of sweets?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the cost of a bag of sweets $= s$

Let the cost of a can of drink $= d$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
3s + 5d &= 4.90 \\\\
s + 3d &= 2.70
\end{aligned}
$

We have got $2$ variables and we have $2$ equations to solve them. Let's eliminate to reduce it to just one variable. 

Multiply the second equation by $3$.

$
\begin{aligned}
3 \times s + 3 \times 3d   &= 3 \times 2.70 \\\\
3s + 9d &= 8.10
\end{aligned}
$

Subtract the first equation from this new equation.

$
\begin{aligned}
(3s + 9d) - (3s + 5d) &= 8.10 - 4.90 \\\\
4d &= 3.20 \\\\
d &= \dfrac{3.20}{4} \\\\
d &= \pounds 0.80
\end{aligned}
$

Substitute the value of $d$ in the second equation.

$
\begin{aligned}
s + 3 \times 0.80 &= 2.70 \\\\
s + 2.40 &= 2.70 \\\\
s &= 2.70 - 2.40 \\\\
s &= \pounds 0.30 \\\\
s &= 30\ \text{p}
\end{aligned}
$

Cost of a bag of sweets $= 30\ \text{p}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$30\ \text{p}$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A plant is growing at a steady rate of $0.2 \ \text{cms}$ every day. At midday on January $19 ^\text{th}$ the plant was $6 \ \text{cms}$ high.  What will the date be when it reaches a height of $11 \ \text{cm}?$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A plant is growing at a steady rate of $0.2 \ \text{cms}$ every day. At midday on January $19 ^\text{th}$ the plant was $6 \ \text{cms}$ high.  What will the date be when it reaches a height of $11 \ \text{cm}?$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number of days $= d$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned} 
6 + 0.2 \times d    &= 11 \\\\
0.2d                &= 11 - 6 \\\\
0.2d                &= 5 \\\\
d                   &= \dfrac {5} {0.2} \\\\
d                   &= \dfrac {5 \times 10} {0.2 \times 10} \\\\
d                   &= \dfrac {50} {2} \\\\
d                   &= 25 \ \text{days}
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned} 
\text{Date}          &= \text{January } 19  + 25 \ \text{days} \\\\
                                            &= \text{February } 13
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$\text{February } 13$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Howard discovers a method to find the heights of buildings. He measures the distance to the foot of the building, $d \ \text{metres}$. 
Then he measures the angle to the horizontal when he looks up at the top of the building, as shown in the diagram.

![papers/the-manchester-grammar-school/2016/arithmetic-b/s01-q06-i00.png](/assets/papers/the-manchester-grammar-school/2016/arithmetic-b/s01-q06-i00.png "papers/the-manchester-grammar-school/2016/arithmetic-b/s01-q06-i00.png")

Using that angle, he then finds the quantity called the **tannangle** from the table below:

| $\text{Angle} \degree$ | $10$  | $20$  | $30$  | $40$  | $50$  | $60$  | $70$  | $80$  |
|------------------------|-------|-------|-------|-------|-------|-------|-------|-------|
| $\text{Tannangle}$     | $0.2$ | $0.4$ | $0.6$ | $0.8$ | $1.2$ | $1.7$ | $2.7$ | $5.7$ |

The height of the building, $h \ \text{metres}$, is given by the following calculation:

$h = d \times \text{tannangle}$

e.g. if the building is $50 \ \text{m}$ away and the angle is $30\degree$ then the height is given by:

$h = 50 \times 0.6 = 30 \ \text{m}$

</div>

**Question**

Find the distance to a building $24 \ \text{m}$ high when the angle is $40\degree$.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Find the distance to a building $24 \ \text{m}$ high when the angle is $40\degree$.
</code></pre>

<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

Using the value of tannangle from the table,

$
\begin{aligned}
24 &= d \times \tan 40 \degree \\\\
24 &= d \times 0.8 \\\\
d &= \dfrac{24}{0.8} \\\\
d &= \dfrac{240}{8} \\\\
d &= \dfrac{8 \times 30}{8} \\\\
d &= \dfrac{\cancel{8} \times 30}{\cancel{8}} \\\\
d &= 30 \ \text{m}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

d &= 30 \ \text{m}
\end{aligned}
$

The method for working out the Rec of two numbers is as follows

$\text{Rec} (a,b) = \dfrac{a + b}{a \times b}$

so

$\text{Rec} (2,3) = \dfrac{2 + 3}{2 \times 3} = \dfrac{5}{6}$ 

and where possible, the fraction answer is simplified

so

$\text{Rec} (2,4) = \dfrac{2 + 4}{2 \times 4} = \dfrac{6}{8} = \dfrac{3}{4}$

\end{aligned}

**Question**

If $\text{Rec} (a,a) = 1$, find the value of $a$.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">If $\text{Rec} (a,a) = 1$, find the value of $a$.
</code></pre>

<div class="workings">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Rec} (a,a)                         &= 1 \\\\
\dfrac {a + a} {a \times a}                         &= 1 \\\\
\dfrac {2a} {a \times a}                            &= 1 \\\\ 
\dfrac {2 \times a} {a \times a}                    &= 1\\\\ 
\dfrac {2 \times \cancel a} {\cancel a \times a}    &= 1 \\\\ 
\dfrac {2} {a}                                      &= 1 \\\\
a                                                   &= 2
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$2$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Aidan was told to divide a certain number by $17$. Instead he divided the number by $7$ and got the answer $68$. What was the answer to the division he was supposed to do?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Aidan was told to divide a certain number by $17$. Instead he divided the number by $7$ and got the answer $68$. What was the answer to the division he was supposed to do?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the original number $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {a}{7}   &= 68 \\\\
a               &= 68 \times 7 \\\\
a               &= 476 \\\\
\text{Actual answer}  &= \dfrac {a}{17} \\\\
&= \dfrac {476}{17} \\\\
&= \dfrac {28 \times 17}{17} \\\\
&= \dfrac {28 \times \cancel {17}} {\cancel {17}} \\\\
&= 28
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$28$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Nancy bought five oranges and two apples and they cost $\pounds 3.40$. At the same shop, 
David bought three oranges and one apple and paid $\pounds 2.00$. 

What would Steve have paid if he bought four oranges and two apples from this shop?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Nancy bought five oranges and two apples and they cost $\pounds 3.40$. At the same shop, 
David bought three oranges and one apple and paid $\pounds 2.00$. 
<emptyline>
What would Steve have paid if he bought four oranges and two apples from this shop?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR: It is really important to use the right units in calculations and convert where required.
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the cost of an apple $= a$

Let the cost of an orange $= b$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned} 
5b + 2a &= 3.40 \\\\
3b + a  &= 2.00
\end{aligned}
$

We have got $2$ variables and we have $2$ equations to solve them. Let's eliminate to reduce it to just one variable. 

Multiply the second equation by $2$.

$
\begin{aligned} 
2 \times 3b + 2 \times a &= 2 \times 2.00 \\\\
6b + 2a                  &= 4.00
\end{aligned}
$

Subtract the first equation from the second below to reduce it to one variable.

$
\begin{aligned} 
6b + 2a - (5b + 2a)     &= 4.00 - 3.40 \\\\
6b + 2a - 5b - 2a       &= 0.60 \\\\
b                       &= \pounds 0.60
\end{aligned}
$

Cost of an orange $= \pounds 0.60$

Let's substitute the value of $b$ in one of the initial equations to find the cost of an apple.

$
\begin{aligned} 
3b + a           &= 2.00 \\\\
3 \times 0.60 + a  &= 2.00 \\\\
1.80 + a          &= 2.00 \\\\
a                &= 2.00 - 1.80 \\\\
a                &= \pounds 0.20
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned} 
\text{Steve paid}   &= 4b + 2a \\\\
                    &= 4 \times 0.60 + 2 \times 0.20 \\\\
                    &= 2.40 + 0.40 \\\\
                    &= \pounds 2.80
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$\pounds 2.80$

</div>
</div>

</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A number is **"pro-added"** if I multiply the number by itself and then add the original number to that answer. 

So, for example, **pro-add**$(8) = 8 \times 8 + 8 = 72$.

What number gives the answer $210$ when it is "pro-added"?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</code></pre>
</div>

a (a + 1)      &= 210

We can easily infer the values by using trial and error. Let's find out $2$ numbers which meets the following critiera based on the equations above.

- The product of the $2$ numbers is $210$ 
- The difference of the $2$ numbers is $1$.

Factors of $210 = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 10, 14, 15, 21, 30, 35, 42, 70, 105, 210$

Factor pairs of $210$ that have a difference of $1 = 14, 15$

A quick check shows that $14$ and $15$ meets all the criteria above.

ABBR: 

*Note*: The two equations form a quadratic equation.

*Note*: This is a quadratic equation.

Solving quadratic equations is beyond the scope and any such equations can be easily inferred by trial and error method.
