</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the cost of a balloon pump $= p$

Let the cost of a pack of balloons $= b$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
p + 3b &= 9 \\\\
p + 4b &= 11
\end{aligned}
$

We have got $2$ variables and we have $2$ equations to solve them. Let's use elimination to reduce it to just one variable. 

Subtract first equation from the second to reduce it to one variable.

$
\begin{aligned}
p + 4b - (p + 3b)  &= 11 - 9 \\\\
p + 4b - p - 3b    &= 11 - 9 \\\\
b                 &= \pounds 2
\end{aligned}
$

Cost of a pack of balloons $= \pounds 2$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$\pounds 2$

</div>
</div>

<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Using workings from previous part,

Let's substitute the value of $b$ in one of the equations.

$
\begin{aligned}
p + 3b &= 9 \\\\
p + 3 \times 2 &= 9 \\\\
p + 6         &= 9 \\\\
p             &= 9 - 6 \\\\
p             &= \pounds 3
\end{aligned}
$

Cost of a pump $= \pounds 3$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Total cost} &= 1 \times 3 +  8 \times 2 \\\\
                    &= 3 + 16 \\\\
                    &= \pounds 19
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Tariq wants to use four planks of wood to make the top of a table.

Each plank of wood is $14 \ \text{cm}$ wide.

He wants the table to be $65 \ \text{cm}$ wide with equal spaces between the 
planks of wood.

![papers/kent-college-canterbury/2020/sample-paper-1/s01-q21-i00.png](/assets/papers/kent-college-canterbury/2020/sample-paper-1/s01-q21-i00.png "papers/kent-college-canterbury/2020/sample-paper-1/s01-q21-i00.png")

How much space should he leave between each of the planks of wood?

Show your working. 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Tariq wants to use four planks of wood to make the top of a table.
<emptyline>
Each plank of wood is $14 \ \text{cm}$ wide.
<emptyline>
He wants the table to be $65 \ \text{cm}$ wide with equal spaces between the 
planks of wood.
<emptyline>
%image%
<emptyline>
How much space should he leave between each of the planks of wood?
<emptyline>
Show your working. 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the space between the planks $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
14 \times 4 + 3 \times a &= 65 \\\\
56 + 3 a                 &= 65 \\\\
3 a                      &= 65 - 56 \\\\
3 a                      &= 9 \\\\
a                        &= \dfrac {9} {3} \\\\
a                        &= \dfrac {3 \times 3} {3} \\\\
a                        &= \dfrac {3 \times \cancel {3}} {\cancel {3}} \\\\
a                        &= 3 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

Space between the planks $= 3 \ \text{cm}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$3 \ \text{cm}$

</div>
</div>
<div class="workingscodeblock">
<div class="tipcodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="tipcodeblock_title">

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Let the space between the planks $= a$
<emptyline>
As per the question,
<emptyline>
$
\begin{aligned}
14 \times 4 + 3 \times a &= 65 \\\\
56 + 3 a                 &= 65 \\\\
3 a                      &= 65 - 56 \\\\
3 a                      &= 9 \\\\
a                        &= \dfrac {9} {3} \\\\
a                        &= \dfrac {3 \times 3} {3} \\\\
a                        &= \dfrac {3 \times \cancel {3}} {\cancel {3}} \\\\
a                        &= 3 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$
<emptyline>
Space between the planks $= 3 \ \text{cm}$
</code></pre>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Woody organised a quiz night in the toy room. He asked $25$ questions.

For each correct answer you gained $4$ points.

For each incorrect answer you lost $2$ points.

For each question you did not attempt you scored $0$ points.


Rex answered all but one of the questions and got a score of $66$ points.
How many correct answers did he have?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Woody organised a quiz night in the toy room. He asked $25$ questions.
<emptyline>
For each correct answer you gained $4$ points.
<emptyline>
For each incorrect answer you lost $2$ points.
<emptyline>
For each question you did not attempt you scored $0$ points.
<emptyline>

Rex answered all but one of the questions and got a score of $66$ points.
How many correct answers did he have?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Rex answered all but one of the questions and so he answered $25 - 1 = 24$ questions.

Let number of correct answers $= a$

Number of incorrect answers $= 24 - a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
4 \times a - 2 \times (24 - a) &= 66 \\\\
4a -48 + 2a                  &= 66 \\\\
6a                            &= 66 + 48 \\\\
6a                            &= 114 \\\\
a                             &= \dfrac {114} {6} \\\\
a                            &= \dfrac {19 \times 6} {6} \\\\
a                             &= \dfrac {19 \times \cancel {6}} {\cancel {6}} \\\\
a                             &= 19
\end{aligned}
$

Number of correct answers $= 19$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$19$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Bill is twice as old as his son, who is $50 \ \text{years}$ younger than Bill's father. If the total of their ages is $142$, how old is Bill?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Bill is twice as old as his son, who is $50 \ \text{years}$ younger than Bill's father. If the total of their ages is $142$, how old is Bill?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let Bill's son age $= a$

Bill's age $= 2a$

Bill's father age $= a + 50$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
a + 2a + (a + 50)                                         &= 142 \\\\
4a + 50                                                 &= 142 \\\\
4a                                                      &= 142 - 50 \\\\
4a                                                      &= 92 \\\\
a                                                       &= \dfrac {92} {4} \\\\
a                                                       &= \dfrac {92} {4} \\\\
a                                                       &= \dfrac {23 \times 4} {4} \\\\
a                                                       &= \dfrac {23 \times \cancel {4}} {\cancel {4}} \\\\
a                                                       &= 23 \ \text{years} \\\\
\text {Bill's age}                                      &= 2 \times a \\\\
                                                        &= 2 \times 23 \\\\
                                                        &= 46 \ \text{years}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$46$

</div>
</div>

**Question**

I think of a number, multiply it by $9$, and the result is $36$.
What is the number I first thought of?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">I think of a number, multiply it by $9$, and the result is $36$.

</code></pre>

<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
a \times 9                         &= 36 \\\\
a                                  &= \dfrac {36} {9} \\\\
a                                  &= \dfrac {4 \times 9} {9} \\\\
a                                  &= \dfrac {4 \times \cancel{9}} {\cancel{9}} \\\\
a                                  &= 4
\end{aligned}
$

Number $= 4$

**Question**

I think of a number, multiply it by $6$ and then subtract $5$. The result is $37$.
What is the number I first thought of?


</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">I think of a number, multiply it by $6$ and then subtract $5$. The result is $37$.
What is the number I first thought of?
<emptyline>
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>

%empty%

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
a \times 6 - 5 &= 37 \\\\
6a     &= 37 + 5 \\\\
6a     &= 42 \\\\
a              &= \dfrac {42} {6} \\\\
a              &= \dfrac {7 \times 6} {6} \\\\
a              &= \dfrac {7 \times \cancel{6}} {\cancel{6}} \\\\
a              &= 7
\end{aligned}
$

Number $= 7$
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

In a money bag there are an equal number of $2 \ \text{p}, 5 \ \text{p}$ and no other coins.

How many coins are in the bag if altogether there is $\pounds 1.26?$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">In a money bag there are an equal number of $2 \ \text{p}, 5 \ \text{p}$ and no other coins.
<emptyline>
How many coins are in the bag if altogether there is $\pounds 1.26?$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR: It is really important to use the right units in calculations and convert where required.
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the count of coins of each denomination $= c$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
2\ \text{p} \times c + 5\ \text{p} \times c &= \pounds 1.26 \\\\
2\ \text{p} \times c + 5\ \text{p} \times c &= 126 \ \text{p} \\\\
2c + 5c                                 &= 126 \\\\
7c                                      &= 126 \\\\
c                                       &= \dfrac {126} {7} \\\\
c                                       &= \dfrac {18 \times 7} { 7} \\\\
c                                       &= \dfrac {18 \times \cancel{7}} { \cancel{7} } \\\\
c                                       &= 18
\end{aligned}
$

There are $18$ coins of each type.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Total coins}   &=  18 \times 2  \\\\
                     &= 36 \text{ coins}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$36 \text{ coins}$

</div>
</div>

</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workingcodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="workingcodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Working Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Let the count of coins of each denomination $= c$
<emptyline>
As per the question,
<emptyline>
$
\begin{aligned}
2\ \text{p} \times c + 5\ \text{p} \times c &= \pounds 1.26 \\\\
2\ \text{p} \times c + 5\ \text{p} \times c &= 126 \ \text{p} \\\\
2c + 5c                                 &= 126 \\\\
7c                                      &= 126 \\\\
c                                       &= \dfrac {126} {7} \\\\
c                                       &= \dfrac {18 \times 7} { 7} \\\\
c                                       &= \dfrac {18 \times \cancel{7}} { \cancel{7} } \\\\
c                                       &= 18
\end{aligned}
$
<emptyline>
There are $18$ coins of each type.
<emptyline>
$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Total coins}   &=  18 \times 2  \\\\
                     &= 36 \text{ coins}
\end{aligned}
$
</code></pre>
</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Three-quarters of a number is $36$ less than the number. What's the number?

- $144$
- $48$
- $124$
- $154$
- $52$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>

<emptyline>

- $124$
- $154$
- $52$
</code></pre>

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {3} {4} \times a &= a - 36 \\\\
a - \dfrac {3a} {4} &= 36 \\\\
\dfrac {a \times 4} {4} -\dfrac {3a} {4} &= 36 \\\\
\dfrac {4a - 3a} {4}  &= 36 \\\\
\dfrac {a} {4}  &= 36 \\\\
a &= 36 \times 4 \\\\
a &= 144
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

- $57$

\end{aligned}

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Robin thinks of a number. When he triples the number and then subtracts $13$, he gets $11$. What's his number?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Robin thinks of a number. When he triples the number and then subtracts $13$, he gets $11$. What's his number?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
a \times 3 - 13               &= 11 \\\\
3a                            &= 11 + 13 \\\\
3a                            &= 24 \\\\
a                             &= \dfrac {24} {3} \\\\
a                             &= \dfrac {8 \times 3} {3} \\\\
a                             &= \dfrac {8 \times \cancel {3}} {\cancel {3}} \\\\
a                             &= 8
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$8$

</div>
</div>

**Question**

Ros thinks of a number. When she subtracts the number from $91$ and then adds $19$ to the answer, she gets $12$. What's her number?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</code></pre>

<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%

$
\begin{aligned}
91 - b + 19                            &= 12 \\\\

b                                      &= 98 
\end{aligned}
$

**Question**

Neetha thinks of a number. When she multiplies the number by $5$ and then subtracts the answer from 84 she gets her original number. What's her number?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Neetha thinks of a number. When she multiplies the number by $5$ and then subtracts the answer from 84 she gets her original number. What's her number?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number $= c$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
84 - (c \times 5) &= c \\\\
84 - 5c           &= c \\\\
c + 5c            &= 84 \\\\
6c                &= 84 \\\\
c                 &= \dfrac {84} {6} \\\\
c                 &= \dfrac {14 \times 6} {6} \\\\
c                 &= \dfrac {14 \times \cancel{6} } { \cancel{6} } \\\\
c                 &= 14 
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$14$

**Question**

What do you get when you combine $3$ and $7$ using this rule?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">What do you get when you combine $3$ and $7$ using this rule?
</code></pre>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Using the rule for numbers $3$ and $7$:

$\begin{aligned}
&= 3^2 + 7^2 \\\\
&= 9 + 49 \\\\
&= 58 \\\\
&= 5 + 8 \\\\
&= 13
\end{aligned}$

**Question**

I'm thinking of two different numbers. When I combine them using this rule, I get the answer $9$. What could my two numbers be?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">I'm thinking of two different numbers. When I combine them using this rule, I get the answer $9$. What could my two numbers be?
</code></pre>

<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the two numbers be $a$ and $b$.

According to the rule, we calculate $a^2 + b^2$, then sum the digits of the result to get $9$.

We can easily infer the values by using trial and error.

|  $N$ | Try $a^2 + b^2$                | $a \ne b$? |  Works? |
| :--: | :----------------------------- | :--------: | :-----: |
| $18$ | $3^2 + 3^2 = 9 + 9 = 18$       |     No     |    No   |
| $27$ | No valid pair                  |      —     |    No   |
| $36$ | $6^2 + 0^2$ |     Yes     |    Yes   |
| $45$ | $6^2 + 3^2 = 36 + 9 = 45$      |     Yes    | Yes |
| $54$ | No valid pair                  |      —     |    No   |
| $63$ | No valid pair                  |      —     |    No   |
| $72$ | No valid pair                  |      —     |    No   |
| $81$ | $9^2 + 0^2$      Yes     |    Yes   |
| $90$ | $9^2 + 3^2 = 81 + 9 = 90$      |     Yes    | Yes |
| $99$ | No valid pair                  |      —     |    No   |

A quick check shows $3$ and $6$ meets the criteria above.

Numbers $= 3, 6$
</div>
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$3, 6$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

$60\%$ of a number is $240$. What is the number? 

- $60$ 
- $144$ 
- $240$ 
- $300$ 
- $400$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">$60\%$ of a number is $240$. What is the number? 
<emptyline>
- $60$ 
- $144$ 
- $240$ 
- $300$ 
- $400$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {60} {100} \times a           &=  240 \\\\
a                                    &=  \dfrac {240 \times 100} {60} \\\\
a                                    &=  \dfrac {60 \times 4 \times 100} {60} \\\\
a                                    &=  \dfrac {\cancel {60} \times 4 \times 100} {\cancel {60}} \\\\
a                                    &=  4 \times 100 \\\\
a                                    &=  400
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Half of a number is $8$ bigger than three sevenths of the number. What's the number? 

- $140$ 
- $126$ 
- $119$ 
- $112$ 
- $98$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Half of a number is $8$ bigger than three sevenths of the number. What's the number? 
<emptyline>
- $140$ 
- $126$ 
- $119$ 
- $112$ 
- $98$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {1} {2} \times a                                                  &=  8 + \dfrac {3} {7} \times a \\\\
\dfrac {a} {2}                                                           &=  8 + \dfrac {3 a} {7} \\\\
\dfrac {a} {2} - \dfrac {3 a} {7}                                        &=  8 \\\\
\dfrac {a \times 7 } {2 \times 7} - \dfrac {3a \times 2 } {7 \times 2}  &=  8 \\\\
\dfrac {7 a} {14} - \dfrac {6 a} {14}                                    &=  8 \\\\
\dfrac {7 a - 6 a} {14}                                                  &=  8 \\\\
\dfrac {a} {14}                                                          &=  8 \\\\
a                                                                        &=  14 \times 8 \\\\
a                                                                        &= 112
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

The total of five different, positive odd numbers is $85$. What's the most that the largest number could be? 

- $69$ 
- $35$ 
- $25$ 
- $21$ 
- $17$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</code></pre>

**Working**

Let the largest odd number $= n$

We want the largest number to be as big as possible. The other four odd numbers should be as small as possible and different from each other.

$4$ smallest different positive odd numbers are $= 1$, $3$, $5$, $7$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
1 + 3 + 5 + 7 + n &= 85 \\\\
n + 16          &= 85 \\\\
n               &= 85 - 16 \\\\
n               &= 69
\end{aligned}
$

Largest number $= 69$
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

I'm thinking of two numbers, one of which is three times as big as the other. When I double one of my numbers and then add it to the other I get $140$. Which of the following cannot possibly be one of my numbers? 

- $20$ 
- $28$ 
- $50$ 
- $60$ 
- $84$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">I'm thinking of two numbers, one of which is three times as big as the other. When I double one of my numbers and then add it to the other I get $140$. Which of the following cannot possibly be one of my numbers? 
<emptyline>
- $20$ 
- $28$ 
- $50$ 
- $60$ 
- $84$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let one number $= a$

Other number $= 3a$

Option $1$: Doubling the smaller number

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
2 \times 3 a + a        &= 140 \\\\
6 a + a                 &= 140 \\\\
7 a                     &= 140 \\\\
a                       &= \dfrac {140} {7} \\\\
a                       &= \dfrac {7 \times 20} {7} \\\\
a                       &= \dfrac {\cancel {7} \times 20} {\cancel {7}} \\\\
a                       &= 20 \\\\
\text {First number}    &= 20 \\\\
\text {Second number}   &= 20 \times 3 \\\\
                        &= 60
\end{aligned}
$

Option $2$: Doubling the larger number

$
\begin{aligned}
3 a + 2 \times a        &= 140 \\\\
3 a + 2 a               &= 140 \\\\
4 a                     &= 140 \\\\
a                       &= \dfrac {140} {5} \\\\
a                       &= \dfrac {5 \times 28} {5} \\\\
a                       &= \dfrac {\cancel {5} \times 28} {\cancel {5}} \\\\
a                       &= 28 \\\\
\text {First number}    &= 28 \\\\
\text {Second number}   &= 28 \times 3 \\\\
                        &= 84
\end{aligned}
$

Possible numbers are $= 20$, $28$, $60$, $84$

The one that cannot be the possible answer $= 50$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$50$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Three different positive odd numbers add up to $15$. What could the three numbers be?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Three different positive odd numbers add up to $15$. What could the three numbers be?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the three numbers $= a, \ a + 2, \ a + 4$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
a + a + 2 + a + 4 &= 15 \\\\
3 a + 6           &= 15 \\\\
3 a               &= 15 - 6 \\\\
3 a               &= 9 \\\\
a                 &= \dfrac {9} {3} \\\\
a                 &= \dfrac {3 \times 3} {3} \\\\
a                 &= \dfrac {3 \times \cancel {3}} {\cancel {3}} \\\\
a                 &= 3
\end{aligned}
$

Three numbers $= 3, \ 5, \ 7$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

a                  &= 52
\end{aligned}
$

Number $= 52$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

a        &= \dfrac {15 \times \cancel {3}} {\cancel {3}} \\\\
a        &= 15
\end{aligned}
$

Number $= 15$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

I think of a number. When I subtract it from $24$, the answer is the same as when I double it.

What's my number? 

- $12$ 
- $10$
- $8$ 
- $6$ 
- $9$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">I think of a number. When I subtract it from $24$, the answer is the same as when I double it.
<emptyline>

<emptyline>
- $12$ 
- $10$
- $8$ 
- $6$ 
- $9$
</code></pre>
</div>

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
24 - a          &= 2 \times a \\\\
24 - a          &= 2 a \\\\
24              &= 2 a + a \\\\
3 a             &= 24 \\\\
a               &= \dfrac {24} {3} \\\\
a               &= \dfrac {8 \times 3} {3} \\\\
a               &= \dfrac {8 \times \cancel{3}} {\cancel{3}} \\\\
a               &= 8
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

**Question**

Two-thirds of a number is $66$. What's the number? 

- $100$ 
- $99$ 
- $44$ 
- $33$ 
- $132$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

a                         &=  33 \times 3 \\\\
a                         &=  99
\end{aligned}
$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Two-thirds of a number is $3$ more than three-fifths of the number. What's the number? 

- $20$ 
- $90$ 
- $54$ 
- $60$ 
- $45$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Two-thirds of a number is $3$ more than three-fifths of the number. What's the number? 
<emptyline>
- $20$ 
- $90$ 
- $54$ 
- $60$ 
- $45$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {2} {3} \times a                                                  &= 3 + \dfrac {3} {5} \times a \\\\
\dfrac {2 a} {3}                                                         &= 3 + \dfrac {3 a} {5} \\\\
\dfrac {2 a} {3} - \dfrac {3 a} {5}                                      &= 3 \\\\
\dfrac {2 a \times 5} {3 \times 5} - \dfrac {3 a \times 3} {5 \times 3}  &= 3 \\\\
\dfrac {10 a} {15} - \dfrac {9 a} {15}                                   &= 3 \\\\
\dfrac {10 a - 9 a} {15}                                                 &= 3 \\\\
\dfrac {a} {15}                                                          &= 3 \\\\
a                                                                        &= 15 \times 3 \\\\
a                                                                        &= 45
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

<div class="option" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$45$

</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Three different, positive odd numbers add together to make $23$. What is the smallest possible value of the largest of the three numbers? 

- $7$ 
- $9$ 
- $11$ 
- $13$ 
- $1$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Three different, positive odd numbers add together to make $23$. What is the smallest possible value of the largest of the three numbers? 
<emptyline>
- $7$ 
- $9$ 
- $11$ 
- $13$ 
- $1$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

We have to find the smallest possible value of the largest of the three numbers, so we should make the other two odd numbers as large as possible.

We can easily infer the answer by using trial and error.

| $a$ | $b$ |  $c = 23 - (a + b)$ | Valid |
| :-: | :-: | :-----------------: | :-: |
| $1$ | $3$ | $23 - (1 + 3) = 19$ | Yes |
| $1$ | $5$ | $23 - (1 + 5) = 17$ | Yes |
| $1$ | $7$ | $23 - (1 + 7) = 15$ | Yes |
| $1$ | $9$ | $23 - (1 + 9) = 13$ | Yes |
| $3$ | $5$ | $23 - (3 + 5) = 15$ | Yes |
| $3$ | $7$ | $23 - (3 + 7) = 13$ | Yes |
| $3$ | $9$ | $23 - (3 + 9) = 11$ | Yes |
| $5$ | $7$ | $23 - (5 + 7) = 11$ | Yes |
| $5$ | $9$ | $23 - (5 + 9) = 9$  | No |
| $7$ | $9$ | $23 - (7 + 9) = 7$  | No |

A quick check shows that the best valid sets are $3, \ 9, \ 11$ and $5, \ 7, \ 11$ with the largest number being $11$.

Answer $= 11$
</div>
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$11$

</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

I'm thinking of a number. When I triple it and subtract the result from $70$, I get half my original number. What's my number? 

- $24$ 
- $30$ 
- $18$ 
- $20$ 
- $25$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">I'm thinking of a number. When I triple it and subtract the result from $70$, I get half my original number. What's my number? 
<emptyline>
- $24$ 
- $30$ 
- $18$ 
- $20$ 
- $25$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
70 - 3a                     &= \dfrac {1} {2} \times a \\\\
\dfrac {a} {2} + 3 a                                   &= 70 \\\\
\dfrac {a} {2} + \dfrac {3 a \times 2} {2}    &= 70 \\\\
\dfrac {a} {2} + \dfrac {6 a} {2}                      &= 70 \\\\
\dfrac {a + 6 a} {2}                                   &= 70 \\\\
\dfrac {7 a} {2}                                       &= 70 \\\\
a                                                      &= \dfrac {70 \times 2} {7} \\\\
a                                                      &= \dfrac {10 \times 7 \times 2} {7}  \\\\
a                                                      &= \dfrac {10 \times \cancel {7} \times 2} {\cancel {7}} \\\\
a                                                      &= 20
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="option" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<p>D</p>
</div>
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$20$

</div>
</div>

\end{aligned}

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

I'm thinking of two numbers. When I double the first and add it to the second I get $160$. One of the numbers is half of the other. Which of these could be one of my numbers?

- $30$ 
- $45$ 
- $60$ 
- $64$ 
- $96$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">I'm thinking of two numbers. When I double the first and add it to the second I get $160$. One of the numbers is half of the other. Which of these could be one of my numbers?
<emptyline>
- $30$ 
- $45$ 
- $60$ 
- $64$ 
- $96$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the smaller number $= a$

Other number $= 2a$

Option $1$: Doubling the smaller number

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
2 \times a + 2a        &= 160 \\\\
4a                    &= 160 \\\\
a                       &= \dfrac {160} {4} \\\\
a                       &= \dfrac {4 \times 40} {4} \\\\
a                       &= \dfrac {\cancel {4} \times 40} {\cancel {4}} \\\\
a                       &= 40 \\\\
\text {First number}    &= 40 \\\\
\text {Second number}   &= 40 \times 2 \\\\
                        &= 80
\end{aligned}
$

$40$ and $80$ are not in the options.

Let's try the other option.

Option $2$: Doubling the larger number

$
\begin{aligned}
a + 2 \times 2a        &= 160 \\\\
a + 4 a                 &= 160 \\\\
5 a                     &= 160 \\\\
a                       &= \dfrac {160} {5} \\\\
a                       &= \dfrac {5 \times 32} {5} \\\\
a                       &= \dfrac {\cancel {5} \times 32} {\cancel {5}} \\\\
a                       &= 32 \\\\
\text {First number}    &= 32 \\\\
\text {Second number}   &= 32 \times 2 \\\\
                        &= 64
\end{aligned}
$

Answer $= 64$
</div>
</div>

</div>
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$64$

</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Mr Humberstone's maths class has $26$ pupils. There are $8$ more girls than there are boys. How many girls are there?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Mr Humberstone's maths class has $26$ pupils. There are $8$ more girls than there are boys. How many girls are there?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number boys $= b$

Number of girls $= b + 8$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
b + b + 8 &= 26 \\\\
2 b + 8   &= 26 \\\\
2 b       &= 26 - 8 \\\\
2 b       &= 18 \\\\
b         &= \dfrac {18} {2} \\\\
b         &= \dfrac {2 \times 9} {2} \\\\
b         &= \dfrac {\cancel {2} \times 9} {\cancel {2}} \\\\
b         &= 9
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number of girls} &= b + 8 \\\\
                       &= 9 + 8 \\\\
                       &= 17
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$17$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

In Miss Home's maths class, the number of girls is three-quarters the number of boys, and there are $28$ children altogether. How many girls are there?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">In Miss Home's maths class, the number of girls is three-quarters the number of boys, and there are $28$ children altogether. How many girls are there?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number boys $= b$

Number of girls $= \dfrac {3b} {4}$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
b + \dfrac { 3b} {4}                                 &= 28 \\\\
\dfrac {b \times 4} {4} +  \dfrac {3 b} {4}          &= 28 \\\\
\dfrac {4 b} {4} + \dfrac {3 b} {4}                  &= 28 \\\\
\dfrac {4 b + 3 b} {4}                               &= 28 \\\\
\dfrac {7 b} {4}                                     &= 28 \\\\
b                                                    &= \dfrac {28 \times 4} {7} \\\\
b                                                    &= \dfrac {7 \times 4 \times 4} {7} \\\\
b                                                    &= \dfrac {\cancel {7} \times 4 \times 4} {\cancel {7}} \\\\
b                                                    &= 4 \times 4 \\\\
b                                                    &= 16
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number of girls} &= \dfrac {3b} {4} \\\\
                       &= \dfrac {3 \times 16} {4} \\\\
                       &= \dfrac {3 \times 4 \times 4} {4} \\\\
                       &= \dfrac {3 \times 4 \times \cancel {4}} {\cancel {4}} \\\\
                       &= 3 \times 4 \\\\
                       &= 12
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$12$

</div>
</div>
<div class="workingscodeblock">

**Question**

In Miss Thompson's class, there are $5$ girls for every $4$ boys, and one-fifth of the girls wear glasses. There are three girls and two boys in the class who wear glasses. What fraction of all the pupils in the class wear glasses?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$
\begin{aligned}

a                                                           &= \dfrac {3 \times 9 \times 5} {5} \\\\
a                                                           &= \dfrac {3 \times 9 \times \cancel {5}} {\cancel {5}} \\\\
a                                                           &= 3 \times 9 \\\\
a                                                           &= 27
\end{aligned}

                                                            &= \dfrac {3 + 2} {27} \\\\
                                                            &= \dfrac {5} {27}
\end{aligned}
$

**Question**

Sarah thinks of a number. When she triples the number and then adds $15$, she gets the answer $39$. What was her number?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Sarah thinks of a number. When she triples the number and then adds $15$, she gets the answer $39$. What was her number?
</code></pre>

<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

Let the number $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
3 \times a + 15  &= 39 \\\\
3 a              &= 39 - 15 \\\\
3 a              &= 24 \\\\
a                &= \dfrac {24} {3} \\\\
a                &= \dfrac {8 \times 3} {3} \\\\
a                &= \dfrac {8 \times \cancel {3}} {\cancel {3}} \\\\
a                &= 8
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

**Question**

Kirsty thinks of a number. When she adds $15$ to the number and then triples the answer, she gets $39$. What was her number?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Kirsty thinks of a number. When she adds $15$ to the number and then triples the answer, she gets $39$. What was her number?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
3 \times (a + 15)  &= 39 \\\\
a + 15             &= \dfrac {39} {3} \\\\
a + 15             &= \dfrac {13 \times 3} {3} \\\\
a + 15             &= \dfrac {13 \times \cancel {3}} {\cancel {3}} \\\\
a + 15             &= 13 \\\\
a                  &= 13 - 15 \\\\
a                  &= - 2
\end{aligned}
$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

I think of a number, multiply it by three and add $7$. The answer is $25$. What is the number I am thinking of?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

$
\begin{aligned}
3 \times a + 7   &= 25 \\\\

a                &= \dfrac {6 \times 3} {3} \\\\
a                &= \dfrac {6 \times \cancel {3}} {\cancel {3}} \\\\
a                &= 6
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

a                                           &= 8 \\\\

                                              &= 800 \ \text{copies}
\end{aligned}
$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

&= 3 \times 6 \\\\
&= 18 \\\\
\text{Second expression} &= 4(k + 2) \\\\

&= 32 \\\\
\text{Third expression} &= k ^ 2 \\\\
&= 6 ^2 \\\\
&= 36
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

**Question**

$3y + 1 = 16$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">$3y + 1 = 16$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
3y + 1 &= 16 \\\\
3y     &= 16 - 1 \\\\
3y     &= 15 \\\\
y      &= \dfrac {15} {3} \\\\
y      &= \dfrac {5 \times 3} {3} \\\\
y      &= \dfrac {5 \times \cancel {3}} {\cancel {3}} \\\\
y      &= 5
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

I think of a number and multiply it by $3$ and then subtract $6$. If the result is $15$ what number was I thinking of?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">I think of a number and multiply it by $3$ and then subtract $6$. If the result is $15$ what number was I thinking of?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
a \times 3 - 6   &= 15 \\\\
3 a - 6          &= 15 \\\\
3 a              &= 15 + 6 \\\\
3 a              &= 21 \\\\
a                &= \dfrac {21} {3} \\\\
a                &= \dfrac {3 \times 7} {3} \\\\
a                &= \dfrac {\cancel {3} \times 7} {\cancel {3}} \\\\
a                &= 7
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$7$

</div>
</div>

\begin{aligned}

a &= \dfrac {26 \times 100} {100} \\\\
a &= \dfrac {26 \times \cancel {100}} {\cancel {100}}\\\\
a &= 26 \ \text {computers}
\end{aligned}
$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

John came home from his vacation at his grandmother's with $5$ books. 
While he was away he bought $2$ books at the bookshop and got $1$ book as a present from his grandmother. 
During his stay at his grandmother's, he also gave his cousin $4$ books that he had finished.
How many books did he take with him when he left for his holiday?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">John came home from his vacation at his grandmother's with $5$ books. 
While he was away he bought $2$ books at the bookshop and got $1$ book as a present from his grandmother. 
During his stay at his grandmother's, he also gave his cousin $4$ books that he had finished.
How many books did he take with him when he left for his holiday?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number of books he took with him $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
a + 2 + 1 - 4 &= 5 \\\\
a - 1        &= 5 \\\\
a             &= 5 + 1 \\\\
a             &= 6
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$6$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

$2$ packets of crisps and $2$ drinks costs $\pounds 1.50$. $2$ packets of crisps and $1$ drink costs $\pounds 1.10$. 
What would it cost me if I buy $3$ packets of crisps and $4$ drinks?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">$2$ packets of crisps and $2$ drinks costs $\pounds 1.50$. $2$ packets of crisps and $1$ drink costs $\pounds 1.10$. 
What would it cost me if I buy $3$ packets of crisps and $4$ drinks?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let cost of packets of crisps $= c$

Let cost of drink $= d$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
2c + 2d &= 1.50 \\\\
2c + d  &= 1.10
\end{aligned}
$

We have got $2$ variables and we have $2$ equations to solve them. Let's use elimination to reduce it to just one variable. 

Subtract second equation from the first to reduce it to one variable.

$
\begin{aligned}
2c + 2d - (2c + d) &= 1.50 - 1.10 \\\\
2c + 2d - 2c - d   &= 0.40 \\\\
b                  &= 0.40
\end{aligned}
$

Let's substitute the value of $b$ in one of the equations.

$
\begin{aligned}
2c + 0.40 &= 1.10 \\\\
2c        &= 1.10 - 0.40 \\\\
2c        &= 0.7 \\\\
c         &= \dfrac{0.7}{2} \\\\
c         &= 0.35
\end{aligned}
$

Cost of packet of crisps $= \pounds 0.35$

Cost of drink $= \pounds 0.40$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Cost of 3 crisps and 4 drinks }   &= 3c + 4d \\\\
                                        &= 3 \times 0.35 + 4 \times 0.40 \\\\
                                        &= 1.05 + 1.60 \\\\
                                        &= \pounds 2.65
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$\pounds 2.65$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Sam thinks of a number, multiplies it by $2$ and then adds $11$. The answer he gets is $29$. What number did he think of?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Sam thinks of a number, multiplies it by $2$ and then adds $11$. The answer he gets is $29$. What number did he think of?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
a \times 2 + 11 &= 29 \\\\
2a      &= 29 - 11 \\\\
2a      &= 18 \\\\
a               &= \dfrac {18} {2} \\\\
a               &= \dfrac {9 \times \cancel {2}} {\cancel {2}} \\\\
a               &= 9
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$9$

**Question**

Julia thinks of a number, multiplies it by $5$, adds $11$ and then divides it by $2$. She gets the answer $28$. 
What number did she think of?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Julia thinks of a number, multiplies it by $5$, adds $11$ and then divides it by $2$. She gets the answer $28$. 
What number did she think of?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
(a \times 5 + 11) \div 2              &= 28 \\\\
(5a + 11) \times \dfrac{1}{2} &= 28 \\\\
5a + 11                       &= 28 \times 2 \\\\
5a + 11                       &= 56 \\\\
5a                            &= 56 - 11 \\\\
5a                            &= 45 \\\\
a                                     &= \dfrac {45} {5} \\\\
a                                     &= \dfrac {9 \times 5} {5} \\\\
a                                     &= \dfrac {9 \times \cancel {5}} {\cancel {5}} \\\\
a                                     &= 9
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Sam and Julia find there is one number for which, if they both start from that number and follow their own rules, they get the same answer. What is the number they both start with?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Sam and Julia find there is one number for which, if they both start from that number and follow their own rules, they get the same answer. What is the number they both start with?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
a \times 2 + 11     &= (a \times 5 + 11) \div 2 \\\\
2a + 11     &= (5a + 11) \times \dfrac{1} {2} \\\\
2a + 11     &= \dfrac{(5a + 11)}{2}  \\\\
2 \times (2 a + 11)  &= 5 a + 11 \\\\
4 a + 22            &= 5 a + 11 \\\\
5a - 4a             &= 22 - 11 \\\\
a                   &= 11
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

How many dogs are there ?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<div class="workings">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number of dogs $= d$

Let the number of kennels $= k$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
d &= 3k + 2 \\\\
d &= 4(k - 1)                           
\end{aligned}
$

We have got $2$ variables and we have $2$ equations to solve them. Let's use elimination to reduce it to just one variable. 

Subtract the second equation from the first equation.

$
\begin{aligned}
d - d &= 3k + 2 - 4(k - 1) \\\\
0     &= 3k + 2 - 4k + 4 \\\\
0     &= -k + 6 \\\\
k     &= 6                     
\end{aligned}
$

Substituting the value of $k$ in the first equation,

$
\begin{aligned}
d   &= 3 \times 6 + 2 \\\\
d   &= 18 + 2 \\\\
d   &= 20                  
\end{aligned}
$

Number of dogs $= 20$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$20$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

$\Psi$ is a new mathematical rule which works like this:

To work out $2 \ \Psi\  4$ add $1$ to $2$, then multiply by $4$, like this:

$2 + 1 = 3$

$3 \times 4 = 12$

So $2 \ \Psi\  4 = 12$

Similarly $4 \ \Psi\  7 = 35$ because $4 + 1 = 5$, then $5 \times 7 = 35$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</code></pre>

<div class="workings">

\begin{aligned}

(2 + 1) \times y &= 18 \\\\

y                &= \dfrac {6 \times 3} {3} \\\\
y                &= \dfrac {6 \times \cancel {3}} {\cancel {3}} \\\\
y                &= 6
\end{aligned}
$

**Question**

If $z \ \Psi\  4 = 36$, what number does $z$ stand for?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">If $z \ \Psi\  4 = 36$, what number does $z$ stand for?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
z \ \Psi \ 4     &= 36 \\\\
(z + 1) \times 4 &= 36 \\\\
z + 1            &= \dfrac {36} {4} \\\\
z + 1            &= \dfrac {9 \times 4} {4} \\\\
z + 1            &= \dfrac {9 \times \cancel {4}} {\cancel {4}} \\\\
z + 1            &= 9 \\\\
z                &= 9 - 1 \\\\
z                &= 8
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$8$

**Question**

If $p \ \Psi\  q = 20$, find all the pairs of whole numbers that $p$ and $q$ could be.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">If $p \ \Psi\  q = 20$, find all the pairs of whole numbers that $p$ and $q$ could be.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
p \ \Psi \ q     &= 20 \\\\
(p + 1) \times q &= 20
\end{aligned}
$

We can easily infer the values by using trial and error. Let's find out $2$ numbers which meets the following critiera based on the equations above.

Factors of $20 = 1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 20$

Factor pairs of $20 = (1, 20), (2, 10), (4, 5)$

Using the factor pairs we will infer the values of $p$ and $q$.

| Factor Pairs   |$p$           |   $q$ |
|:-------:  |:--------------------:  |:----------------------:   |
| $1, 20$   |       $1 -1 = 0$       |       $20$                  |
| $2, 10$   |       $2 - 1 = 1$      |       $10$                  |
| $4, 5$    |       $4 - 1 = 3$      |       $5$                   |
| $5, 4$    |       $5 - 1 = 4$      |       $4$                  |
| $10, 2$   |       $10 - 1 = 9$     |       $2$                  |
| $20, 1$   |       $20 - 1 = 19$    |       $1$                  |

Answer $= (0,20), \ (1,10), \ (3,5), \ (4,4), \ (9,2), \ (19,1)$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$(0,20), \ (1,10), \ (3,5), \ (4,4), \ (9,2), \ (19,1)$

</div>

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">As per the question,
<emptyline>
$
\begin{aligned}
p \ \Psi \ q     &= 20 \\\\
(p + 1) \times q &= 20
\end{aligned}
$
<emptyline>
We can easily infer the values by using trial and error. Let's find out $2$ numbers which meets the following critiera based on the equations above.
<emptyline>
Factors of $20 = 1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 20$
<emptyline>
Factor pairs of $20 = (1, 20), (2, 10), (4, 5)$
<emptyline>
Using the factor pairs we will infer the values of $p$ and $q$.
<emptyline>
| Factor Pairs   |$p$           |   $q$ |
|:-------:  |:--------------------:  |:----------------------:   |
| $1, 20$   |       $1 -1 = 0$       |       $20$                  |
| $2, 10$   |       $2 - 1 = 1$      |       $10$                  |
| $4, 5$    |       $4 - 1 = 3$      |       $5$                   |
| $5, 4$    |       $5 - 1 = 4$      |       $4$                  |
| $10, 2$   |       $10 - 1 = 9$     |       $2$                  |
| $20, 1$   |       $20 - 1 = 19$    |       $1$                  |
<emptyline>

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Leaves at the end of second day} &= \dfrac {1} {2} \times \dfrac {1} {2} \times 400000 \\\\
                                            &= \dfrac {400000} {4} \\\\
                                            &= \dfrac {100000 \times 4} {4} \\\\
                                            &= \dfrac {100000 \times \cancel {4}} {\cancel {4}} \\\\
                                            &= 100000
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

In a barn there are only horses and people. If there are $12$ heads and $34$ legs how many horses and how many people are there?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">In a barn there are only horses and people. If there are $12$ heads and $34$ legs how many horses and how many people are there?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let number of people $= p$

Let number of horses $= h$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
p + h   &= 12 \\\\
2p + 4h &= 34
\end{aligned}
$

We have got $2$ variables and we have $2$ equations to solve them. Let's use elimination to reduce it to just one variable. 

Multiply first equation by $2$.

$
\begin{aligned}
2 \times p + 2 \times h &= 2 \times 12 \\\\
2p + 2h                 &= 24
\end{aligned}
$

Subtract the above equation from the second equation.

$
\begin{aligned}
2p + 4h - (2p + 2h)        &= 34 - 24 \\\\
2p + 4h - 2p - 2h          &= 10 \\\\
2h                         &= 10 \\\\
h                          &= \dfrac{10} {2} \\\\
h                          &= \dfrac{2 \times 5} {2} \\\\
h                          &= \dfrac{\cancel 2 \times 5} {\cancel 2} \\\\
h                          &= 5
\end{aligned}
$

Let's substitute the value of $h$ in one of the equations.

$
\begin{aligned}
p + 5  &= 12 \\\\
p      &= 12 - 5 \\\\
p      &= 7
\end{aligned}
$

Number of people $= 7$

Number of horses $= 5$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

People $=$ $7$

</div>
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

Horses $=$ $5$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Ali has six times as much chocolate as Beth. Carl has twice as much chocolate as Beth. If Carl has $200 \ \text{g}$ of chocolate, how much chocolate does Ali have?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Ali has six times as much chocolate as Beth. Carl has twice as much chocolate as Beth. If Carl has $200 \ \text{g}$ of chocolate, how much chocolate does Ali have?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the chocolate with Beth $= a$

Chocolate with Ali $= 6 a$

Chocolate with Carl $= 2 a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
2a                         &= 200 \\\\
a                          &= \dfrac {200} {2} \\\\
a                          &= \dfrac {100 \times 2} {2} \\\\
a                          &= \dfrac {100 \times \cancel {2}} {\cancel {2}} \\\\
a                          &= 100 \ \text{g} \\\\
\text{Chocolate with Ali} &= 6a \\\\
                           &= 6 \times 100 \\\\
                           &= 600 \ \text{g}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$600 \ \text{g}$

</div>
</div>

**Working**

Let number of pupils in year $8 = a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {1} {4} \times a        &= 30 \\\\
\dfrac {a} {4}                 &= 30 \\\\
a                              &= 30 \times 4 \\\\
a                              &= 120
\end{aligned}
$

Number of pupils in year $8 = 120$
$

x       &= 7
\end{aligned}
$

<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</code></pre>

<div class="workings">

\begin{aligned}

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Anna has $3$ brothers and $5$ sisters. Her brother Tom has $S$ sisters and $B$ brothers. What is the value of $S \times B?$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Anna has $3$ brothers and $5$ sisters. Her brother Tom has $S$ sisters and $B$ brothers. What is the value of $S \times B?$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

For Tom, there are $5$ sisters and so $S = 5$.

For Tom, there are $2$ brothers (all the boys except himself) and so $B = 2$.

$
\begin{aligned}
S \times B &= 5 \times 2 \\\\
           &= 10
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$10$

</div>
</div>
