<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

John picked strawberries every day for $7 \ \text{days}$. Each day after the first day, he picked $5$ more strawberries than the day before. In total he picked $175$ strawberries. How many strawberries did John pick on the last day? 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">John picked strawberries every day for $7 \ \text{days}$. Each day after the first day, he picked $5$ more strawberries than the day before. In total he picked $175$ strawberries. How many strawberries did John pick on the last day? 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number of strawberries picked on the first day $= s$

$
\begin{aligned}
s + (s + 5) + (s + 10) + (s + 15) + (s + 20) + (s + 25) + (s + 30) &= 175 \\\\
7s + 105                                                                &= 175 \\\\
7s                                                                      &= 175 - 105 \\\\
7s                                                                      &= 70 \\\\
s                                                                       &= 10 \\\\
\text{Strawberries picked on the last day} &= s + 30 \\\\
                                                                        &= 40
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$40$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A school has $995$ pupils. If there are $7$ less girls than boys, how many boys are there in the school?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A school has $995$ pupils. If there are $7$ less girls than boys, how many boys are there in the school?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number of boys $= b$

Number of girls $= b - 7$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
b + (b - 7)                                               &= 995 \\\\
2b - 7                                                    &= 995 \\\\
2b                                                        &= 995 + 7 \\\\
2b                                                        &= 1002 \\\\
b                                                         &= \dfrac {1002} {2} \\\\
b                                                         &= \dfrac {2 \times 501} {2} \\\\
b                                                         &= \dfrac {\cancel{2} \times 501} {\cancel{2}} \\\\
b                                                         &= 501
\end{aligned}
$

Number of boys $= 501$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$501$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

$\dfrac {2} {5}$ of the children in a class are boys. There are $12$ girls in the class. How many boys are there?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">$\dfrac {2} {5}$ of the children in a class are boys. There are $12$ girls in the class. How many boys are there?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the total number of children $= c$

Number of boys $= \dfrac {2} {5} \times c$

Number of girls $= 12$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {2} {5} \times c + 12                                      &= c \\\\
c - \dfrac {2c} {5}                                &= 12 \\\\
\dfrac {5 \times c} {5} - \dfrac {2c} {5}                     &= 12 \\\\
\dfrac {5c - 2c} {5}                                 &= 12 \\\\
\dfrac {3c} {5}                                       &= 12 \\\\
c                                                   &= \dfrac {12 \times  5} {3} \\\\
c                                                   &= \dfrac {4 \times 3 \times  5} {3} \\\\
c                                                   &= \dfrac {\cancel{3} \times 4 \times  5} {\cancel{3}} \\\\
c                                                   &= 20 \\\\
\text{Number of boys}                             &= \dfrac {2} {5} \times 20 \\\\
                                                    &= \dfrac {2 \times 20} {5} \\\\
                                                    &= \dfrac {2 \times 4 \times 5} {5} \\\\
                                                    &= \dfrac {2 \times 4 \times \cancel{5}} {\cancel{5}} \\\\
                                                    &= 8
\end{aligned}
$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

When you add up two numbers you get $35$, but when you subtract the two numbers you get $13$. What are the two numbers? 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">When you add up two numbers you get $35$, but when you subtract the two numbers you get $13$. What are the two numbers? 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the first number $= a$

Let the second number $= b$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned} 
a + b                    &= 35 \\\\
a - b                    &= 13
\end{aligned}
$

We have got $2$ variables and we have $2$ equations to solve them. Lets eliminate to reduce it to just one variable.

Subtract the first equation from the second to reduce it to one variable.

$
\begin{aligned} 
a + b - (a - b)          &= 35 - 13 \\\\
a + b - a + b            &= 22 \\\\
2b                       &= 22 \\\\
b                        &= \dfrac {22} {2} \\\\
b                        &= \dfrac {2 \times 11} {2} \\\\
b                        &= \dfrac {\cancel{2} \times 11} {\cancel{2}} \\\\
b                        &= 11
\end{aligned}
$

Let's substitute the value of $b$ in one of the initial equations.

$
\begin{aligned} 
a + b                    &= 35 \\\\
a + 11                   &= 35 \\\\
a                        &= 35 - 11 \\\\
a                        &= 24
\end{aligned}
$

First number $= 24$

Second number $= 11$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$24$

</div>
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$11$

</div>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the missing number $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac{a - 6}{6} &= 6 \\\\
a - 6            &= 6 \times 6 \\\\
a - 6            &= 36 \\\\
a                &= 36 + 6 \\\\
a                &= 42
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Tom and Sarah are playing with number machines.

Tom's machine adds $4$ to any number put into it and then multiplies the result by $5$.

![papers/reigate-grammar-school/2010/sample-paper-1/s01-q36-i00.png](/assets/papers/reigate-grammar-school/2010/sample-paper-1/s01-q36-i00.png "papers/reigate-grammar-school/2010/sample-paper-1/s01-q36-i00.png")

When he puts $2$ in, out comes $30$.

Fill in the missing numbers for Tom's machine

|**in**  |**out** |
|:------:|:------:|
|$2$     |$30$    |
|$3$     |$\ldots$|
|$4$     |$\ldots$|
|$8$     |$\ldots$|
|$\ldots$|$75$    |

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Tom and Sarah are playing with number machines.
<emptyline>
Tom's machine adds $4$ to any number put into it and then multiplies the result by $5$.
<emptyline>
%image%
<emptyline>

<emptyline>
Fill in the missing numbers for Tom's machine
<emptyline>
|**in**  |**out** |
|:------:|:------:|
|$2$     |$30$    |
|$3$     |$\ldots$|
|$4$     |$\ldots$|
|$8$     |$\ldots$|
|$\ldots$|$75$    |
</code></pre>
</div>

<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let's calculte the last missing input first.

Let the input $= a$

$\begin{aligned}
(a + 4) \times 5 &= 75 \\\\
a + 4 &= \dfrac{75}{5} \\\\
a + 4 &= \dfrac{15 \times 5}{5} \\\\
a + 4 &= \dfrac{15 \times \cancel{5}}{\cancel{5}} \\\\
a + 4 &= 15 \\\\
a &= 15 - 4 \\\\
a &= 11
\end{aligned}$

Lets fill in the other missing outputs.

| **in** | **out**              |
| :----: | :----------------------------------: |
|   $2$  | $ 30 $   |
|   $3$  | $ (3+4)\times 5 = 7\times 5 = 35 $   |
|   $4$  | $ (4+4)\times 5 = 8\times 5 = 40 $   |
|   $8$  | $ (8+4)\times 5 = 12\times 5 = 60 $  |
|  $11$  | $ 75 $ |
</div>
</div>

<div class="question subsubquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

If $45$ comes out of Tom's machine what comes out of Sarah's$?$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">If $45$ comes out of Tom's machine what comes out of Sarah's$?$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the input into Tom's machine $= a$

As per the question,

$\begin{aligned}
(a + 4) \times 5 &= 45 \\\\
a + 4 &= \dfrac{45}{5} \\\\
a + 4 &= \dfrac{9 \times 5}{5} \\\\
a + 4 &= \dfrac{9 \times \cancel{5}}{\cancel{5}} \\\\
a + 4 &= 9 \\\\
a &= 9 - 4 \\\\
a &= 5 \\\\
\text{Output from Sarah's machine} &= (5 \times 5) + 4 \\\\
&= 25 + 4 \\\\
&= 29
\end{aligned}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$29$

</div>
</div>

$\begin{aligned}

5a &= 19 - 4 \\\\
5a &= 15 \\\\
a &= \dfrac{15}{5} \\\\
a &= \dfrac{3 \times 5}{5} \\\\
a &= \dfrac{3 \times \cancel{5}}{\cancel{5}} \\\\
a &= 3 \\\\
\text{Output from Tom's machine} &= (3 + 4) \times 5 \\\\
&= 7 \times 5 \\\\
&= 35
\end{aligned}$
</div>

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Let the input into Sarah's machine $= a$

a &= \dfrac{3 \times 5}{5} \\\\
a &= \dfrac{3 \times \cancel{5}}{\cancel{5}} \\\\
a &= 3 \\\\

&= 7 \times 5 \\\\
&= 35
\end{aligned}$

**Question**

When you add up two numbers you get $11$, but when you multiply the two numbers you get $28$. What are the two numbers?

</div>

$
\begin{aligned} 
a + b                         &= 11 \\\\
a \times b                    &= 28
\end{aligned}

We can easily infer the values by using trial and error. Let's find out $2$ numbers which meets the following critiera based on the equations above.

- The product of the $2$ numbers is $28$. 
- The sum of the $2$ numbers is $11$.

Factors of $28 = 1, 2, 4, 7, 14, 28$

Factor pairs of $28$ that add upto $11 = (7,4)$

| $a, b$    | $a \times b$  |    a + b          |
|:---------:|:-------------:|:-----------------:|
| $7, 4$    |   $28$        |       $11$        |

A quick check shows that $7$ and $4$ meets all the criteria above.

ABBR: 

*Note*: The two equations form a quadratic equation.

*Note*: This is a quadratic equation.

Solving quadratic equations is beyond the scope and any such equations can be easily inferred by trial and error method.


The two numbers are $4$ and $7$.

**Question**

I think of a number, double it and take away $5$. The answer is $13$. What was my number?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">I think of a number, double it and take away $5$. The answer is $13$. What was my number?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
2a - 5                                                       &= 13 \\\\
2a                                                           &= 13 + 5 \\\\
2a                                                           &= 18 \\\\
a                                                            &= \dfrac {18} {2} \\\\
a                                                            &= \dfrac {9 \times 2} {2} \\\\
a                                                            &= \dfrac {9 \times \cancel{2}} {\cancel{2}} \\\\
a                                                            &= 9
\end{aligned}
$

Number $= 9$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$9$

</div>
</div>

**Question**

$(\boxed{\phantom{9}} + 4) \times 7 = 63$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">$(\boxed{\phantom{9}} + 4) \times 7 = 63$

$
\begin{aligned}
(a + 4) \times 7 &= 63 \\\\
a + 4            &= \dfrac{63}{7} \\\\

a + 4            &= \dfrac{9 \times \cancel{7}}{\cancel{7}} \\\\
a + 4            &= 9 \\\\
a                &= 9 - 4 \\\\
a                &= 5
\end{aligned}
$

a              &= \dfrac{13 \times 2}{2} \\\\
a              &= \dfrac{13 \times \cancel{2}}{\cancel{2}} \\\\
a              &= 13
\end{aligned}
$

**Question**

$(13 - \boxed{\phantom{9}})^2 = 25$ 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">$(13 - \boxed{\phantom{9}})^2 = 25$ 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the missing number $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
(13 - a)^2      &= 25 \\\\
13 - a          &= \sqrt{25} \\\\
13 - a          &= \pm 5
\end{aligned}
$

When the root is positive,

$
\begin{aligned}
13 - a          &= 5 \\\\
a               &= 13 - 5 \\\\
a               &= 8
\end{aligned}
$

Let's solve for the negative root as well.

$
\begin{aligned}
13 - a          &= -5 \\\\
a              &= 13 + 5 \\\\
a              &= 18
\end{aligned}
$

Answer $= 8 \ \text{or} \ 18$
</div>
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

If $41$ comes out of Tom's machine what comes out of Sarah's?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">If $41$ comes out of Tom's machine what comes out of Sarah's?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the input number into Tom's machine $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
(a \times 5) + 6 &= 41 \\\\
5a &= 41 - 6 \\\\
5a &= 35 \\\\
a &= \dfrac {35} {5} \\\\
a &= \dfrac {7 \times 5} {5} \\\\
a &= \dfrac {7 \times \cancel {5}} {\cancel {5}} \\\\
a &= 7 \\\\
\text {Sarah's Output} &= (7 + 6) \times 5 \\\\
&= 13 \times 5 \\\\
&= 65
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$65$

If $55$ comes out of Sarah's machine what comes out of Tom's?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">If $55$ comes out of Sarah's machine what comes out of Tom's?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the input number into Sarah's machine $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
(a + 6) \times 5 &= 55 \\\\
a + 6 &= \dfrac {55} {5} \\\\
a + 6 &= \dfrac {11 \times 5} {5} \\\\
a + 6 &= \dfrac {11 \times \cancel {5}} {\cancel {5}} \\\\
a + 6 &= 11 \\\\
a &= 11 - 6 \\\\
a &= 5 \\\\
\text {Tom's Output} &= (5 \times 5) + 6 \\\\
&= 25 + 6 \\\\
&= 31
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Find two numbers that have a difference of $5$ and add up to $19$. 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Find two numbers that have a difference of $5$ and add up to $19$. 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the first number $= a$

Let the second number $= b$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned} 
a - b                    &= 5 \\\\
a + b                    &= 19
\end{aligned}
$

We have $2$ variables and we have $2$ equations to solve them. Lets eliminate to reduce it to just one variable.

Let's add the second equation to the first to reduce it to one variable.

$
\begin{aligned}
a - b + a + b            &= 5 + 19 \\\\
2a                       &= 24 \\\\
a                        &= \dfrac {24} {2} \\\\
a                        &= \dfrac {2 \times 12} {2} \\\\
a                        &= \dfrac {\cancel{2} \times 12} {\cancel{2}} \\\\
a                        &= 12
\end{aligned}
$

Let's substitute the value of $a$ in one of the equations.

$
\begin{aligned} 
a + b                    &= 19 \\\\
12 + b                   &= 19 \\\\
b                        &= 19 - 12 \\\\
b                        &= 7
\end{aligned}
$

Numbers are $= 12$, $7$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$12$

</div>
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$7$

</div>
</div>

<div class="tipcodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>

</code></pre>

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Let the first number $= a$

a + b                    &= 19
\end{aligned}

<emptyline>
Let's add the second equation to the first to reduce it to one variable.
<emptyline>
$
\begin{aligned}
a - b + a + b            &= 5 + 19 \\\\
2a                       &= 24 \\\\

a                        &= \dfrac {2 \times 12} {2} \\\\
a                        &= \dfrac {\cancel{2} \times 12} {\cancel{2}} \\\\
a                        &= 12
\end{aligned}
$
<emptyline>

<emptyline>
$
\begin{aligned} 
a + b                    &= 19 \\\\
12 + b                   &= 19 \\\\
b                        &= 19 - 12 \\\\
b                        &= 7
\end{aligned}
$
<emptyline>
Numbers are $= 12$, $7$

**Question**

$(8 + \boxed{\phantom{9}}) \times 5 = 85$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">$(8 + \boxed{\phantom{9}}) \times 5 = 85$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">

</div>

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the missing number $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
(8 + a) \times 5            &= 85 \\\\
(8 + a)                     &= \dfrac{85}{5} \\\\
(8 + a)                     &= \dfrac{17 \times 5}{5} \\\\
8 + a                       &= \dfrac{17 \times \cancel{5}}{\cancel{5}} \\\\
8 + a                       &= 17 \\\\
a                           &= 17 - 8 \\\\
a                           &= 9
\end{aligned}
$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Three quarters of a local tennis club are girls. There are $20$ boys in the club. How many girls are there?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Three quarters of a local tennis club are girls. There are $20$ boys in the club. How many girls are there?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the total number of children $= c$

Number of girls in the club $= \dfrac {3c} {4}$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {3c} {4} + 20                                    &= c \\\\
c - \dfrac {3c} {4}                                     &= 20 \\\\
\dfrac {4 \times c} {4} - \dfrac {3c} {4}               &= 20 \\\\
\dfrac {4c -3c} {4}                                      &= 20 \\\\
\dfrac {c} {4}                                            &= 20 \\\\
c                                                        &= 20 \times 4 \\\\
c                                                        &= 80 \\\\
\text{Number of girls}                             &= 80 - 20 \\\\
                                                         &= 60
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$60$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A ball is dropped onto a hard surface and each time it bounces, it rebounds to one third of the height from which it fell. After the second bounce it rises $9 \ \text{cm}$. How high was it initially dropped from?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A ball is dropped onto a hard surface and each time it bounces, it rebounds to one third of the height from which it fell. After the second bounce it rises $9 \ \text{cm}$. How high was it initially dropped from?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the initially height $= h$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac{1}{3} \times \dfrac{1}{3} \times h   &= 9 \\\\
\dfrac { h} {3 \times 3}                       &= 9 \\\\
h                                            &= 9 \times 3 \times 3 \\\\
h                                            &= 81 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

Initial height $= 81 \ \text{cm}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$81 \ \text{cm}$

</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Find two numbers that have a difference of $8$ and added upto $18$.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Find two numbers that have a difference of $8$ and added upto $18$.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the first number $= a$

Let the second number $= b$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned} 
a - b                    &= 8 \\\\
a + b                    &= 18
\end{aligned}
$

We have $2$ variables and we have $2$ equations to solve them. Lets eliminate to reduce it to just one variable.

Let's add the second equation to the first to reduce it to one variable.

$
\begin{aligned}
a - b + (a - b)          &= 8 + 18 \\\\
a - b + a + b            &= 26 \\\\
2a                       &= 26 \\\\
a                        &= \dfrac {26} {2} \\\\
a                        &= \dfrac {2 \times 13} {2} \\\\
a                        &= \dfrac {\cancel{2} \times 13} {\cancel{2}} \\\\
a                        &= 13
\end{aligned}
$

Let's substitute the value of $a$ in one of the equations.

$
\begin{aligned} 
a + b                    &= 18 \\\\
13 + b                   &= 18 \\\\
b                        &= 18 - 13 \\\\
b                        &= 5
\end{aligned}
$

Numbers $= 13$, $5$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$13$

</div>
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

a                                             &= 20
\end{aligned}
$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

I have forgotten the last two digits of my PIN number, but know that the first two digits are $8$ and $6$.

$8 \ 6 * *$

However,I know that my PIN number is divisible by $3, 4$ and $5$. What is my PIN number?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">I have forgotten the last two digits of my PIN number, but know that the first two digits are $8$ and $6$.
<emptyline>
$8 \ 6 * *$
<emptyline>
However,I know that my PIN number is divisible by $3, 4$ and $5$. What is my PIN number?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

LCM of $3, \ 4 \ \text{and} \ 5 = 60$

Since, Multiplying $60$ with any number will give $0$ at last digit. So, The last digit of the PIN is $0$.

$
\begin{aligned}
&= \dfrac {8700} {60} \\\\
&= \dfrac {6 \times 1450} {60} \\\\
&= \dfrac {6 \times 145 \times 10} {6 \times 10} \\\\
&= \dfrac {\cancel{6} \times 145 \times \cancel{10}} {\cancel{6} \times \cancel{10}} \\\\
&= 145
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{As the remainder is } 0, \text{Subtracting } 60 \text{ from } 8700 &= 8700 - 60 \\\\
                                                                        &= 8640 
\end{aligned}
$

The PIN number is $= 8640$
</div>
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Alternative solution

We can solve this my trial and error method using divisibility rule.

We know,

A number is divisible by $5$ if the last digit $0$ or $5$.

A number is divisible by $4$ if the last $2$ digits are divisible by $4$.

A number is divisible by $3$ if the cross addition is divisible by $3$.

Let's look at units place

$= 0$ (then only my PIN will be divisible by $4$)

Let's look at tens place

$\not 1$ (as $10$ is not divisible by $4$)

$= 2$ (as $20$ is divisible by $4$)

Let's now check if $8620$ is divisible by $3$

$= 8 + 6 + 2 + 0 = 16 \not$ divisible by $3$ 

The next multiple of $3$ would be $18$

$= 8 + 6 + 4 + 0 = 18$ 

$18$ is divisible by $3$

$40$ is divisible by $4$ and

$8640$ has $0$ at unit place, as such divisible by $5$.

My PIN number is $8640$.
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$8640$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Seven telegraph poles are equally spaced along a road. The distance between the first and the third pole is $268 \ \text{m}$. How far is it between the first and last pole?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Seven telegraph poles are equally spaced along a road. The distance between the first and the third pole is $268 \ \text{m}$. How far is it between the first and last pole?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>

</div>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the distance between two poles $= d$

The distance between the first and third pole covers $2$ gaps.

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
2d                      &= 268 \\\\
d                       &= \dfrac {268} {2} \\\\
d                       &= \dfrac {2 \times 134} {2} \\\\
d                       &= \dfrac {\cancel{2} \times 134} {\cancel{2}} \\\\
d                       &= 134 \ \text{m} \\\\
\text{Distance between 1st and 7th pole } &= 6d \\\\
                            &= 6 \times 134 \\\\
                            &= 804 \ \text{m}  
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A block of chocolate is divided between three friends. Paul gets half of it and Peter gets one third of it. Richard gets $100 \ \text{g}$ of chocolate. How heavy was the bar originally?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A block of chocolate is divided between three friends. Paul gets half of it and Peter gets one third of it. Richard gets $100 \ \text{g}$ of chocolate. How heavy was the bar originally?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the original weight of the chocolate bar $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {1} {2} \times a + \dfrac {1} {3} \times a + 100                           &= a \\\\
\dfrac {a} {2} + \dfrac {a} {3} + 100                                 &=  a \\\\
a - \dfrac {a} {2} - \dfrac {a} {3}                                                                         &= 100 \\\\
\dfrac {a \times 6} {1 \times 6} - \dfrac {a \times 3} {2 \times 3} - \dfrac {a \times 2} {3 \times 2}      &= 100 \\\\
\dfrac {6a} {6} - \dfrac {3a} {6} - \dfrac {2a} {6}                                                         &= 100 \\\\
\dfrac {6a - 3a - 2a} {6}                                                                                   &= 100 \\\\
\dfrac {a} {6}                                                                                              &= 100 \\\\
a                                                                                                           &= 100 \times 6 \\\\
a                                                                                                           &= 600 \ \text{g}
\end{aligned}
$

Answer $= 600 \ \text{g}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$600 \ \text{g}$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Sarah is $24 \ \text{years}$ old. Peter is half as old as Sarah. Mike is $\dfrac{2} {3}$ of Peter’s age.

What is their total age?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Sarah is $24 \ \text{years}$ old. Peter is half as old as Sarah. Mike is $\dfrac{2} {3}$ of Peter’s age.
<emptyline>
What is their total age?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Sarah's age} &= 24 \ \text{years} \\\\
\text{Peter's age} &= 24 \times \dfrac{1}{2} \\\\
&= \dfrac{24}{2} \\\\
&= \dfrac{2 \times 12}{2} \\\\
&= \dfrac{\cancel{2} \times 12}{\cancel{2}} \\\\
&= 12 \ \text{years} \\\\
\text{Mike's age} &= 12 \times \dfrac{2}{3} \\\\
&= \dfrac{12 \times 2}{3} \\\\
&= \dfrac{3 \times 4 \times 2}{3} \\\\
&= \dfrac{\cancel{3} \times 4 \times 2}{\cancel{3}} \\\\
&= 8 \ \text{years} \\\\
\text{Total age} &= \text{Sarah} + \text{Peter} + \text{Mike} \\\\
&= 24 + 12 + 8 \\\\
&= 36 + 8 \\\\
&= 44 \ \text{years}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$44 \ \text{years}$

</div>
</div>
<div class="workingscodeblock">
<div class="tipcodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="tipcodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Tips Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">%empty%
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="formulacodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="formulacodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Formulas Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">%empty%
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workingcodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="workingcodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Working Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Sarah's age} &= 24 \ \text{years} \\\\
\text{Peter's age} &= 24 \times \dfrac{1}{2} \\\\
&= \dfrac{24}{2} \\\\
&= \dfrac{2 \times 12}{2} \\\\
&= \dfrac{\cancel{2} \times 12}{\cancel{2}} \\\\
&= 12 \ \text{years} \\\\
\text{Mike's age} &= 12 \times \dfrac{2}{3} \\\\
&= \dfrac{12 \times 2}{3} \\\\
&= \dfrac{3 \times 4 \times 2}{3} \\\\
&= \dfrac{\cancel{3} \times 4 \times 2}{\cancel{3}} \\\\
&= 8 \ \text{years} \\\\
\text{Total age} &= \text{Sarah} + \text{Peter} + \text{Mike} \\\\
&= 24 + 12 + 8 \\\\
&= 36 + 8 \\\\
&= 44 \ \text{years}
\end{aligned}
$
</code></pre>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Find two numbers that have a difference of $6$ and add up to $14$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Find two numbers that have a difference of $6$ and add up to $14$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the first number $= a$

Let the second number $= b$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned} 
a - b                    &= 6 \\\\
a + b                    &= 14
\end{aligned}
$

We have $2$ variables and we have $2$ equations to solve them. Lets eliminate to reduce it to just one variable.

Let's add the second equation to the first to reduce it to one variable.

$
\begin{aligned}
(a - b) + (a + b)            &= 6 + 14 \\\\
2a                       &= 20 \\\\
a                        &= \dfrac {20} {2} \\\\
a                        &= \dfrac {2 \times 10} {2} \\\\
a                        &= \dfrac {\cancel{2} \times 10} {\cancel{2}} \\\\
a                        &= 10
\end{aligned}
$

Let's substitute the value of $a$ in one of the equations.

$
\begin{aligned} 
a + b                    &= 14 \\\\
10 + b                   &= 14 \\\\
b                        &= 14 - 10 \\\\
b                        &= 4
\end{aligned}
$

Numbers $= 10$, $4$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$4$

</div>

**Answer**

$10$

</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

I think of a number, divide it by $3$, then add $7$. The result is $18$. What was the number I first thought of?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">I think of a number, divide it by $3$, then add $7$. The result is $18$. What was the number I first thought of?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {a} {3} + 7                                  &= 18 \\\\
\dfrac {a} {3}                                      &= 18 - 7 \\\\
\dfrac {a} {3}                                      &= 11 \\\\
a                                                   &= 11 \times 3 \\\\
a                                                   &= 33
\end{aligned}
$

Number $= 33$
</div>
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>

a                                                   &= \dfrac {\cancel{12} \times 13} {\cancel{12}} \\\\
a                                                   &= 13
\end{aligned}
$

Missing number is $= 13$

$(7 - \boxed{\phantom{9}} ) \times 13 = 78$

<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$
\begin{aligned}
(7 - a) \times 13                                   &= 78 \\\\
7 - a                                               &= \dfrac {78} {13} \\\\
7 - a                                               &= \dfrac {6 \times 13} {13} \\\\
7 - a                                               &= \dfrac {6 \times \cancel{13}} {\cancel{13}} \\\\
7 - a                                               &= 6 \\\\
a                                                   &= 7 - 6 \\\\
a                                                   &= 1
\end{aligned}
$

Missing number is $= 1$

**Question**

Find $𝑏$ if $𝑏 * 𝑏 = 28$.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Find $𝑏$ if $𝑏 * 𝑏 = 28$.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
b * b                                                   &= 28 \\\\
(b - 3) \times b                                                   &= 28 
\end{aligned}
$

ABBR: 

*Note*: The two equations form a quadratic equation.

*Note*: This is a quadratic equation.

Solving quadratic equations is beyond the scope and any such equations can be easily inferred by trial and error method.


We can easily infer the values by using trial and error. Let's find out $2$ numbers which meets the following critiera based on the equations above.

- The product of the $2$ numbers is $28$. 
- The difference of the $2$ numbers is $3$.

Factors of $28 = 1, 2, 4, 7, 14 \ \text{and} \ \ 28$

|  $b$ |    $b - 3$    |  $(b - 3)\times b$  | $= 28$? |
| :--: | :-----------: | :-----------------: | :-----: |
|  $1$ |  $1 - 3 = -2$ | $(-2)\times 1 = -2$ |    No   |
|  $2$ |  $2 - 3 = -1$ | $(-1)\times 2 = -2$ |    No   |
|  $4$ |  $4 - 3 = 1$  |   $1\times 4 = 4$   |    No   |
|  $7$ |  $7 - 3 = 4$  |   $4\times 7 = 28$  |   Yes   |

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

I think of a number, multiply it by $5$, then subtract $3$. The result is $57$. What was the number I first thought of? 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">I think of a number, multiply it by $5$, then subtract $3$. The result is $57$. What was the number I first thought of? 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
5 \times a - 3                                      &= 57 \\\\
5a                                                  &= 57 + 3 \\\\
5a                                                  &= 60 \\\\
a                                                   &= \dfrac {60} {5} \\\\
a                                                   &= \dfrac {5 \times 12} {5} \\\\
a                                                   &= \dfrac {\cancel{5} \times 12} {\cancel{5}} \\\\
a                                                   &= 12
\end{aligned}
$

Number $= 12$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$12$

</div>
</div>

$

a                                                   &= 4
\end{aligned}
$

Missing number $= 4$

**Question**

Find $b$ if $b * b = 32$.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Find $b$ if $b * b = 32$.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">

</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
b * b                                                   &= 32 \\\\
(b + 4) \times b                                        &= 32 
\end{aligned}
$

ABBR: 

*Note*: The two equations form a quadratic equation.

*Note*: This is a quadratic equation.

Solving quadratic equations is beyond the scope and any such equations can be easily inferred by trial and error method.


We can easily infer the values by using trial and error. Let's find out $2$ numbers which meets the following critiera based on the equations above.

- The product of the $2$ numbers is $32$. 
- The difference of the $2$ numbers is $4$.

Factors of $32 = 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 \ \text{and} \ \ 32$

|  $b$ |    $b + 4$    |       $b(b + 4)$      | $= 32$? |
| :--: | :-----------: | :-------------------: | :-----: |
|  $1$ |  $1 + 4 = 5$  |    $1 \times 5 = 5$   |    No   |
|  $2$ |  $2 + 4 = 6$  |   $2 \times 6 = 12$   |    No   |
|  $4$ |  $4 + 4 = 8$  |   $4 \times 8 = 32$   |   Yes   |
|  $8$ |  $8 + 4 = 12$ |   $8 \times 12 = 96$  |    No   |
| $16$ | $16 + 4 = 20$ |  $16 \times 20 = 320$ |    No   |
| $32$ | $32 + 4 = 36$ | $32 \times 36 = 1152$ |    No   |

A quick check shows that $4$ meets the criteria above.

Answer $= 4$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$4$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Gary and Martin have some money. Martin has $\pounds 13$ more than Gary, together they have $\pounds 51$. How much money does Martin have?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Gary and Martin have some money. Martin has $\pounds 13$ more than Gary, together they have $\pounds 51$. How much money does Martin have?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the money Gary has $= a$

Money Martin has $= 13 + a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
a + 13 + a                                              &= 51 \\\\                                  
2a                                                      &= 51 - 13 \\\\
2a                                                      &= 38 \\\\
2a                                                      &= 38 \\\\
a                                                       &= \dfrac {38} {2} \\\\
a                                                       &= \dfrac {2 \times 19} {2} \\\\
a                                                       &= \dfrac {\cancel{2} \times 19} {\cancel{2}} \\\\
a                                                       &= \pounds 19 \\\\
\text{Money Gary has}                                   &= \pounds 19 \\\\
\text{Money Martin has}                                 &= 19 + 13 \\\\
                                                        &= \pounds 32
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$\pounds 32$

</div>
</div>

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">What values of $a$ makes $a * 5 = 29?$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$
\begin{aligned}
a * 5 &= 29 \\\\ 
a \times 3 + 5 &= 29 \\\\ 
3a             &= 29 - 5 \\\\ 
3a             &= 24 \\\\ 
a              &= \dfrac{24}{3} \\\\ 
a              &= \dfrac{8 \times 3}{3} \\\\ 
a              &= \dfrac{8 \times \cancel{3}}{\cancel{3}} \\\\ 
a              &= 8 
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

\end{aligned}

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

The entry prices at a theme park are: Adults $\pounds20.00$ & Children $\pounds15.00$.

A group visited the theme park and were charged $\pounds105.00$. How many adults & children were in the party? There was at least one adult.

Show all of your working clearly. 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">The entry prices at a theme park are: Adults $\pounds20.00$ & Children $\pounds15.00$.
<emptyline>
A group visited the theme park and were charged $\pounds105.00$. How many adults & children were in the party? There was at least one adult.
<emptyline>
Show all of your working clearly. 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number of adults $= a$

Let the number of children $= c$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
20a + 15c     &= 105 \\\\
5 \times (4a + 3c) &= 5 \times 21 \\\\
4a + 3c                             &= 21 \\\\
c                                   &= \dfrac{21 - 4a}{3}
\end{aligned}
$

We can easily infer the values by using trial and error. Let's find out the value of $a$ and $c$ which satisfies the condition above.

| $a$ |                $c$                | Whole number? |
| :-: | :------------------------------------------------: | :-----------: |
| $1$ |   $c = \dfrac{21 - 4\times 1}{3} = \dfrac{17}{3}$  |       No      |
| $2$ |   $c = \dfrac{21 - 4\times 2}{3} = \dfrac{13}{3}$  |       No      |
| $3$ | $c = \dfrac{21 - 4\times 3}{3} = \dfrac{9}{3} = 3$ |     Yes       |
| $4$ |   $c = \dfrac{21 - 4\times 4}{3} = \dfrac{5}{3}$   |       No      |
| $5$ |   $c = \dfrac{21 - 4\times 5}{3} = \dfrac{1}{3}$   |       No      |

A quick check shows that $a = 3$ and $c = 3$ meets all the criteria above.

Number of adults     = $3$

Number of children   = $3$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

adults $=$ $3$

</div>
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

children $=$ $3$

</div>
</div>

**Question**

$3x - 5 = 31$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">$3x - 5 = 31$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
3x - 5 &= 31 \\\\
3x     &= 31 + 5 \\\\
x      &= \dfrac {36} {3} \\\\
x      &= \dfrac {12 \times 3 } {3} \\\\
x      &= \dfrac {12 \times \cancel {3} } {\cancel{3} } \\\\
x      &= 12
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$12$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

In a box of pens, one half are black, one sixth are red and the rest are blue.  What fraction of the pens is blue?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">In a box of pens, one half are black, one sixth are red and the rest are blue.  What fraction of the pens is blue?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the total pens $= a$

Black pens $= \dfrac{a}{2}$

Red pens $= \dfrac{a}{6}$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Blue pens}                 &= a - \dfrac {a} {2} - \dfrac {a} {6}    \\\\
                                 &= \dfrac {6 \times a} {6} - \dfrac {3 \times a} {3 \times 2} - \dfrac {a} {6} \\\\
                                 &= \dfrac {6a} {6} - \dfrac {3a} {6} - \dfrac {a} {6} \\\\
                                 &= \dfrac {6a - 3a - a} {6}             \\\\
                                 &= \dfrac {2a} {6}             \\\\
                                 &= \dfrac {2 \times a} {2 \times 3} \\\\
                                 &= \dfrac {\cancel{2} \times a} {3 \times \cancel {2}} \\\\
                                 &= \dfrac {1} {3} \times a
\end{aligned}
$

Fraction of blue pens $= \dfrac{1}{3}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$\dfrac {1} {3}$

</div>
</div>
<div class="workingscodeblock">
<div class="tipcodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="tipcodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Tips Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">%empty%
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="formulacodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="formulacodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Formulas Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">%empty%
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workingcodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="workingcodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Working Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Let the total pens $= a$
<emptyline>
Black pens $= \dfrac{a}{2}$
<emptyline>
Red pens $= \dfrac{a}{6}$
<emptyline>
As per the question,
<emptyline>
$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Blue pens}                 &= a - \dfrac {a} {2} - \dfrac {a} {6}    \\\\
                                 &= \dfrac {6 \times a} {6} - \dfrac {3 \times a} {3 \times 2} - \dfrac {a} {6} \\\\
                                 &= \dfrac {6a} {6} - \dfrac {3a} {6} - \dfrac {a} {6} \\\\
                                 &= \dfrac {6a - 3a - a} {6}             \\\\
                                 &= \dfrac {2a} {6}             \\\\
                                 &= \dfrac {2 \times a} {2 \times 3} \\\\
                                 &= \dfrac {\cancel{2} \times a} {3 \times \cancel {2}} \\\\
                                 &= \dfrac {1} {3} \times a
\end{aligned}
$
<emptyline>
Fraction of blue pens $= \dfrac{1}{3}$
</code></pre>
</div>
</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

$(a \times 9) \div 6 = 6$ 

Find $a$.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">$(a \times 9) \div 6 = 6$ 
<emptyline>
Find $a$.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
(a\times 9) \div 6     &= 6 \\\\
\dfrac{9a} {6}         &= 6 \\\\
a                      &= \dfrac {6 \times 6} {9} \\\\
a                      &= \dfrac {3 \times 2 \times 3 \times 2} {3 \times 3} \\\\
a                      &= \dfrac {\cancel {3} \times 2 \times \cancel {3} \times 2} {\cancel {3} \times \cancel {3}} \\\\
a                      &= 2 \times 2 \\\\
a                      &= 4
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$4$

</div>
</div>

**Question**

$(b + 6) \times 8 = 64$

Find $b$.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">$(b + 6) \times 8 = 64$

$
\begin{aligned}
(b + 6) \times 8   &= 64 \\\\
b + 6              &= \dfrac {64} {8} \\\\
b + 6              &= \dfrac {8 \times 8} {8} \\\\
b + 6              &= \dfrac {8 \times \cancel {8} } {\cancel {8} } \\\\
b + 6              &= 8 \\\\
b                  &= 8 - 6 \\\\
b                  &= 2
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

b + 6              &= \dfrac {64} {8} \\\\
b + 6              &= \dfrac {8 \times 8} {8} \\\\
b + 6              &= \dfrac {8 \times \cancel {8} } {\cancel {8} } \\\\
b + 6              &= 8 \\\\
b                  &= 8 - 6 \\\\
b                  &= 2
\end{aligned}
$
</code></pre>
</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Seeta and Ben eat Weetabix breakfast cereal every day. They each eat more than one biscuit a day. Each Weetabix box contains $24$ biscuits. Ben eats $x$ biscuits each morning. Seeta is less hungry and only has $y$ biscuits.

$4$ days after buying a new box, there are only $4$ biscuits left in the Weetabix box.

Find $x$ and $y$.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Seeta and Ben eat Weetabix breakfast cereal every day. They each eat more than one biscuit a day. Each Weetabix box contains $24$ biscuits. Ben eats $x$ biscuits each morning. Seeta is less hungry and only has $y$ biscuits.
<emptyline>
$4$ days after buying a new box, there are only $4$ biscuits left in the Weetabix box.
<emptyline>
Find $x$ and $y$.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Total biscuits eaten in $4$ days $= 24 - 4 = 20$

Total biscuits eaten per day $= x + y$

As per the question,

$\begin{aligned}
4 \times (x + y) &= 20 \\\\
x + y            &= \dfrac{20}{4} \\\\
x + y            &= \dfrac{5 \times 4}{4} \\\\
x + y            &= \dfrac{5 \times \cancel{4}}{\cancel{4}} \\\\
x + y            &= 5
\end{aligned}$

Integer pairs that sum to $5$ are $(1, 4)$ and $(2, 3)$.

We are given that each eats more than one biscuit, so $x > 1$ and $y > 1$. Since $x, y > 1$, we can eliminate the pair $(1, 4)$.

The pair must be $(2, 3)$.

Seeta is less hungry than Ben, so $x > y$.

Therefore, $x = 3$ and $y = 2$.
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$x$ $=$ $3$

</div>
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$y$ $=$ $2$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

When freezing, water increases its volume by $\dfrac {1} {11}$. By what part of its volume will ice decrease when it melts and turns back into water?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">When freezing, water increases its volume by $\dfrac {1} {11}$. By what part of its volume will ice decrease when it melts and turns back into water?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the original volume of water $= v$

The volume of ice formed is:

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Volume of ice} &= v + \dfrac{v}{11} \\\\
&= \dfrac{11v}{11} + \dfrac{v}{11} \\\\
&= \dfrac{12v}{11}
\end{aligned}
$

When the ice melts, it returns to the original volume of water $v$.
The decrease in volume is:

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Decrease} &= \dfrac{12v}{11} - v \\\\
&= \dfrac{12v}{11} - \dfrac{11v}{11} \\\\
&= \dfrac{12v - 11v}{11} \\\\
&= \dfrac{v}{11}
\end{aligned}
$

We need to find this decrease as a part of the ice's volume.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Fraction decrease} &= \dfrac{\text{Decrease in volume}}{\text{Volume of ice}} \\\\
&= \dfrac{v}{11} \div \dfrac{12v}{11} \\\\
&= \dfrac{v}{11} \times \dfrac{11}{12v} \\\\
&= \dfrac{v \times 11}{11 \times 12 \times v} \\\\
&= \dfrac{\cancel{v} \times \cancel{11}}{\cancel{11} \times 12 \times \cancel{v}} \\\\
&= \dfrac{1}{12}
\end{aligned}
$

Answer $= \dfrac{1}{12}$
</div>
</div>

$\dfrac {1} {12}$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Find three consecutive numbers with a sum of $36$.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Find three consecutive numbers with a sum of $36$.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the first number $= a$

Second number $= a + 1$

Third number $= a + 2$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
a + (a+1) + (a+2)  &= 36 \\\\
3a + 3             &= 36 \\\\
3a                 &= 36 - 3 \\\\
3a                 &= 33 \\\\
a                  &= \dfrac {33} {3} \\\\
a                  &= \dfrac {3 \times 11} {3} \\\\
a                  &= \dfrac {\cancel{3} \times 11} {\cancel{3}} \\\\
a                  &= 11 \\\\
\text {1st number} 				 &= 11 \\\\
\text {2nd number} &= 11 + 1 \\\\
									 &= 12 \\\\
\text {3rd number}  &= 12 + 1 \\\\
									 &= 13
\end{aligned}
$

Numbers $= 11$, $12$, $13$
</div>
</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Find three consecutive numbers which give $336$ when multiplied together.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Find three consecutive numbers which give $336$ when multiplied together.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the consecutive numbers $= n$, $n+1$, $n+2$

As per the question,

$n \times (n+1) \times (n+2) = 336$

We can easily infer the values by using trial and error.

We try sensible values of $n$. For example, $1 \times 2 \times 3 = 6$ is too small and $8 \times 9 \times 10 = 720$ is too big.

| $n$ |   $ n(n+1)(n+2)$            | Equals $336$? |
| :-: | :-------------------------: | :-----------: |
| $4$ | $4 \times 5 \times 6 = 120$ |       No      |
| $5$ | $5 \times 6 \times 7 = 210$ |       No      |
| $6$ | $6 \times 7 \times 8 = 336$ |       Yes     |
| $7$ | $7 \times 8 \times 9 = 504$ |       No      |

A quick check shows that $6$, $7$ and $8$ meets the criteria above.

Numbers $= 6$, $7$, $8$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$6$

</div>
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$7$

</div>
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$8$

</div>

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Let the consecutive numbers $= n$, $n+1$, $n+2$

<emptyline>

<emptyline>
We can easily infer the values by using trial and error.
<emptyline>
We try sensible values of $n$. For example, $1 \times 2 \times 3 = 6$ is too small and $8 \times 9 \times 10 = 720$ is too big.
<emptyline>
| $n$ |   $ n(n+1)(n+2)$            | Equals $336$? |
| :-: | :-------------------------: | :-----------: |
| $4$ | $4 \times 5 \times 6 = 120$ |       No      |
| $5$ | $5 \times 6 \times 7 = 210$ |       No      |
| $6$ | $6 \times 7 \times 8 = 336$ |       Yes     |
| $7$ | $7 \times 8 \times 9 = 504$ |       No      |
<emptyline>

<emptyline>
Numbers $= 6$, $7$, $8$

**Question**

$(x \times 18) \div 9 = 16$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">$(x \times 18) \div 9 = 16$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>
</div>
