<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
(x \times 18) \div 9                                &= 16 \\\\
(x \times 18) \times \dfrac{1}{9}                   &= 16 \\\\
\dfrac {18x}{9}                                     &= 16 \\\\
x                                                   &= \dfrac {16 \times 9} {18} \\\\
x                                                   &= \dfrac {2 \times 8 \times 9} {2 \times 9} \\\\
x                                                   &= \dfrac {\cancel {2} \times 8 \times \cancel {9}} {\cancel {2} \times \cancel {9}} \\\\
x                                                   &= 8
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

$(x + 12) \times 4 + 2 = 62$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">$(x + 12) \times 4 + 2 = 62$
</code></pre>

<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
(x + 12) \times 4 + 2    &= 62 \\\\
(x + 12) \times 4        &= 62 - 2\\\\
(x + 12) \times 4        &= 60 \\\\
x + 12                   &= \dfrac {60}{4} \\\\
x + 12                   &= \dfrac {60}{4} \\\\
x + 12                   &= \dfrac {15 \times 4} {4} \\\\
x + 12                   &= \dfrac {15 \times \cancel {4} } {\cancel {4} } \\\\
x + 12                   &= 15 \\\\
x                        &= 15 - 12 \\\\
x                        &= 3
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">$5x + 1 = 2x + 7$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>

<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
5x + 1    &= 2x + 7 \\\\
5x - 2x   &= 7 - 1 \\\\
3x        &= 6 \\\\
x         &= \dfrac {6} {3} \\\\
x         &= \dfrac{2 \times \cancel {3} }{\cancel {3} } \\\\
x         &= 2
\end{aligned}

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Albert, Brian and Charlie are dogs. Albert and Brian weigh $22 \ \text{kg}$ together. Brian and Charlie weigh $20 \ \text{kg}$ together. All three dogs weigh $30 \ \text{kg}$. How much does each dog weigh?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Albert, Brian and Charlie are dogs. Albert and Brian weigh $22 \ \text{kg}$ together. Brian and Charlie weigh $20 \ \text{kg}$ together. All three dogs weigh $30 \ \text{kg}$. How much does each dog weigh?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the weight of Albert $= a$

Let the weight of Brian $= b$

Let the weight of Charlie $= c$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
a + b &= 22 \\\\
b + c &= 20 \\\\
a + b + c &= 30
\end{aligned}
$

Let's substitute the value of $a+b$ from the first equation into the third equation:

$
\begin{aligned}
(a + b) + c &= 30 \\\\
22 + c &= 30 \\\\
c &= 30 - 22 \\\\
c &= 8
\end{aligned}
$

Let's substitute the value of $c$ into the second equation to find $b$:

$
\begin{aligned}
b + c &= 20 \\\\
b + 8 &= 20 \\\\
b &= 20 - 8 \\\\
b &= 12
\end{aligned}
$

Let's substitute the value of $b$ into the first equation to find $a$:

$
\begin{aligned}
a + b &= 22 \\\\
a + 12 &= 22 \\\\
a &= 22 - 12 \\\\
a &= 10
\end{aligned}
$

Albert $= 10 \ \text{kg}$

Brian $= 12 \ \text{kg}$

Charlie $= 8 \ \text{kg}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

Albert $=$ $10 \ \text{kg}$

</div>
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

Brian $=$ $12 \ \text{kg}$

</div>
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

Charlie $=$ $8 \ \text{kg}$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Tim, David and Alison are given some money by their grandfather. Tim gets twice as much as David and three times as much as Alison. If they get $\pounds 49.50$ in total, how much do they each get?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Tim, David and Alison are given some money by their grandfather. Tim gets twice as much as David and three times as much as Alison. If they get $\pounds 49.50$ in total, how much do they each get?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the money Alison gets $= a$

Money Tim gets $= 3a$

Money David gets $= \dfrac{1}{2} \times 3a = 1.5a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
3a + 1.5a + a                 &= 49.50 \\\\
5.5a                          &= 49.50 \\\\
a                             &= \dfrac{49.50}{5.5} \\\\
a                             &= \dfrac{49.50 \times 10}{5.5 \times 10} \\\\
a                             &= \dfrac{495}{55} \\\\
a                             &= \dfrac{5 \times 11 \times 9}{5 \times 11} \\\\
a                             &= \dfrac{\cancel{5} \times \cancel{11} \times 9}{\cancel{5} \times \cancel{11}} \\\\
a                             &= 9 \\\\
\text{Money Alison gets}      &= \pounds 9 \\\\
\text{Money Tim gets}         &= 3 \times 9 \\\\
                              &= \pounds 27 \\\\
\text{Money David gets}       &= 1.5 \times 9 \\\\
                              &= \pounds 13.50
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

Tom $=$ $\pounds27$

</div>
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

David $=$ $\pounds13.5$

</div>
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

Alison $=$ $\pounds9$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A ball is dropped from a height of $10 \ \text{metres}$. It bounces off the floor to half its original height. How far will the ball have travelled when it reaches the floor for the second time?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A ball is dropped from a height of $10 \ \text{metres}$. It bounces off the floor to half its original height. How far will the ball have travelled when it reaches the floor for the second time?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Total distance} &= \text{Initial Drop} + \text{Bounce Up} + \text{Bounce Down} \\\\
&= 10 + \dfrac{1}{2} \times 10 + \dfrac{1}{2} \times 10 \\\\
&= 10 + 5 + 5 \\\\
&= 20 \ \text{m}
\end{aligned}
$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Two numbers have a sum of $87$. The larger of the numbers is twice the smaller. What are the two numbers?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Two numbers have a sum of $87$. The larger of the numbers is twice the smaller. What are the two numbers?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the smaller number $= a$

Larger number $= 2a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
a + 2a                      &= 87 \\\\
3a                          &= 87 \\\\
a                           &= \dfrac {87} {3} \\\\
a                           &= \dfrac {29 \times 3} {3} \\\\
a                           &= \dfrac {29 \times \cancel {3}} {\cancel {3}} \\\\
a                           &= 29 \\\\
\text{Smaller number}       &= 29 \\\\
\text{Larger number}        &= 2 \times 29 \\\\
                            &= 58
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$29$

\end{aligned}

\end{aligned}

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Gavin spends $\pounds 4.90$ on two items in a shop. One item cost $40 \ \text{p}$ more than the other.  How much did each item cost?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Gavin spends $\pounds 4.90$ on two items in a shop. One item cost $40 \ \text{p}$ more than the other.  How much did each item cost?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR: It is really important to use the right units in calculations and convert where required.
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the cost of the cheaper item (in pence) $= c$ 

Cost of the other item (in pence) $= c + 40$ 

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
c + (c + 40)            &= 4.90 \times 100 \\\\
2c + 40                 &= 490 \\\\
2c                      &= 490 - 40 \\\\
2c                      &= 450 \\\\
c                       &= \dfrac {450} {2} \\\\
c                       &= \dfrac {225 \times 2} {2} \\\\
c                       &= \dfrac {225 \times \cancel{2}} {\cancel {2}} \\\\
c                       &= 225 \ \text{p}  \\\\
                        &= \pounds 2.25 \\\\
\text {Cost of other item} &= 225 + 40 \\\\
                        &= 265 \ \text{p} \\\\
                        &= \pounds 2.65
\end{aligned}
$

Costs $= \pounds 2.25$ and $\pounds 2.65$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$$\pounds 2.25$

</div>
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$\pounds 2.65$

</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

In the sum below the letters $J, M$ and $C$ represent three different non-zero digits.

What is the value of $J + M + C \text{?}$

$
\begin{array}{cccc}
      & &J  &J \\
{}+   & &M  &M \\
{}+   & &C  &C \\
\hline
      &J  &M  &C \\ 
\end{array}
$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">In the sum below the letters $J, M$ and $C$ represent three different non-zero digits.
<emptyline>
What is the value of $J + M + C \text{?}$
<emptyline>
$
\begin{array}{cccc}
      & &J  &J \\
{}+   & &M  &M \\
{}+   & &C  &C \\
\hline
      &J  &M  &C \\ 
\end{array}
$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

JJ, MM, CC are all multiples of $11$

If you add 3 2.digit numbers as in question then the highest number achieved is 

$
\begin{array}{cccccccccccccc}
       &    & 9     & 9  \\
       &    & 8     & 8  \\
{}+    &    & 7     & 7 \\
\hline
       & 2  & 6     & 4
\end{array}
$

So, the largest value of $J$ can be $2$ or smallest value $1$

Now let's consider the Units places.

$J + M + C = C$, i.e. $J+M$ must add to $10$, then only $J+M+C$ will result in $C$ at untis place. 

Now refer to the Tens places, which has $1$ as carry over from sum of units places and $J + M = 10$ or $J + M$ will have $0$ in unit place.

$
\begin{aligned}
1 + J + M + C &= M \\
1 + 0 + C &= M \\
1 + C = M
\end{aligned}
$

To summarise the assumptions above: 

$
\begin{aligned}
J = 1 \text {\ or,} \\
J = 2 \\
J + M & = 10 \\
1 + C = M
\end{aligned}
$

Now let's substitute our assumptions

Assumption J = 1

$
\begin{aligned}
J + M &= 10 \\
1 + M &= 10 \\
    M &= 10 - 1  \\
      &= 9 \\
C + 1 &= M\\
C &= 9 -1 \\
  &= 8
\end{aligned}
$

If J is $1$, M is $9$ and C is $8$

$
\begin{array}{cccccccccccccc}
       &    & 1     & 1  \\
       &    & 9     & 9  \\
{}+    &    & 8     & 8 \\
\hline
       & 1  & 9     & 8
\end{array}
$

Assumption J = 2

$
\begin{aligned}
J + M &= 10 \\
2 + M &= 10 \\
    M &= 10 - 2  \\
      &= 8 \\
C + 1 &= M\\
    C &= 8 -1 \\
      &= 7
\end{aligned}
$

If J is $2$, M is $8$ and C is $7$

$
\begin{array}{cccccccccccccc}
       &    & 2     & 2  \\
       &    & 8     & 8  \\
{}+    &    & 7     & 7 \\
\hline
       & 2  & 8     & 7
\end{array}
$
</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Michelle has the same number of $10$p and $50$p coins. The total value of the coins is $\pounds 9$. How many of each coin does she have?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Michelle has the same number of $10$p and $50$p coins. The total value of the coins is $\pounds 9$. How many of each coin does she have?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR: It is really important to use the right units in calculations and convert where required.
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number of $10 \ \text{p}$ coins $= c$

Number of $50 \ \text{p}$ coins $= c$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
10\ \text{p} \times c + 50\ \text{p} \times c         &= \pounds9 \\\\
10\ \text{p} \times c + 50\ \text{p} \times c         &= 900 \ \text{p} \\\\
10c + 50c                         				  &= 900\\\\
60c                               				  &= 900 \\\\
c                                 				  &= \dfrac {900} {60} \\\\
c                                 				  &= \dfrac {15 \times 60 }{60} \\\\
c                                 				  &= \dfrac {15 \times \cancel {60} } {\cancel {60}} \\\\
c                                 				  &= 15
\end{aligned}
$

Number of $10 \ \text{p}$ coins $= 15$

Number of $50 \ \text{p}$ coins $= 15$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$10 \ \text{p}$ $=$ $15$ coins

</div>
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$50 \ \text{p}$ $=$ $15$ coins

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Dini thought of a number. She doubled this number and added $10$ to give the result $52$. What number did Dini think of?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Dini thought of a number. She doubled this number and added $10$ to give the result $52$. What number did Dini think of?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number $=a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
2a + 10           &= 52 \\\\
2a                &= 52 - 10 \\\\
2a                &= 42 \\\\
a                 &= \dfrac {42} {2} \\\\
a                 &= \dfrac {21 \times 2} {2} \\\\
a                 &= \dfrac {21 \times \cancel {2}} {\cancel {2}} \\\\
a                 &= 21
\end{aligned}
$

Number $= 21$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$21$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Rex has $80$ books altogether. They are arranged on three shelves. If Rex moved seven books from the top shelf to the middle shelf and took eight books away from the bottom shelf, there would be an equal number of books on each shelf. 

How many books are on the middle shelf originally?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Rex has $80$ books altogether. They are arranged on three shelves. If Rex moved seven books from the top shelf to the middle shelf and took eight books away from the bottom shelf, there would be an equal number of books on each shelf. 
<emptyline>
How many books are on the middle shelf originally?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number of books on each shelf finally $= a$

Original number of books on top shelf $= a + 7$ (since it gave away $7$ books)

Original number of books on middle shelf $= a - 7$ (since it received $7$ books)

Original number of books on bottom shelf $= a + 8$ (since $8$ books were taken away)

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
(a + 7) + (a - 7) + (a + 8) &= 80 \\\\
3a + 8 &= 80 \\\\
3a &= 80 - 8 \\\\
3a &= 72 \\\\
a &= \dfrac {72} {3} \\\\
a &= \dfrac {24 \times 3} {3} \\\\
a &= \dfrac {24 \times \cancel{3}} {\cancel{3}} \\\\
a &= 24 \\\\
\text{Original book in middle} &= a - 7 \\\\
&= 24 - 7 \\\\
&= 17
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$17$

</div>
</div>
<div class="workingscodeblock">
<div class="tipcodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="tipcodeblock_title">

</div>

</div>
<div class="formulacodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="formulacodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Formulas Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">%empty%
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workingcodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="workingcodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Working Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Let the number of books on each shelf finally $= a$
<emptyline>
Original number of books on top shelf $= a + 7$ (since it gave away $7$ books)
<emptyline>
Original number of books on middle shelf $= a - 7$ (since it received $7$ books)
<emptyline>
Original number of books on bottom shelf $= a + 8$ (since $8$ books were taken away)
<emptyline>
As per the question,
<emptyline>
$
\begin{aligned}
(a + 7) + (a - 7) + (a + 8) &= 80 \\\\
3a + 8 &= 80 \\\\
3a &= 80 - 8 \\\\
3a &= 72 \\\\
a &= \dfrac {72} {3} \\\\
a &= \dfrac {24 \times 3} {3} \\\\
a &= \dfrac {24 \times \cancel{3}} {\cancel{3}} \\\\
a &= 24 \\\\
\text{Original book in middle} &= a - 7 \\\\
&= 24 - 7 \\\\
&= 17
\end{aligned}
$
</code></pre>
</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A book costs $\pounds 3.40$ and a magazine costs $\pounds 1.60$. Clara spends exactly $\pounds 23$ on books and magazines. 

How many magazines does she buy?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A book costs $\pounds 3.40$ and a magazine costs $\pounds 1.60$. Clara spends exactly $\pounds 23$ on books and magazines. 
<emptyline>
How many magazines does she buy?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR: It is really important to use the right units in calculations and convert where required.
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Lets convert all the costs in pence.

Let the number of books $= b$

Let the number of magazines $= m$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
340b + 160m &= 2300 \\\\
\dfrac {340b + 160m} {20} &= \dfrac {2300} {20} \\\\
17b + 8m &= 115 \\\\
m &= \dfrac {115 - 17b} {8}
\end{aligned}
$

We can easily infer the values by using trial and error. 

Since $b$ and $m$ represent the number of items, they must be whole numbers.

| $b$ (books) |      $m = \dfrac{115 - 17b}{8}$               | $m$ whole? |
|:-----------:|:-------------------------------------------:|:----------:|
| $1$         | $m = \dfrac{115 - 17 \times 1}{8} = \dfrac{98} {8} = 12.25$   | No         |
| $2$         | $m = \dfrac{115 - 17 \times 2}{8} = \dfrac{81} {8} = 10.125$  | No         |
| $3$         | $m = \dfrac{115 - 17 \times 3}{8} = \dfrac{64} {8} = 8$       | Yes      |

A quick check shows that $b = 3$ and $m = 8$ meets the criteria above.

Number of magazines $= 8$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$8$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

The sum of three different primes is $16$. What are the three numbers?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">The sum of three different primes is $16$. What are the three numbers?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR: Prime numbers between $1$ and $20= 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19$
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

The sum of the three prime numbers is $16$, which is an even number.

Since the sum of three odd numbers is always odd, one of the prime numbers must be even. The only even prime number is $2$.

Let the three different primes be $= 2, a, b$.

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
2 + a + b &= 16 \\\\
a + b &= 16 - 2 \\\\
a + b &= 14 \\\\
b &= 14 - a
\end{aligned}
$

We can easily infer the values by using trial and error. 

We need to find two different primes $a$ and $b$ that add up to $14$

| $a$ | $b = 14 - a$ | Valid? |
| :-: | :-: | :--------------------: |
| $3$ | $14 -3 = 11$ | Yes |
| $5$ | $14 - 5 = 9$ | No |
| $7$ | $14 - 7 = 7$ | No (must be different) |

Prime numbers $= 2, 3, 11$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$2, 3, 11$

</div>
</div>
<div class="workingscodeblock">
<div class="tipcodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</code></pre>

</code></pre>
</div>

</div>

<emptyline>
Since the sum of three odd numbers is always odd, one of the prime numbers must be even. The only even prime number is $2$.
<emptyline>

<emptyline>

<emptyline>
$

a + b &= 16 - 2 \\\\
a + b &= 14 \\\\
b &= 14 - a
\end{aligned}
$

<emptyline>

</code></pre>

<div class="answers">

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Archie thinks of a number. Five sixths of the number is $60$. What is three quarters of the number?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Archie thinks of a number. Five sixths of the number is $60$. What is three quarters of the number?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac{5}{6} \times a         &= 60 \\\\
\dfrac{5 \times a}{6}         &= 60 \\\\
a                             &= \dfrac {60 \times 6} {5} \\\\
a                             &= \dfrac {5 \times 12 \times 6} {5} \\\\
a                             &= \dfrac {\cancel {5} \times 12 \times 6} {\cancel {5}} \\\\
a                             &= 72 \\\\
\dfrac {3} {4} \times a       &= \dfrac {3} {4} \times 72 \\\\
                              &= \dfrac {3 \times 72} {4} \\\\
                              &= \dfrac {3 \times 4 \times 18} {4} \\\\
                              &= \dfrac {3 \times \cancel {4} \times 18} {\cancel {4}} \\\\
                              &= 3 \times 18 \\\\
                              &= 54
\end{aligned}
$

Answer $= 54$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$54$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

The snowfall on Tuesday was $5 \ \text{cm}$ less than on Monday. On Wednesday twice as much snow fell than on Tuesday. In fact, $30 \ \text{cm}$ of snow fell on Wednesday. How much snow fell on Monday?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">The snowfall on Tuesday was $5 \ \text{cm}$ less than on Monday. On Wednesday twice as much snow fell than on Tuesday. In fact, $30 \ \text{cm}$ of snow fell on Wednesday. How much snow fell on Monday?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the snowfall on Monday $= m$

Snowfall on Tuesday $= m - 5$

Snowfall on Wednesday $= 2 \times (m - 5)$

As per the question,

$\begin{aligned}
2 \times (m - 5) &= 30 \\\\
m - 5 &= \dfrac{30}{2} \\\\
m - 5 &= \dfrac{2 \times 15}{2} \\\\
m - 5 &= \dfrac{\cancel{2} \times 15}{\cancel{2}} \\\\
m - 5 &= 15 \\\\
m &= 15 + 5 \\\\
m &= 20 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}$

Snowfall on Monday $= 20 \ \text{cm}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$20 \ \text{cm}$

</div>
</div>

\end{aligned}

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
a \times 6 -7                     &= 41 \\\\
a \times 6                        &= 41 + 7 \\\\
a \times 6                        &= 48 \\\\
a                                 &= \dfrac{48} {6} \\\\
a                                 &= \dfrac{6 \times 8} {6} \\\\
a                                 &= \dfrac{\cancel 6 \times 8} {\cancel 6} \\\\
a                                 &= 8
\end{aligned}
$

Number $= 8$
</div>

<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

a           &= 9
\end{aligned}

**Question**

If she works out $b \times 4 + 4$ she gets $4$.
What is the value of $b$?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">If she works out $b \times 4 + 4$ she gets $4$.
What is the value of $b$?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR: Using BIDMAS
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
b \times 4 + 4    &= 4 \\\\
b \div 4 - 4      &= 4 \\\\
b \div 4          &= 4 + 4 \\\\
\dfrac{b}{4}      &= 8 \\\\
b                 &= 8 \times 4 \\\\
b                 &= 32
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$32$

**Question**

The rule  $a * b$ means $a \times a + b \times b$.

That is, you multiply the first number by itself, multiply the second number by itself and then add the answers together.

For example, 

$
\begin{aligned}
2 * 3 &= 2 \times 2 + 3 \times 3 \\\\
      &= 4          + 9          \\\\
      &= 13     
\end{aligned}
$

And

$
\begin{aligned}
1 * 2 &= 1 \times 1 + 2 \times 2 \\\\
      &= 1          + 4          \\\\
      &= 5     
\end{aligned}
$

</div>

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<div class="workings">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
a * 1                         &= 65 \\\\
a \times a + 1 \times 1       &= 65 \\\\
a ^ 2 + 1                     &= 65 \\\\
a ^ 2                         &= 65 - 1 \\\\
a ^ 2                         &= 64 \\\\
a                             &= \sqrt {64} \\\\
a                             &= 8
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

**Question**

A rule for numbers is to add $12$ and divide the answer by $2$.

For example if you start with $10$ you add $12$ and get $22$ and then you divide by $2$ to get $11$.

So applying the rule to the number $10$ you get the answer $11$. 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

&= 21
\end{aligned}
$

\end{aligned}$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

There is a number of coins on a table. One quarter of them are showing heads. If I turn over two more coins to show heads then one third of the coins now show heads. How many coins are on the table?  

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">There is a number of coins on a table. One quarter of them are showing heads. If I turn over two more coins to show heads then one third of the coins now show heads. How many coins are on the table?  
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the total number of coins $= c$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {c} {4} + 2                                                          &= \dfrac {c} {3} \\\\ 
\dfrac {c} {3} - \dfrac {c} {4}                                             &= 2 \\\\
\dfrac {c \times 4} {3 \times 4} - \dfrac {c \times 3} {4 \times 3}         &= 2 \\\\
\dfrac {4c} {12} - \dfrac {3c} {12}                                         &= 2 \\\\
\dfrac {4c - 3c} {12}                                                       &= 2 \\\\
\dfrac {c} {12}                                                             &= 2 \\\\
c                                                                           &= 2 \times 12 \\\\
c                                                                           &= 24
\end{aligned}
$

Number of coins $= 24$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$24$

</div>
</div>

<div class="tipcodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Let the total number of coins $= c$
<emptyline>
As per the question,
<emptyline>
$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {c} {4} + 2                                                          &= \dfrac {c} {3} \\\\ 
\dfrac {c} {3} - \dfrac {c} {4}                                             &= 2 \\\\
\dfrac {c \times 4} {3 \times 4} - \dfrac {c \times 3} {4 \times 3}         &= 2 \\\\
\dfrac {4c} {12} - \dfrac {3c} {12}                                         &= 2 \\\\
\dfrac {4c - 3c} {12}                                                       &= 2 \\\\
\dfrac {c} {12}                                                             &= 2 \\\\
c                                                                           &= 2 \times 12 \\\\
c                                                                           &= 24
\end{aligned}
$
<emptyline>
Number of coins $= 24$
</code></pre>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

One quarter of the people at a party are men, a half are girls, one sixth are women, and there are five boys. How many people were at the party? 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">One quarter of the people at a party are men, a half are girls, one sixth are women, and there are five boys. How many people were at the party? 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number of people in the party $= a$

Number of men in the party $= \dfrac {a} {4}$

Number of girls in the party $= \dfrac {a} {2}$

Number of women in the party $= \dfrac {a} {6}$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {a} {4} + \dfrac {a} {2} + \dfrac {a} {6} + 5                                                                                            &= a \\\\
a - \dfrac {a} {4} - \dfrac {a} {2} - \dfrac {a}{6}                                                                                             &= 5 \\\\
\dfrac{a \times 12}{12} - \dfrac {a \times 3} {4 \times 3} - \dfrac {a \times 6} {2 \times 6} - \dfrac {a \times 2}{6 \times 2}        &= 5 \\\\
\dfrac{12a}{12} - \dfrac {3a} {12} - \dfrac {6a} {12} - \dfrac {2a}{12}                                                                         &= 5 \\\\
\dfrac{12a - 3a - 6a - 2a}{12}                                                                                                                  &= 5 \\\\
\dfrac{9a - 6a - 2a}{12}                                                                                                                        &= 5 \\\\
\dfrac{3a - 2a}{12}                                                                                                                             &= 5 \\\\
\dfrac{a}{12}                                                                                                                                   &= 5 \\\\
a                                                                                                                                               &= 5 \times 12 \\\\
a                                                                                                                                               &= 60
\end{aligned}
$

Number of people $= 60$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$60$

**Question**

The rule $a * b$ means $(a \times a) + (b \times b)$
 
That is, you multiply the first number by the first number, the second number by the second number and then you add your answers together.

For example, 

$
\begin{aligned}
6 * 4 &= (6 \times 6) + (4 \times 4) \\
      &= 36           + 16           \\
      &= 52     
\end{aligned}
$

<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
a * 8                         &= 208 \\\\
(a \times a) + (8 \times 8)   &= 208 \\\\
a^2 + 64                      &= 208 \\\\
a^2                           &= 208 - 64 \\\\
a^2                           &= 144 \\\\
a                             &= \sqrt {144} \\\\
a                             &= 12
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

**Question**

$b * 2 = 4b$. Work out the value of $b$.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">$b * 2 = 4b$. Work out the value of $b$.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">

</div>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
b * 2                                     &= 4b \\\\
(b \times b) + (2 \times 2)               &= 4b \\\\
b^2 + 4                                   &= 4b \\\\
b^2 - 4b + 4                              &= 0
\end{aligned}
$

ABBR: 

*Note*: The two equations form a quadratic equation.

*Note*: This is a quadratic equation.

$b = 2$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

$\dfrac {3} {8}$  of a number is $27$. What is $\dfrac {1} {2}$ of the number? 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">$\dfrac {3} {8}$  of a number is $27$. What is $\dfrac {1} {2}$ of the number? 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {3} {8} \times a             &= 27 \\\\
a                                   &= \dfrac {27 \times 8} {3} \\\\
a                                   &= \dfrac {3 \times 9 \times 8} {3} \\\\
a                                   &= \dfrac {\cancel {3} \times 9 \times 8} {\cancel {3}} \\\\
a                                   &= 9 \times 8 \\\\
a                                   &= 72 \\\\
\dfrac {1} {2} \times a             &= \dfrac {1} {2} \times 72 \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {72} {2} \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {36 \times 2} {2} \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {36 \times \cancel {2}} {\cancel {2}} \\\\
                                    &= 36
\end{aligned}
$

Answer $= 36$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$36$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

I am thinking of a number less than $50$. When I divide my number by $7$ I get a remainder of $3$. When I divide my number by $5$ I get a remainder of $2$. What is my number? 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">I am thinking of a number less than $50$. When I divide my number by $7$ I get a remainder of $3$. When I divide my number by $5$ I get a remainder of $2$. What is my number? 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number $= 7n + 3$ (since when divided by $7$ leaves remainder $3$)

As per the question, $(7n + 1)$ must be divisible by $5$, because the number leaves a remainder of $2$ when divided by $5$.

We can easily infer the values by using trial and error.

|$n$|  $7n + 1$              | Divisible by $5$|
|:-:|:----------------------:|:---------------:|
|$1$| $7 \times 1 + 1 = 8$   |        No       |
|$2$| $7 \times 2 + 1 = 15$  |        Yes      |
|$3$| $7 \times 3 + 1 = 22$  |        No       |
|$4$| $7 \times 4 + 1 = 29$  |        No       |
|$5$| $7 \times 5 + 1 = 36$  |        No       |
|$6$| $7 \times 6 + 1 = 43$  |        No       |

A quick check shows that $n = 2$ meets the criteria above.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number} &= 7 \times 2 + 3 \\\\
              &= 14 + 3 \\\\
              &= 17
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$17$

</div>
</div>
<div class="workingscodeblock">
<div class="tipcodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="tipcodeblock_title">

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Let the number $= 7n + 3$ (since when divided by $7$ leaves remainder $3$)
<emptyline>
As per the question, $(7n + 1)$ must be divisible by $5$, because the number leaves a remainder of $2$ when divided by $5$.
<emptyline>
We can easily infer the values by using trial and error.
<emptyline>
|$n$|  $7n + 1$              | Divisible by $5$|
|:-:|:----------------------:|:---------------:|
|$1$| $7 \times 1 + 1 = 8$   |        No       |
|$2$| $7 \times 2 + 1 = 15$  |        Yes      |
|$3$| $7 \times 3 + 1 = 22$  |        No       |
|$4$| $7 \times 4 + 1 = 29$  |        No       |
|$5$| $7 \times 5 + 1 = 36$  |        No       |
|$6$| $7 \times 6 + 1 = 43$  |        No       |
<emptyline>
A quick check shows that $n = 2$ meets the criteria above.
<emptyline>
$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number} &= 7 \times 2 + 3 \\\\
              &= 14 + 3 \\\\
              &= 17
\end{aligned}
$
</code></pre>

A quick check shows $2$ and $9$ meets the criteria above.

Numbers $= 2$, $9$

\end{aligned}

Time $= 4.5 \ \text {hours}$

**Question**

In a particular kind of arithmetic  $a \circ b$ means multiply $a$ by itself and add the result to the answer you get if you multiply $b$ by itself.

So, for example

$
\begin{aligned} 
&= 3 \circ 5 \\\\
&= 3 \times 3 + 5 \times 5 \\\\
&= 9 + 25 \\\\
&= 34
\end{aligned}
$

Work out $\dfrac {1} {2} \circ  \dfrac {1} {2}$         

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</code></pre>

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
&= \dfrac {1} {2} \circ \dfrac {1} {2} \\\\
&= \dfrac {1} {2} \times \dfrac {1} {2} + \dfrac {1} {2} \times \dfrac {1} {2} \\\\

&= \dfrac {1 + 1} {4} \\\\
&= \dfrac {2} {4} \\\\
&= \dfrac {2} {2 \times 2} \\\\
&= \dfrac {\cancel{2}} {\cancel{2} \times 2} \\\\
&= \dfrac {1} {2}
\end{aligned}
$

**Question**

Find a positive value of $c$ that works in the following:

$c \circ c = 50$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Find a positive value of $c$ that works in the following:
<emptyline>

</code></pre>

<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned} 
c \circ c               &= 50 \\\\
c \times c + c \times c &= 50 \\\\
c^{2} + c^{2}           &= 50 \\\\

c^{2}                   &= \dfrac {50} {2} \\\\
c^{2}                   &= \dfrac {2 \times 25} {2} \\\\
c^{2}                   &= \dfrac {\cancel{2} \times 25} {\cancel{2}} \\\\
c^{2}                   &= 25 \\\\
c                       &= \sqrt {25} \\\\
c                       &= 5
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

The temperature of water in a tank is decreasing at $3 \degree \text{C per minute}$. If the bath starts with a temperature of $48 \degree \text{C}$ , after how long will the temperature reach $15 \degree \text{C?}$ 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">The temperature of water in a tank is decreasing at $3 \degree \text{C per minute}$. If the bath starts with a temperature of $48 \degree \text{C}$ , after how long will the temperature reach $15 \degree \text{C?}$ 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>

</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the time taken $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
48 - 3 \times a                                      &= 15 \\\\
48 - 3a                                               &= 15 \\\\
3a                                                    &= 48 - 15 \\\\
3a                                                    &= 33 \\\\
a                                                     &= \dfrac {33} {3} \\\\
a                                                     &= \dfrac {3 \times 11} {3} \\\\
a                                                     &= \dfrac {\cancel {3} \times 11} {\cancel {3}} \\\\
a                                                     &= 11 \ \text {minutes}
\end{aligned}
$

Time taken $= 11 \ \text {minutes}$
</div>
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

The number of stinging nettle plants in Mr Beefshaw's rose patch doubles each year. In $2016$ there are $8$ stinging nettle plants. In which year will the number of stinging nettle plants first be more than $1000?$ 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">The number of stinging nettle plants in Mr Beefshaw's rose patch doubles each year. In $2016$ there are $8$ stinging nettle plants. In which year will the number of stinging nettle plants first be more than $1000?$ 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

We can easily infer the value by using trial and error. 

| Year  | Number of plants                      |
|:-----:|:-------------------------------------:|
| $2016$  | $8$                                    |
| $2017$  | $8 \times 2 = 16$                      |
| $2018$  | $16 \times 2 = 32$                     |
| $2019$  | $32 \times 2 = 64$                     |
| $2020$  | $64 \times 2 = 128$                    |
| $2021$  | $128 \times 2 = 256$                   |
| $2022$  | $256 \times 2 = 512$                   |
| $2023$  | $512 \times 2 = 1024$                  |

Year $= 2023$
</div>
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number of years after $2016 = n$

As per the question,

$\begin{aligned}
8 \times 2^n &> 1000 \\\\
2^n &> \dfrac{1000}{8} \\\\
2^n &> \dfrac{8 \times 125}{8} \\\\
2^n &> \dfrac{\cancel{8} \times 125}{\cancel{8}} \\\\
2^n &> 125
\end{aligned}$

We can easily infer the value by using trial and error. 

Lets find out the value of $n$ that satisfies the above equation.

|  $n$  | $2^n$ |  $> 125$    |
|:------------:|:------------------:|:------------------:|
|     $2$      |        $4$         |    No    |
|     $3$      |        $8$         |    No    |
|     $4$      |        $16$        |    No    |
|     $5$      |        $32$        |    No    |
|     $6$      |        $64$        |    No    |
|     $7$      |        $128$       |    Yes   |

$\begin{aligned}
\text{Year} &= 2016 + 7 \\\\
            &= 2023
\end{aligned}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$2023$

</div>
</div>

<div class="formulacodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="formulacodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Formulas Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">%empty%
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workingcodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="workingcodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Working Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Let the number of years after $2016 = n$
<emptyline>
As per the question,
<emptyline>
$\begin{aligned}
8 \times 2^n &> 1000 \\\\
2^n &> \dfrac{1000}{8} \\\\
2^n &> \dfrac{8 \times 125}{8} \\\\
2^n &> \dfrac{\cancel{8} \times 125}{\cancel{8}} \\\\
2^n &> 125
\end{aligned}$
<emptyline>
We can easily infer the value by using trial and error. 
<emptyline>
Lets find out the value of $n$ that satisfies the above equation.
<emptyline>
|  $n$  | $2^n$ |  $> 125$    |
|:------------:|:------------------:|:------------------:|
|     $2$      |        $4$         |    No    |
|     $3$      |        $8$         |    No    |
|     $4$      |        $16$        |    No    |
|     $5$      |        $32$        |    No    |
|     $6$      |        $64$        |    No    |
|     $7$      |        $128$       |    Yes   |
<emptyline>
$\begin{aligned}
\text{Year} &= 2016 + 7 \\\\
            &= 2023
\end{aligned}$
</code></pre>
</div>
</div>

</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">$2023$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A theatre has seats arranged in rows of $22$. If an audience of $483$ fills the rows one by one, leaving no empty seats, how many rows will be full? 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A theatre has seats arranged in rows of $22$. If an audience of $483$ fills the rows one by one, leaving no empty seats, how many rows will be full? 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Number of rows fully occupied}     &= \dfrac {\text{Total audience}} {\text{Seats per row}} \\\\
                                          &= \dfrac {483} {22} \\\\
                                          &= 21 \ \text {remainder} \ 21 \\\\
                                          &\approx 21
\end{aligned}
$

Number of full rows $= 21$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$21$

</div>
</div>
